docs.title: Pandora ITSM — Product documentation
docs.text: Pandora ITSM is Pandora's service management tool: it brings tickets, inventory, projects, time and customer relationships together in a single web console. This documentation covers what to install, how to configure each module and what the product does today, with technical details checked against the source code.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: If you are installing Pandora ITSM for the first time, start with Part 01 — Installation: requirements, cloud or on-premise installation and the first connection. If the product is already running and you need a specific module, go straight to the matching part in the map below.

docs.title: Glossary of terms
docs.text: This glossary gathers the terms Pandora ITSM uses with a meaning of their own. It does not replace the functional chapters: it fixes the vocabulary so two people do not call different things "user". Each block links to the chapter where the concept is developed.

docs.title: Product and release cycle
docs.text: Term Definition Pandora ITSM / PITSM Pandora FMS's IT service management product. "Pandora ITSM" is the brand; "PITSM" is the abbreviation used after the first mention. Pandora FMS / PFMS Pandora FMS monitoring product. It integrates with Pandora ITSM for authentication, inventory and tickets, but it is not the same product. Pandora RC Pandora remote control product. It integrates with Pandora ITSM to manage devices. Warp Update Pandora ITSM updater. It supports online and offline updates, options and journal review. OUM / MR / LTS / FR OUM is the Offline Update Manager, the offline update package. MR is the Minor Release or database migration level. LTS is a long-term support release. FR is a Feature Release with new features. Patch Point fix on a release. It does not change the support cycle by itself. Perpetual licence / subscription A perpetual licence is bought once; a subscription is renewed per period. Both may limit the number of administrators. Manager Count / Manager Limit Licence terms: number of administrators used and the allowed limit.

docs.title: Users, permissions and organisation
docs.text: Term Definition Grouped / standalone user A grouped user belongs to a group and shares visibility with colleagues; a standalone user only sees their own content. Contact / company A contact is a CRM person without application access; a company is the entity that groups contacts, contracts, invoices and tickets. Group / profile / role The group controls visibility; the profile grants permissions; the role refines functions within a project or company. They are not interchangeable. User mode / ACL / permission bit User mode is a user's mode over a group; the ACL is the resulting access control list; the permission bit is each concrete profile permission. Superadmin / administrator / Manager A superadmin is the superuser and always authenticates locally; an administrator has the Administration profile; a Manager is responsible for a CRM company. HR / UM / VCM People permissions: HR for human resources, UM for user management and VCM for vacation management. CR / CW / CM CRM permissions: read, write and manage. CIR / CIW / CIM Invoice permissions: read, write and manage. RR / RM Report permissions: read and manage. KW / KM Knowledge base permissions: write and manage. WR / WW / WM Wiki permissions: read, write and administer. PR / IR / VR / AR / WOR Visibility bits for projects, tickets, inventory, calendar and work orders.

docs.title: Tickets and support
docs.text: Term Definition Ticket / incident A ticket is the object opened, assigned and closed in the console. "Incident" is a general concept, not a synonym for the object. Creator / editor / owner The creator describes the problem; the editor enters the ticket; the owner is responsible for solving it. Contributor / associated user A contributor provides information without being creator or owner; an associated user has taken part and receives notifications. Support team / Round Robin / Load Balanced / fallback The team groups agents; Round Robin rotates; Load Balanced assigns the least loaded; fallback receives the ticket if nobody is available. Status / status mapping The status is the ticket phase; the mapping defines which transitions are allowed. Resolution / epilogue The resolution is the outcome; the epilogue explains what was done on closure. Priority / criticality Priority orders work; criticality measures impact. They do not always match. SLA / FRT / TTR / escalation SLA is the service level agreement; FRT is first response time; TTR is resolution time; escalation changes owner, group or priority. Workflow / rule / condition / action / macro A workflow automates tickets; the rule contains conditions and actions; the macro replaces ticket data. Do not confuse it with the CRM workflow. Work unit / internal note / private note A work unit records time and detail; an internal note is hidden from the creator; a private note is visible only to administrators and its author. Work order PDF document generated from a template with ticket data, as a delivery note or proof of work. Ticket type / custom field / combo / linked The type groups fields; a custom field adds data; combo is an option list; linked chains a parent and child field. Q/A / survey / satisfaction Quality assurance rates closure; the survey expands a negative rating; satisfaction is the customer's opinion.

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Term Definition SMTP / POP / IMAP Sending (SMTP) and receiving (POP or IMAP) protocols. OAuth 2.0 / Client ID / Tenant ID / Client Secret / Redirect URI Delegated authentication for Microsoft 365: application identifiers, secret and return URL. Mail queue / Email destination / Email origin The queue holds pending messages; Email destination identifies the mailbox that creates tickets; Email origin filters valid senders. Message delimiter / masking / blacklist The delimiter cuts the thread; masking hides addresses; the blacklist discards senders or domains. Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace Corporate email services supported by the integration. PostMark / SPF / DKIM PostMark is a sending server; SPF and DKIM are DNS records that improve deliverability. Bounce Email that could not be delivered. It is measured in campaigns.

docs.title: Knowledge, Wiki and downloads
docs.text: Term Definition Knowledge base (KB) / article / category / product type The knowledge base stores solutions in articles classified by category and product. Wiki / page ACL / side_menu / TOC The Wiki is internal documentation; the page ACL controls read and write; side_menu is the side menu; TOC is the table of contents. Download / release / folder / download category / internal or private file Downloads distribute files and releases in folders and categories; an internal or private file has limited visibility.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: Term Definition Inventory / CMDB Inventory is the asset base; CMDB is the configuration management database. Object / object type The object is a concrete instance; the type defines its fields and behaviour. Custom field / external field A custom field is defined by the organisation; an external field is filled from another source. Relationship / tree view / stock / status / tag A relationship links objects; the tree view shows hierarchy; stock controls quantity; status and tag classify. Remote inventory / agent / module / node Remote inventory is synchronised from Pandora FMS; the agent sends data; the module is a check; the node is the monitoring server.

docs.title: Projects and time
docs.text: Term Definition Project / task / subtask The project groups work; the task is a planable unit; the subtask hangs from another task. Milestone / Gantt / board A milestone is a zero-duration date; the Gantt shows time planning; the board organises tasks by status. Start-to-start / finish-to-start / finish-to-finish dependency Rules that prevent one task from starting or finishing before another. Time booking / cost / profitability / deviation Time booking records hours; cost values them; profitability compares revenue and cost; deviation measures the gap from plan. Timetracker / clock-in / pause / shift Timetracker records activity; clock-in marks start and end; a pause interrupts the shift; the shift is planned time. Vacation / leave / remote work Absences and work mode that affect availability and reports. Hour bucket Contracted or budgeted hours for a project, with consumption and remaining balance.

docs.title: CRM and marketing
docs.text: Term Definition Contract / contract type / contract template The contract covers a service; the type defines fields; the template generates the PDF with macros. Received / submitted invoice Received is an incoming invoice; Submitted is an issued invoice. The issued one is locked and generates a PDF. Quote Formal commercial proposal linked to a deal or contact. Deal / opportunity / pipeline / stage A deal is a sales opportunity; the pipeline is the funnel; the stage is the phase inside the funnel. Deal registration Opportunity registration by partners or resellers, separate from the main pipeline. Campaign / template / static list / dynamic list The campaign sends a message; the template is the design; the static list is fixed; the dynamic list is recalculated at send time. Form Web form that captures contacts and creates or updates them in the CRM. Tag Cross-cutting mark for classification and filtering; it does not grant permissions. Consent The contact's authorisation to receive communications or accept a policy. Parent company / company role / IT service The parent company organises hierarchy; the role classifies the company; the IT service classifies tickets.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text: Term Definition Change / change request A change is a controlled modification; the request is its entry point. Authorisation / planning / change task Authorisation approves; planning organises; the change task executes the work. Review / closure Review checks the result; closure ends the cycle. Risk / impact Risk is the probability of a negative effect; impact is its scope. Approver / change team People and teams that authorise and execute the change.

docs.title: API and integrations
docs.text: Term Definition API v1 / API v2 Pandora ITSM programming interfaces. v2 is the current API; v1 is the legacy one. Token / endpoint The token authenticates the request; the endpoint is the concrete resource URL. JSON / OpenAPI / pagination JSON is the data format; OpenAPI describes the API; pagination splits long results. Webhook / rate limit A webhook notifies events; a rate limit caps requests per period. ChatBot / AI / prompt / channel The ChatBot handles conversations; AI generates answers; the prompt is the instruction; the channel is the contact medium. GitLab Repository platform integrated to read project tickets.

docs.title: Administration and security
docs.text: Term Definition Setup / token Setup is configuration; a token is each parameter stored in it. Visibility Hidden or Full level of a section for a group. 2FA / TOTP Second authentication factor based on temporary codes. Session / timeout Period from login until it expires through inactivity. HTTPS / SSL/TLS / certificate / CA HTTPS encrypts the connection; SSL/TLS is the protocol; the certificate identifies the server; the CA validates it. FQDN / IP / port Full name, network address and connection port. Backup / restore Backup and restoration of database and attachments. Cron Periodic system task that runs automatic processes. Audit / log / event Audit records user actions; the log stores errors; the event records system activity. Diagnostics / DB Manager Diagnostics shows system status; DB Manager runs SQL with elevated permissions.

docs.title: Technical terms and formats
docs.text: Term Definition CSV / PDF / JSON / XML / SQL Exchange, report, data and query formats used by the application. HTML / URL / URI Markup language, resource locator and resource identifier. PHP-FPM / Apache / MySQL / Percona Common web server and database components. EL9 / EL10 / Ubuntu Supported operating systems for installation. MB / GB File and storage size units.

docs.title: Ambiguous terms
docs.text: Problematic form Recommended form company / "compañía" company ( English) / empresa (Spanish) workunit work unit (the workunit identifier is cited as code) KB knowledge base ticket / incident ticket for the object; "incident" as a general concept user / contact user with access; contact without access profile / role profile grants permissions; role refines functions group / team group controls visibility; team distributes tickets console interface SLA / ANS SLA, expanded on first mention PandoraFMS Pandora FMS Office 365 Microsoft 365 LTS / FR / OUM / MR Expand each acronym on first mention

docs.title: Upgrading PHP versions
docs.text:
PHP is one of those dependencies you only remember once support has run out. The Pandora ITSM web console relies on the PHP of the operating system, and an unmaintained version keeps starting up just as happily while it piles up unpatched vulnerabilities. This annex gathers the upgrade per distribution: Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and RHEL in versions 8, 9 and 10 on one side; Ubuntu Server 22.04 on the other.

The commands are given as they are, with no rewrites and no shortcuts. The prose around them only explains what each block does and what is worth checking; the command does not negotiate.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before touching repositories it is worth knowing where you start from and having a way back.

Requirement Detail Terminal with the root user or equivalent The commands manage DNF modules, APT repositories and the php-fpm service; administrator privileges are required. Starting PHP version Run php -v and check that version 7.x is installed. Backup A backup of the server is recommended before resetting modules or purging packages.

docs.title: Rocky Linux / AlmaLinux / RHEL 8, 9 and 10
docs.text:
Commands valid for EL8, EL9 and EL10

The commands in this section (Remi modules and installation) are identical in Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and RHEL 8, 9 and 10. EL8 is legacy support; EL9 and EL10 are the current versions. On EL10, dnf module warns that modularity is obsolete, but the command still works: it is an informative warning, not a failure.

The three distributions share the procedure and their module commands are identical in versions 8, 9 and 10: the only thing that changes is the PHP module that is enabled. The first step resets the module so that DNF does not drag the previous version along; only then is the Remi repository enabled with the chosen version.

docs.title: Upgrade to PHP 8.0
docs.text:
Configure the repositories:

dnf module reset php -y
dnf -y module enable php:remi-8.0

Install PHP:

dnf install -y \
php php-mcrypt php-cli php-gd \
php-curl php-session php-mysqlnd \
php-ldap php-zip php-zlib php-fileinfo \
php-gettext php-snmp php-mbstring \
php-pecl-zip php-xmlrpc \
php-xml php-yaml

Restart php-fpm: systemctl restart php-fpm.

Check the installed version: php -v.

docs.title: Upgrade to PHP 8.2
docs.text:
The 8.2 procedure condenses configuration, installation and restart into a single block. It is reproduced as it is:

dnf module reset php -y
dnf -y module enable php:remi-8.2

dnf install -y \
php php-mcrypt php-cli php-gd \
php-curl php-session php-mysqlnd \
php-ldap php-zip php-zlib php-fileinfo \
php-gettext php-snmp php-mbstring \
php-pecl-zip php-xmlrpc \
php-xml php-yaml

systemctl restart php-fpm

Check the installed version: php -v.

docs.title: Upgrade to PHP 8.4
docs.text:
Same as the previous one, with the php:remi-8.4 module:

dnf module reset php -y
dnf -y module enable php:remi-8.4

dnf install -y \
php php-mcrypt php-cli php-gd \
php-curl php-session php-mysqlnd \
php-ldap php-zip php-zlib php-fileinfo \
php-gettext php-snmp php-mbstring \
php-pecl-zip php-xmlrpc \
php-xml php-yaml

systemctl restart php-fpm

Check the installed version: php -v.

docs.title: Ubuntu Server 22.04
docs.text: On Ubuntu the path is different. First the old PHP is purged without ceremony, then the Ondrej PPA repository is added and, finally, /etc/php.ini is adjusted so that the console works with the limits it needs: input time, execution time, upload size, memory, POST size and disabled functions. The script from the wiki is meant to be run in one go and it is reproduced in full here. The only thing that changes from one version to another is the PHPVER variable.

docs.title: Upgrade to PHP 8.2
docs.text:
dpkg -l | grep php | tee packages.txt
# Remove old PHP
# When upgrading from older PHP version:
a2disconf php8.1-fpm 2> /dev/null
a2disconf php8.0-fpm 2> /dev/null
dpkg -l | grep php | awk '{print $2}' | xargs apt -y purge


## Define new php
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
export NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1
export PHPVER="8.2"
add-apt-repository ppa:ondrej/php
apt update
apt install -y php$PHPVER php$PHPVER-fpm php$PHPVER-common \
                    php$PHPVER-cli libapache2-mod-fcgid apache2 \
                    php$PHPVER-bz2 php$PHPVER-mbstring php$PHPVER-intl  php$PHPVER-mcrypt \
                    php$PHPVER-gd  php$PHPVER-curl  php$PHPVER-mysql php$PHPVER-ldap \
                    php$PHPVER-fileinfo php$PHPVER-gettext php$PHPVER-snmp php$PHPVER-mbstring \
                    php$PHPVER-zip php$PHPVER-xmlrpc php$PHPVER-xml php$PHPVER-yaml

a2enmod proxy_fcgi setenvif
a2enconf php$PHPVER-fpm

## Prepare php config
rm -f /etc/php.ini
ln -s /etc/php/$PHPVER/fpm/php.ini /etc/
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/^max_input_time.*/max_input_time = -1/g" /etc/php.ini
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/^max_execution_time.*/max_execution_time = 0/g" /etc/php.ini
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/^upload_max_filesize.*/upload_max_filesize = 800M/g" /etc/php.ini
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/^memory_limit.*/memory_limit = 800M/g" /etc/php.ini
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/.*post_max_size =.*/post_max_size = 800M/" /etc/php.ini
sed --follow-symlinks -i -e "s/^disable_functions/;disable_functions/" /etc/php.ini

systemctl enable php$PHPVER-fpm --now
systemctl restart php$PHPVER-fpm
systemctl restart apache2

Check the installed version: php -v.

docs.title: Upgrading MySQL 5.7 to MySQL 8
docs.text: MySQL 8 changes enough that a blind upgrade is not a good idea: the query cache is gone, authentication plugins change and the engine needs a backup that can be imported into the new version. This annex covers the procedure to move from MySQL 5.7 to Percona Server 8 on Pandora ITSM.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
To migrate from MySQL 5.7 to MySQL 8 you must be on Pandora ITSM version 104 or later.

Requirement Detail root user The commands manage services, repositories and the database; administrator privileges are required. MySQL version Run mysql --version and check that you are on 5.7. Backup Save the database and the my.cnf file before touching anything. Maintenance window The console is stopped during the migration.

Check the starting point:

mysql --version

The response should be similar to:

mysql  Ver 14.14 Distrib 5.7.33, for Linux (x86_64) using EditLine wrapper

Back up the database. The general procedure is in 12.2 Maintenance and backups. The database is referred to in this annex as <pandora_itsm_db_name>.

docs.title: Rocky Linux 8 / AlmaLinux 8 / RHEL 8
docs.text:
Stop Apache:

systemctl stop httpd.service

Or, if the installation uses SysV:

/etc/init.d/httpd stop

Make a special database backup compatible with MySQL 8:

mysqldump -u root -p <pandora_itsm_db_name> \
  --skip-add-drop-table \
  --complete-insert \
  --no-create-info > backup_pandora_itsm.sql

Also make a backup as it was done in MySQL 5.7, as a safety net for going back:

mysqldump -u root -p <pandora_itsm_db_name> > backup_pandora_itsm_5.7.sql

Save the configuration file:

cp /etc/my.cnf /tmp/my.cnf.BACK

Remove the Percona 5 repositories:

rpm -qa | grep Percona-Server | xargs rpm -e --nodeps

Install the Percona 8 repository:

dnf install https://repo.percona.com/yum/percona-release-latest.noarch.rpm -y

Enable the repository:

percona-release setup ps80

Install Percona Server 8:

dnf install percona-server-server

Restore the configuration file:

mv /tmp/my.cnf.BACK /etc/my.cnf

Disable the query cache directives, which no longer exist in MySQL 8:

sed -i -e "s/^query_cache_type.*/#query_cache_type/g" /etc/my.cnf
sed -i -e "s/^query_cache_size.*/#query_cache_size/g" /etc/my.cnf
sed -i -e "s/^query_cache_min_res_unit.*/#query_cache_min_res_unit/g" /etc/my.cnf
sed -i -e "s/^query_cache_limit.*/#query_cache_limit/g" /etc/my.cnf

If you do not have a high-availability environment, disable binary logging by adding this line to the [mysqld] section of my.cnf:

skip-log-bin

Start MySQL:

systemctl start mysql

Or, if the service uses another name:

service mysqld start

Check the installed version:

mysql --version

The response should be similar to:

mysql  Ver 8.0.28-19 for Linux on x86_64 (Percona Server (GPL), Release 19, Revision 31e88966cd3)

docs.title: Migrate the database
docs.text:
Enter the MySQL command line:

mysql -u root -p <pandora_itsm_db_name>

Drop the old database, create a new one and import the schema and data from the special backup:

DROP DATABASE <pandora_itsm_db_name>;
CREATE DATABASE <pandora_itsm_db_name>;
USE <pandora_itsm_db_name>;
SOURCE /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/integria_db.sql;
SOURCE backup_pandora_itsm.sql;

The integria_db.sql schema is the one from the Pandora ITSM installation. Do not use the schema from another version or another product.

docs.title: Permissions and authentication
docs.text:
The database permissions must be created again. If you are not connected as root, enter with:

mysql -uroot -p

Inside MySQL, disable the password validation component if it was active (this is optional):

UNINSTALL COMPONENT 'file://component_validate_password';

Create the connection user if it does not exist:

CREATE USER "<DBUSER>"@'%' IDENTIFIED BY "<DBPASS>";

If you want to restrict the connection to a specific IP, replace % with the source address.

Set MySQL native authentication:

ALTER USER "<DBUSER>"@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY "<DBPASS>";

Grant permissions on the Pandora ITSM database:

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON <pandora_itsm_db_name>.* TO "<DBUSER>"@'%';

Save the changes and exit:

FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
exit

If you need to switch to SHA authentication, check the MySQL 8 documentation for your version before changing the user.

docs.title: Start the console
docs.text:
Start Apache again:

systemctl start httpd.service

Or, if the installation uses SysV:

/etc/init.d/httpd start

Check that the console responds, that you can log in and that the previous data is still there. If something fails, keep both backups and my.cnf until the installation has been validated.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 integration
docs.text: Microsoft 365 requires OAuth 2.0 for Pandora ITSM to send and receive email with a corporate account. The integration is configured in two places: an Azure AD application and the SMTP/POP/IMAP settings in Pandora ITSM. Functional email configuration is in 3.4 Email and support; this annex explains the Azure AD registration step by step.

docs.title: Create an Azure AD application
docs.text: The application represents Pandora ITSM inside Microsoft 365. It is registered once and reused for sending and receiving.

docs.title: Enter the portal
docs.text:
1. Go to https://portal.azure.com/.
  2. Search for Azure Active Directory.
  3. In the side menu, select App registrations.

docs.title: Register a new application
docs.text:
1. Click New registration.
  2. Fill in Name with a descriptive name, for example PANDORA.
  3. Choose Supported account types for your organisation. For a single organisation, use Accounts in this organizational directory only.
  4. In Redirect URI (optional) choose Web and enter a sample URL such as http://localhost/pandora.
  5. Click Register.

docs.title: Get the identifiers
docs.text:
On the application home page you will see:

  • Application (client) ID: this is Pandora ITSM's Client ID.
  • Directory (tenant) ID: this is the Tenant ID.

Copy both values. They are public, but they must match the registered application exactly.

docs.title: Create a secret
docs.text:
1. In the side menu, open Certificates & secrets.
  2. Under Client secrets, click + New client secret.
  3. Add a description and a duration, for example 6 or 12 months.
  4. Click Add.
  5. Copy the Value immediately: it is shown only once. That is the Client Secret.

An expired secret does not send a polite email: it simply stops authenticating. Note the expiry date and renew it as part of maintenance.

docs.title: Configure redirect URIs
docs.text:
1. Open Authentication.
  2. Under Platform configurations, select Add a platform → Web.
  3. In Redirect URIs, add every valid URL where the application will receive the token. For example:
http://localhost/pandora
http://localhost/pandoraitsm/godmode/godmode/setup/setup_mail

In production use the real Pandora ITSM URL, always over HTTPS. A localhost URL is only for testing.

docs.title: Connecting with a non-administrator user
docs.text: If the application will not use a global administrator, review permissions and user consent.

docs.title: API permissions
docs.text:
1. In Azure Portal → Azure Active Directory → App registrations, select the application.
  2. Open API permissions.
  3. Check that the Microsoft Graph permissions needed for email are present: email, Mail.Read, Mail.ReadBasic, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, MailboxSettings.Read, offline_access and User.Read.

docs.title: User consent
docs.text:
1. Go to Azure AD → Enterprise applications → User settings.
  2. Open Consent and permissions → User consent settings.
  3. Allow user consent for applications from verified publishers or for the low-impact permissions the application needs.

If the organisation requires administrator consent, an administrator must approve it. Without that consent, the user cannot authorise the application.

docs.title: Secret and Pandora ITSM configuration
docs.text:
1. Generate a new Client Secret if you changed permissions.
  2. Copy the Value.
  3. Paste it into the POP/IMAP Secret field in Pandora ITSM.
  4. Repeat the process if you change permissions again: the previous secret may stop working.

In Pandora ITSM, sending and receiving with Microsoft OAuth 2.0 requires Client ID, Tenant ID and Secret, plus clicking Connect to Microsoft and accepting the permissions.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The application appears under App registrations.
  • Client ID and Tenant ID are copied without spaces.
  • The Client Secret is valid and stored.
  • Redirect URIs include the real Pandora ITSM URL.
  • Microsoft Graph permissions are granted.
  • User or administrator consent is resolved.
  • Pandora ITSM can connect and send a test email.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use one application per environment: development, testing and production.
  • Document the secret expiry date.
  • Do not share the secret by email or store it in the repository.
  • Use HTTPS in production.
  • Review permissions after every Azure AD change.
  • If something stops working, check the secret and consent first.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Installing Pandora ITSM has an easy part and a part that gets complicated the moment someone decides to improvise. The official script does almost everything: it installs the dependencies, creates the database, loads the schema and leaves the console ready. What it does not do is guess whether the server is short on memory, whether the database lives somewhere else or whether someone will keep the default password until audit day.

The point of this chapter is simple: installations rarely fail because of the software; they fail because of haste. With two gigabytes of RAM, ten gigabytes of disk and a clear decision about the database, the rest is following the order. Without that, the script stops, and it is right to do so.

The default installation is the online installation: an official script that runs as root, installs the dependencies, creates the database, loads the schema and the initial data and leaves the console at http://<IP-or-FQDN>/pandoraitsm. For environments without Internet access there is the offline installation.

docs.title: What is installed
docs.text:
The installer leaves these components on the server:

  • Web console in /var/www/html/pandoraitsm.
  • Apache web server and PHP-FPM.
  • MySQL or Percona database, local or external.
  • Pandora ITSM schema and initial data.
  • Cron every five minutes for internal tasks.
  • Chat server and its Node.js dependencies.
  • Configuration in include/config.inc.php.

It is not a managed service or a desktop installation. The whole product is used from the browser, and the server remains the responsibility of whoever administers it: patching, backing up and monitoring are not included in the package.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Before running the installer, check these points:

  • You have root or sudo access on the server.
  • The server has a resolvable hostname or FQDN.
  • The time zone is correct; the installer sets it with TZ.
  • There is Internet access and connectivity to packages.pandorafms.com.
  • Ports 80 and 443 are free. If the database is external, port 3306 must also be reachable from the server.
  • SELinux and the firewall allow web traffic.
  • You have decided whether the database will be local or external.
  • If you have decided to install the database externally, you have its passwords ready and they meet the MySQL password policy.
  • If you are reinstalling, you have a backup or a snapshot of the machine.

The installer stops if it finds Pandora ITSM packages, the /var/www/html/pandoraitsm directory or a database with the same name. It does not clean up a previous installation on its own. If your plan was "we will see", the installer has another one: stop.

docs.title: Online installation
docs.text:
The online installation runs with a single command, whatever the distribution. Run it as root:

curl -SsL https://pfms.me/deploy-pandora-itsm | bash

The script detects the system and downloads the matching installer. The rest of this chapter explains what it does, which variables it accepts and how to check the result.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Requirement Minimum Recommended CPU 2.4 GHz, dual core Four cores or more depending on concurrent users RAM 2 GB 4 GB Disk 10 GB free 20 GB or more, depending on history and attachments Network 100 Mbps 1 Gbps

The installer checks memory and disk space before changing anything. On EL9 and EL10 it requires 9 GB free in /var and 1 GB in /usr. If the server does not meet the minimum, the script stops. This is not a suggestion: it is a condition.

docs.title: Operating systems
docs.text: System Supported versions RHEL, Rocky Linux or AlmaLinux EL 9 and EL 10 Ubuntu Server 22.04 and 24.04

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Component Version PHP 8.2 or 8.4 MySQL or Percona 8.0 or 8.4 depending on the distribution Web server Apache with PHP-FPM Browser Current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari; minimum resolution 1280 × 720

EL10 only accepts MySQL/Percona 8.4. EL9 and Ubuntu accept 8.0 and 8.4. The installer sets the PHP and MySQL versions with the PHPVER and MYVER variables. There is no prize for using the version that is no longer supported.

docs.title: PHP extensions
docs.text: The console needs the mysqli, gd, session, mbstring, ldap, gettext, imap, phar and zip extensions. The installer adds them with the PHP packages; if you install manually, check that they are enabled before opening the console. An extension error disguises itself as a blank screen, and a blank screen never brings good news.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Pandora ITSM needs a MySQL or Percona database. It can run on the same server or on a dedicated one. A shared database is valid, but performance depends on the server capacity and the volume of history: tickets, their attachments and the audit log grow with use.

If the database is external, prepare the host, port, user and permissions first. The installer can create the database and user, or use existing ones with SKIP_DATABASE_INSTALL=1.

docs.title: Installation modes
docs.text:
Mode When to use it Needs Internet Online New installation on a server with Internet access Yes Offline Isolated or restricted servers No Manual web installer Debugging or a piece-by-piece installation with install.php Depends

The manual web installer is not the recommended path for production. It helps you understand each step and works for tightly controlled environments; the online script is the supported procedure. Do not confuse "I can do it by hand" with "I should do it by hand".

docs.title: Run the script
docs.text:
The generic script takes its configuration from environment variables and detects the system to download the matching installer. These are the values you can adjust:

Variable Default Purpose TZ Europe/Madrid System time zone MYVER 84 MySQL/Percona version: 80 or 84 PHPVER 8.4 PHP version: 8.2 or 8.4 DBHOST 127.0.0.1 Database host DBNAME pandoraitsm Database name DBUSER pandoraitsm Database user DBPASS P4ndor4.itsm Database user password DBPORT 3306 MySQL port DBROOTPASS P4ndor4.itsm MySQL root password DBROOTUSER root MySQL administrator user SKIP_PRECHECK 0 Skips the previous-installation check SKIP_KERNEL_OPTIMIZATIONS 0 Skips kernel tuning SKIP_DATABASE_INSTALL 0 Uses an existing database POOL_SIZE Calculated from RAM PHP-FPM pool size

Always replace the example passwords. If you use MySQL 8 with the password policy enabled, P4ndor4.itsm may not meet the requirements; choose a longer password with upper and lower case letters, numbers and symbols. Today's convenience is tomorrow's incident.

docs.title: EL10 example
docs.text:
env TZ='Europe/Madrid' \
    MYVER='84' \
    PHPVER='8.4' \
    DBHOST='127.0.0.1' \
    DBNAME='pandoraitsm' \
    DBUSER='pandoraitsm' \
    DBPASS='ChangeThisPassword' \
    DBPORT='3306' \
    DBROOTPASS='ChangeThisRootPassword' \
    DBROOTUSER='root' \
    SKIP_PRECHECK=0 \
    SKIP_KERNEL_OPTIMIZATIONS=0 \
    SKIP_DATABASE_INSTALL=0 \
    bash itsm_deploy_enterprise_entrypoint.sh

The generic script detects EL10 and downloads the EL10 installer. To use PHP 8.2, change PHPVER='8.2'. On EL10 the installer only accepts MYVER=84; on EL9 you can use MYVER='80' if your database is MySQL 8.0.

docs.title: What the script does
docs.text:
1. Checks the operating system, memory, disk and permissions.
  2. Adds the Pandora and Remi repositories for PHP.
  3. Installs Apache, PHP-FPM, MySQL or Percona, Node.js and the extensions.
  4. Creates the database and user, or reuses existing ones.
  5. Loads integria_db.sql and integria_dbdata.sql.
  6. Writes include/config.inc.php with the connection details.
  7. Sets up the integria_cron.php cron job every five minutes.
  8. Installs and starts the chat server.
  9. Applies kernel and PHP-FPM tuning.
  10. Prints the access URL and the initial credentials.

The script writes the details to /tmp/pandoraitsm-deploy-enterprise-el9-YYYY-MM-DD.log (or the name for your system). If something fails, that log is the first thing to read. Guessing the error costs more than opening the file.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
When it finishes, the script prints an address similar to:

http://192.0.2.10/pandoraitsm

and the initial credentials. Open that address from a browser with access to the server.

docs.title: Offline installation
docs.text:
The offline installation uses a package with the dependencies and a local script. The flow is:

  1. Download the dependency package and the script for your distribution.
  2. Copy them to the isolated server.
  3. Unpack the package.
  4. Run itsm_deploy_enterprise_local_el10.sh as root, with the same variables as in the online installation.

Offline installation is not supported on Ubuntu with the current scripts.

docs.title: Console URL
docs.text:
The console is available at:

http://<IP-or-FQDN>/pandoraitsm

If you have configured TLS, use https://. The /pandoraitsm path is what the installer writes in config.inc.php; do not change it without updating the Apache configuration.

docs.title: Licence and login
docs.text:
If you use the manual web installer, the first screen asks you to accept the licence. With the online script, the first access is the login screen directly.

The initial credentials are:

User Password admin pandoraitsm

Change the password on first access

The admin account is an installation user. Change its password before connecting the console to the production network and create your own users afterwards. Do not share the admin account between several people.

A default password is a welcome, not a security policy. The sooner it disappears, the better.

docs.title: Change the password
docs.text: Log in as admin, open the user menu and change the password. Then create a user with your name, assign the profile and group it needs and keep admin for administration tasks.

docs.title: Initial data and "Reset all data"
docs.text:
The installation loads integria_dbdata.sql, which includes sample data: companies, contacts, tickets and other records that let you see the console with content from day one.

If you want to start with a clean system:

  1. Open Setup → Setup → Old data maintenance.
  2. Click Reset all data.
  3. Confirm twice in the dialogs.

Reset all data deletes data and attachments

The option deletes the database data and the attachment files. It keeps the current admin user and some configuration settings. There is no undo: make a backup first if you need to keep anything.

Sample data is great for a demo and a liability in production. The button exists so you do not have to delete it by hand, table by table.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Check that the web server, PHP-FPM and the database are running:

# RHEL, Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux
systemctl status httpd php-fpm mysqld

# Ubuntu
systemctl status apache2 php8.4-fpm mysql

Adjust the PHP-FPM name to the installed version (php8.2-fpm or php8.4-fpm). A service you do not check is a service that fails on Monday.

docs.title: Cron
docs.text:
The installer leaves three scheduled tasks, all every five minutes:

*/5 * * * * root php /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/integria_cron.php
*/5 * * * * php /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/crm_cron.php
*/5 * * * * php /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/campaign_cron.php

Each one has its job:

Task What it does integria_cron.php Core: daily checks (calendar, projects, tasks, changes, autowu, automatic ticket closing, cleanup and notifications), mail queue, CRM and inventory task reminders, Enterprise cron, SLAs and time workflow rules. crm_cron.php CRM: Gmail sent and inbox, contact and deal workflows, overdue schedules, due-task emails, activity notifications, Google Meet transcripts and Zadarma calls. campaign_cron.php Campaigns: runs pending campaigns and checks email bounces.

Inventory also has its own script, inventory_cron.php: it syncs inventory from Pandora FMS nodes, expires overdue schedules and cleans orphan objects. The current installer does not add it to /etc/crontab; add its entry if you need it:

*/5 * * * * php /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/inventory_cron.php

Check that the tasks are active and the files exist:

grep pandoraitsm /etc/crontab
ls -l /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/*_cron.php

If a task is missing, check /etc/crontab and the application log. A cron that does not run does not warn you; it simply stops doing its job.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Log Content /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/pandora_itsm.log Application errors /var/log/php-fpm/www-error.log PHP and PHP-FPM errors /tmp/pandoraitsm-deploy-enterprise-<system>-YYYY-MM-DD.log Installation

If PHP does not start or the console returns a 500 error, start with /var/log/php-fpm/www-error.log: the real error is there, not in the generic message the browser shows.

docs.title: Minimum security
docs.text:
• Change the admin password.
  • Create your own users and remove or disable the sample ones.
  • Decide whether to keep the sample data.
  • Review the firewall: only 80/443 should be open to the Internet.
  • Configure TLS if the console is reachable outside the internal network.
  • Make sure the database is not exposed to the Internet.
  • Schedule backups before loading real data.

docs.title: Reinstallation and cleanup
docs.text:
The installer does not overwrite an existing installation. If it finds packages, /var/www/html/pandoraitsm or the database, it stops. To reinstall from scratch, remove first:

  • The Pandora ITSM packages.
  • The /var/www/html/pandoraitsm directory.
  • The database and the database user.
  • The cron entry.
  • The Apache and PHP-FPM configuration if you customised it.

There is no automatic uninstaller. If you only want to start over with the data, use Reset all data instead of reinstalling. If you need to keep anything, back up the database and the attachments before deleting.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause Check The script says the system is not supported Distribution or version other than EL9, EL10 or Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 Check /etc/os-release and use the right script Memory or disk check fails Less than 2 GB RAM or less than 10 GB free Increase the server or free space Cannot reach packages.pandorafms.com No Internet access or DNS Test ping and check the proxy PHP or MySQL not supported Version outside 8.2/8.4 or 8.0/8.4 Adjust PHPVER and MYVER MySQL rejects the password MySQL 8 password policy Use a stronger password The installer finds a previous installation Existing packages, directory or database Clean up or use another machine The console does not respond after the script Apache, PHP-FPM or SELinux Check services and logs The console opens but does not load data Database or configuration Check config.inc.php and the application log

If the problem is not in this table, see Part 14 (FAQ) and attach the installation log when opening an issue. An "it does not work" without a log is a conversation that starts badly.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
With the console running, the recommended order is:

  1. Review the licence and the version policy (1.3 and 1.4).
  2. Configure users, groups and profiles (Part 02).
  3. Set up email (Part 03).
  4. Schedule backups and review the advanced configuration (Part 12).
  5. Only when you have a stable version, plan the update (1.2).

Installing is the beginning, not the end. The installation gets the engine running; what comes next depends on how you configure it and how much you respect the data it will store.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Updating Pandora ITSM is not about pressing a button and keeping your fingers crossed. It is a controlled-risk operation: there is data, there are users and there is a version that works. The difference between a boring update and an afternoon of incidents is almost always in what you do before, not in what you press afterwards.

The point of this chapter is simple: if you do not have a backup, you do not have an update; you have a bet. With a backup, a maintenance window and a clear target version, Warp update does almost everything. Without them, the prettiest button in the world will not save you.

docs.title: Before updating
docs.text:
Before touching anything, prepare the ground:

  • Full backup: database, /var/www/html/pandoraitsm and attachments. A database dump alone is not enough; files count too.
  • Maintenance window: tell users and leave time to check the console afterwards.
  • Current and target version: write down the version, MR and package you have. You will find them in About ITSM.
  • Access to the update repository: online updates require registration; offline updates use a temporary code.
  • Disk space and memory: leave room to download, unpack and apply.
  • Compatibility: check that PHP and MySQL/Percona for the target version are still within the supported window.
  • Update path: Warp update online, Warp update offline or the legacy tarball.
  • Plan B: if something fails, do you restore the backup? How long does it take? Who do you tell?

Do not skip versions without confirming the path first. A bad jump is not fixed with another jump; it is fixed by restoring the backup.

If the problem is that your licence does not allow updates, this is not the chapter that solves it: see the licensing chapter (1.4).

docs.title: How it is updated
docs.text:
There are two interfaces and three real paths:

Path When to use it Needs Internet Warp update online Installation with Internet access and registration Yes Warp update offline Isolated or restricted servers No Legacy tarball Only if support confirms it is still valid No

Warp update is the recommended path. The tarball is kept as a legacy option for very specific cases, but it is not the path I would choose for 5.0.110 without asking first.

docs.title: Online web update
docs.text:
Open Warp update → Update online.

The first time, you must register the installation with an email address. The server returns a permanent UID (pandora_uid) that is stored for future updates. Without registration, the online update does not start: the code says so clearly with "Update online requires registration".

Once registered, the screen offers two buttons:

  • Update to next version: applies the next available version.
  • Update to latest version: jumps to the latest published version.

If you are already on the latest version, neither button will be enabled. That is not a failure: there is nothing to install.

Before applying, review the summary of changes and fixes. The download may take a while; do not close the tab or walk away while the process writes files. When it finishes, check the system status and confirm the version in About ITSM.

docs.title: Offline web update
docs.text:
Open Warp update → Update offline.

This path is for environments without Internet access or for installations that, for security reasons, must not talk directly to the repository. Applying offline patches can leave the console unusable; a full backup is not a suggestion, it is the requirement.

If you have not registered the installation, request a temporary code to access the repository. The flow is:

  1. Enter the email and click Register.
  2. Copy the code and open the link that appears.
  3. Download the .itsm files for the version you are going to apply.
  4. Go back to Update offline and upload each file with BROWSE IT.
  5. Wait for the analysis and apply the update with the green button.

Only .itsm files are uploaded through this screen; server packages do not go through it.

The files must fit within the PHP limits:

post_max_size
upload_max_filesize
memory_limit

The updater warns if memory_limit is below 800M. On EL it is usually in /etc/php.ini; on Ubuntu, in /etc/php/8.2/fpm/php.ini or /etc/php/8.4/fpm/php.ini, depending on the installed version. If the file does not upload, the problem is almost never the file: it is the limit.

docs.title: Legacy tarball update
docs.text:
The tarball is downloaded to /tmp, unpacked and the update script is run as root:

cd /tmp
tar xzf <name_packet>.tar.gz
cd integria_enterprise
./integria_update -p /var/www/html/pandoraitsm

The script copies the code, fixes permissions, removes install.php and protects config.php. It is an old tool: it declares version 3.0 and only covers a database migration from 3.0 to 3.1. For 5.0.110, do not use it on your own; confirm with support first that it is still the correct procedure.

If you use it anyway, make the backup first and then check the version, MR, services and logs. A badly applied tarball shows up late.

When it finishes, apply the pending database MRs:

cd /var/www/html/pandoraitsm
php godmode/um_client/updateMR.php

The script prints the current MR and applies the pending ones. If you skip it, the code may be updated while the database stays behind.

docs.title: Warp Update settings
docs.text:
On the Warp update screen you can adjust the connection to the repository:

Option Purpose Warp Update URL Address of the update server Use secured Warp Update Forces TLS on the connection Proxy server / port / user / password Outbound access through a proxy Allow no-consecutive patches Allows non-consecutive updates Limit to LTS updates Restricts updates to LTS versions

Contact support before changing the URL, TLS or proxy. These options are not decoration: if you get them wrong, the console stops seeing the repository and it looks as if the product is broken.

About Allow no-consecutive patches: in the reference screenshot it is disabled, which is the recommended option. Do not enable it without confirming the behaviour of your version. Limit to LTS updates is enabled by default; if you need a current release, you will have to disable it deliberately.

docs.title: Warp journal
docs.text:
Warp update → Warp journal shows the history of applied updates. Each row stores:

  • Version.
  • Type.
  • Origin: online or offline.
  • User.
  • Date.

The data lives in the tupdate_journal table and can be filtered by keyword. In an audit, this journal is worth more than any email saying "I think I updated it in March".

docs.title: After updating
docs.text:
When it finishes, log in again. Then check, in this order:

  1. About ITSM: version, MR and package. They must have changed.
  2. Services: Apache, PHP-FPM and MySQL/Percona running.
  3. Cron: integria_cron.php, crm_cron.php and campaign_cron.php still in /etc/crontab.
  4. Logs: pandora_itsm.log and /var/log/php-fpm/www-error.log.
  5. Functional test: log in, open a ticket, check inventory, enter CRM and run a test campaign.
  6. Warp journal: the update appears with the correct version.

If something fails, do not improvise on a half-updated installation. Restore the backup, go back to the previous version and open an issue with the logs. A system restored in time is better than one that is "almost updated" for a week.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Check No update is offered No registration, no connection or LTS active Check pandora_uid, the network and Limit to LTS updates Memory error when applying memory_limit too low Raise it to 800M or more The offline file does not upload Extension, size or PHP limits Check .itsm, post_max_size and upload_max_filesize The console is unusable after a patch Incomplete or incompatible patch Restore the backup and check the log MR does not change Pending MR process Check updateMR.php and the journal Services do not start Dependencies or configuration Check Apache, PHP-FPM, MySQL and their logs Cron has disappeared Update that rewrites /etc/crontab Add the three entries again Version does not change in About ITSM Update not applied or cache Check the journal and log in again

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
With the update closed:

  • Review the versions and support lifecycle (1.3).
  • Review licensing if the update was limited by licence (1.4).
  • Schedule backups and monitoring (Part 12).
  • Note the applied version and date in the journal.
  • Plan the next update before the calendar catches you.

docs.title: Versions and support lifecycle
docs.text:
Pandora ITSM is not updated for the sake of updating. Each release has a goal: an LTS prioritises keeping the system standing; an FR prioritises getting what is new sooner. Choosing the wrong channel does not break the product on day one; it breaks the team's peace of mind when the first incident arrives.

The point of this chapter is simple: do not look for the highest version; look for the one you can defend. The latest LTS is the usual reference for production, but a well-supported earlier version is still better than a badly tested latest one.

docs.title: How versions are read
docs.text:
Each installation is described by four pieces of data:

Data Example What it is Version 5.0.110 Product version OUM 110 Offline Update Manager release MR 110 Database migration level Package 5.0.110-261001 Package and build date

The version is the product version. The OUM is the release package published through the Offline Update Manager. The MR is the database migration level. The package adds the build date; it is not a different version.

Since 105, the OUM matches the version: 5.0.105 is OUM 105, 5.0.106 is OUM 106 and so on up to 110. The MR does not always follow: 5.0.105 was OUM 105 and MR 98; 5.0.106 was already MR 106. That is why the three are read together in About ITSM; none replaces the others.

An example: an installation with version 5.0.110, OUM 110 and MR 110 is on release 110 and has the database up to date. If the MR lags behind, the code may be new while the schema is old.

docs.title: LTS version
docs.text:
LTS stands for Long Term Support. It is the reference version for production: it is published less often than FRs, it is validated more and it is maintained with security patches and critical fixes.

What you need to keep clear:

  • An LTS does not receive the new features from FRs. It receives fixes, not novelties.
  • LTS patches come out as needed, not on a fixed cadence.
  • The end-of-support date shown in About ITSM is the licence date, not the version date. It tells you whether you are covered, not when to update.
  • The real limit is usually the operating system: if the vendor stops supporting EL9 or Ubuntu 22.04, the longest-lived LTS loses its foundation.

Unless there is a specific reason otherwise, production runs on LTS. And to stay on track without thinking about it, Warp Update has the Limit to LTS updates option, which skips intermediate versions.

docs.title: Feature Release (FR) version
docs.text:
FR stands for Feature Release. It is the version that brings new features, improvements and fixes on a more frequent cadence than the LTS.

It makes sense in three cases:

  • You need a specific feature before it reaches the LTS.
  • You have a pilot environment where you can test without putting the service at risk.
  • The team accepts that each release must be reviewed, tested and applied.

Keeping a critical environment on FR without room for testing is not a good idea. An FR may also receive patches, but changes normally arrive with the next FR. Novelty is tested where you can go back.

docs.title: LTS patches
docs.text:
An LTS does not stand still: it receives patches. An LTS patch fixes a vulnerability, a relevant incident or a critical failure without changing the family or bringing new features.

Patches are identified by the version and the release number published by the vendor; the source is the official updates page and the notes for each OUM. Do not invent your own naming or mix an FR patch with an LTS.

They are applied with Warp Update, just like a full release. The procedure is in 1.2; here only the criterion matters: if it is an LTS patch, it goes to the LTS; if it is a new feature, it goes to the FR.

docs.title: Support lifecycle
docs.text:
The reference for production is the latest LTS or, with a justified reason, the previous one that is still supported. There is no promise of indefinite support for an old LTS: when a new one is published, the previous one enters the planning zone.

Two dates are easy to confuse and should be kept apart:

  • Licence end of support: shown in About ITSM. It is tied to payment and the contract.
  • Version end of life: marked by the release cycle and, in practice, by the operating system.

Before stretching an LTS, look at the operating system calendar and the support contract. Licensing details are in 1.4; here it is enough to know that the licence date is not the version date.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
The reference version, 5.0.110, lives in this window:

Component Versions RHEL, Rocky Linux or AlmaLinux EL 9 and EL 10 Ubuntu Server 22.04 and 24.04 PHP 8.2 and 8.4 MySQL or Percona 8.0 and 8.4, with EL10 limited to 8.4

The full matrix and installation are in 1.1. If your current version does not meet this window, the problem is not solved by updating the product: it is solved by updating the platform.

docs.title: How to choose
docs.text:
For production, the rule is boring and it works:

  1. Check the latest published LTS and its notes.
  2. Confirm that the operating system, PHP and MySQL are still supported.
  3. If you need a feature that only exists in FR, test it in a pilot.
  4. Update to the next release or the latest one, not to an invented combination.
  5. Verify version, MR, services, cron and logs.

If the FR solves a real problem, bring the update forward, but do it with a backup and a maintenance window. Stability is not negotiated on what keeps the service running.

docs.title: Where to look
docs.text:
• About ITSM: version, MR and package of the installation.
  • Warp journal: history of applied updates.
  • Official updates page: published releases and notes.
  • OUM notes: what each release brings and fixes.
  • Warp Update: LTS, non-consecutive patches and proxy options.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text: The procedure is in 1.2. Here the criterion remains: choose the channel, check compatibility, make a backup and update. Then check the MR and the journal.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Review the licence and support contract (1.4).
  • Check the compatibility matrix before the next update.
  • Schedule backups and monitoring (Part 12).
  • Note the version, OUM and MR in the journal.
