docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
A licence is not a sticker: it decides who can log in, how many administrators fit and what happens when the support date gets close. In Pandora ITSM the limit you notice most is the manager user limit; regular users are rarely the problem, but administrators pile up with surprising ease.

The point of this chapter is simple: manage the licence before it hurts. Checking the count when nobody can log in is too late; checking it before creating the next administrator is cheap.

docs.title: Licence types
docs.text:
Pandora ITSM works with four modes:

Mode What it is Expiry Manager limit Perpetual Indefinite use of the product Support and update access expire Per contract Subscription Use while the subscription is active On expiry, the console enters limited mode Per contract Trial Product evaluation 30 days 25 Free Free use with limited features No use expiry 1

A perpetual licence does not stop working when it expires: what expires is support and access to updates. Subscription and trial do condition use: on expiry, the console enters limited mode and Enterprise features stop working. Free is the entry door: one administrator and the features available in that mode.

Do not confuse the licence date with the version date. The first is tied to the contract; the second to the release cycle. Version details are in 1.3.

docs.title: How it is limited and counted
docs.text:
The limit applied today is the manager user limit. A user counts as a manager if they have any profile with management permissions (im, am, um, dm, fm, pm, km, vm, wm, cm, frm or chm) or if they are a superadministrator. Regular users are the rest.

The count:

  • Counts distinct users, not profiles. A user with three manager profiles takes one seat.
  • Does not count disabled users. A deactivated user frees their seat.
  • Does count users blocked by licence until they are disabled or deleted. Blocking does not give the seat back by magic.
  • Is calculated on the spot: creating, enabling or disabling a user changes the number.

The regular-user limit exists in the code, but the current commercial licence leaves it practically without effect. In practice, the number to watch is Manager Count against Manager Limit.

docs.title: What happens when the limit is exceeded
docs.text:
When the number of managers exceeds the limit, Pandora ITSM does not delete users or change profiles on its own. It does something simpler: it blocks login for the extra ones.

The criterion is creation order: the oldest managers keep access and the newest are blocked. They appear in the user list with login disabled, and when they try to log in they receive a notice that the limit has been exceeded.

There are three ways to recover access:

  1. Disable or delete managers who no longer need the account.
  2. Change the profile of a manager to a regular profile, if their duties allow it.
  3. Expand the licence with more manager seats.

When the licence is expanded, blocked users are enabled again. The notice and the block disappear, but the count remains: the seat is not free, it is paid for.

docs.title: How the licence looks
docs.text:
The Warp update → License screen shows the four pieces of data that matter:

  • License Mode: perpetual, subscription, trial or free.
  • Expires: licence or support expiry date.
  • Manager Limit: contracted manager seats.
  • Manager Count: managers currently occupying a seat.

The same information appears in About ITSM. If the count is close to the limit, do not wait for the next hire: review inactive users or expand the licence.

docs.title: How to update the licence
docs.text:
The normal flow is:

  1. Open Warp update → License.
  2. Paste the licence key into License key.
  3. Click Update license.
  4. Confirm that the mode, expiry and limit have changed.

If you need a new licence:

  1. Click Request new license.
  2. Copy the Request key shown in the window.
  3. Provide the Auth key you receive from support.
  4. Validate online with Online validation or, if the server has no outbound access, use offline validation: enter the Auth key, click Generate and copy the resulting licence.
  5. Go back to the console, paste the licence and click Update license.

docs.title: Expired licences
docs.text:
When a subscription or trial licence expires, the console stops working normally: the expired or invalid licence warning appears and Enterprise features become limited. It is not a configuration error; it is the licence.

With a perpetual licence the product keeps working. What expires is support and access to updates; the console warns you, but it does not block normal use.

In either case, the path is the same: Request new license, support Auth key and online or offline validation. If the licence has expired, do not try to fix it by updating the product: renew the licence first.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Check Manager Count before creating a new administrator.
  • Disable the accounts of people who leave; a disabled account frees a seat.
  • Do not share the admin account or make someone an administrator just because they need to read reports.
  • Keep the licence key in a safe place; do not paste it into tickets.
  • Watch the Expires date and renew before the console enters limited mode.
  • If you are going to expand the licence, do it before a mass user creation.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Review the version and support lifecycle (1.3).
  • Review the update procedure (1.2).
  • Check users and profiles (Part 02).
  • Schedule backups and monitoring (Part 12).

docs.title: First steps and interface
docs.text:
The Pandora ITSM console has changed more than the continuity of its name suggests. The first login no longer leaves the user in front of a greeting and a search box: it opens a tactical dashboard, a notifications bell with its own centre and a side menu that can be collapsed. Anyone coming from the old documentation will recognise the product; the screen, not so much.

This chapter covers the first day: signing in, understanding what you are looking at and not mistaking a feature that has changed for one that is broken. Each module is covered in its own chapter; this is the map.

docs.title: Login screen
docs.text:
The console opens at http://<IP-or-FQDN>/pandoraitsm, or at the path used by your installation. On a first start, read chapter 1.1 first: the initial connection screen may include steps that do not appear in a normal login.

The form asks for two things and hides neither: the user (Nick) and the password. The eye icon shows what you have typed; the LOG IN button sends it. The Docs and Support links are at the top left; the version appears at the bottom unless the administrator hides it.

The initial load creates an installation account:

User Password admin pandoraitsm

The historical integria password is no longer the one shipped with the initial load. If you use it, login fails and the error message will not tell you that you are mixing up manuals.

The admin account is not for everyday use

Sign in as admin, change the password and create the named accounts the team needs. Sharing admin between several people is an expensive way to lose track of who did what. Account creation and permissions are explained in chapter 2.1.

On a new Enterprise installation, the licence agreement may appear before the form. You must accept it to continue; without acceptance there is no console.

If two-factor authentication is enabled, a second field appears after the user name and password: Double factor authentication code. The code is requested once per login. An administrator can reset it from the login screen with Reset auth code; a standard user must ask their administrator for a reset. Security configuration is covered in chapter 2.2.

Forgot your password? The Forgot your password? link opens the recovery flow: enter the user name, the console sends an email with a validation code and, once the code is entered, shows a new password. If the user has no email address configured or email delivery is unavailable, the form itself refers you to the administrator. The new password is shown only once; copy it before closing the window.

docs.title: Pandora ITSM home page
docs.text:
After login, the console decides what to show on the home page. There are two scenarios, and it is worth knowing which one applies to you:

  • Tactical welcome view: shown by default when the user has no dashboard assigned. It displays Welcome back <name> !👋, the sentence This is the latest data in your default tactical view. and the link Change to a custom dashboard →.
  • Dashboard: if the administrator has defined a global dashboard, or the user has one assigned and has report read permission (RR), the home page loads that dashboard instead of the tactical view.

The Change to a custom dashboard link opens the profile, at the Dashboard (welcome screen) field. There you can choose Global dashboard or one of your own. The profile is detailed in chapter 2.1 and dashboards in 9.1.

A dashboard is made of widgets: welcome message, search box, ticket lists, evolution and SLA charts, statistics, links and custom SQL. It is not a copy of the tactical view; it is a screen you assemble and arrange.

The tactical view is not decoration: it summarises activity for the configured period, 21 days by default (Welcome view field, on the Setup page). These are its blocks:

Block What it shows Open / Closed tickets Tickets opened and closed in the period, with the total and percentage. Tickets activity Ticket activity trend. Tickets statistics Total tickets, work units, average lifetime, average work time, positive ratings, SLA compliance and total time. Top 5 companies by creator The five companies that opened the most tickets. Top 5 assigned users The five users with the most assigned tickets. Top 5 ticket submitters The five users who submitted the most tickets. Top 5 active tickets The tickets with the most work unit hours. Tickets by status Ticket distribution by status. Tickets by priority Ticket distribution by priority. Latest tickets Latest tickets with title, date, owner, status and priority. Logged in users Users connected at that moment. Tickets general report Time series of tickets for the period.

When there is no data, the block says No data to show; this is not a loading error. A user without IR permission does not see real statistics: the blocks appear empty. That is ACL behaviour, not a broken screen.

The home page is not the only place to search. Global search is in the header and covers every area you can access: tickets, projects, people, knowledge base, contracts, invoices and wiki, plus deals, quotes, deal registrations, notes, tasks and CRM meetings. The old search box on the home page still exists, but as a dashboard widget (Search box), with check boxes for Knowledge Base, Wiki, Ticket management, Project management, People, Contacts, Contracts, Companies and Invoices. If you do not see it, it is not missing: it is not on the dashboard.

The result limit per area is configured under Setup → Visual (global_search_limit, 10 by default). CRM blocks show five and a Search more button when there are more results.

Three optional notices may appear before you are fully in: a window with your last login if the administrator enables it, News board updates once per session and a browser reminder if you are not using Firefox, Chrome or Safari. None of them blocks your work; close them and continue.

docs.title: Console elements
docs.text:
The console has three fixed areas and one floating guest: header, side menu, workspace and chatbot.

The header groups the global actions:

Element What it is for Logo and title Return to the home page. The title and subtitle are customised under Setup → Visual. Search Global search across every permitted area. Autorefresh Automatic refresh; it only appears in All tickets. Bell Opens the notification centre and shows pending notices. Chat notifications Internal chat status, if the module is active and you have permission. Help Documentation, support portal, feedback form (Enterprise) or community forum. Setup Console configuration; administrators or profiles with management permission only. User Opens your profile and shows the identifier in brackets. Sign out Ends the session.

The title, subtitle and light and dark theme logos are changed under Setup → Visual. A group can have its own banner, which replaces the general logo in the side menu.

The bell is not decoration. It opens a list with search by subject, type or source, a type filter and actions to mark as read or unread and delete, one by one or in bulk. In the profile, on the Notifications tab, you choose the channel for each type of notice: Email, Notification or Both. The configurable sources are Support, Projects, Changes, CRM, People and Inventory; personal notices are shown in the centre but are not configured per channel. System notices (PHP, MySQL, cron, licence, database, files, Chromium, API and Warp) are managed by the administrator and only appear if the console supervisor has enabled that group. The bell updates without reloading the page and each notice links to the ticket, task, change or note that originated it.

Mentions are written as @user in a note, work unit or comment. The mentioned user receives a Mention in a ticket, Mention in a work unit or Company note mention notification, depending on the source, and can open the item from the bell.

The chat icon in the header shows internal chat notifications and its status. Do not confuse that chat with the chatbot in the bottom-right corner: the first is a conversation between users; the second is the AI assistant, configured in chapter 11.6.

The side menu has two modes: classic, with labels visible, and collapsed, with icons only and fly-out submenus. The button at the end of the menu switches between them and the preference is stored in the browser. The menu logo returns to the home page.

The menu includes two quick navigation aids: Go to User, under People, and Go to Inventory #, under Inventory. They only appear with permission and accept the identifier or the name, depending on the field.

The theme is chosen in the profile: Light, Dark or System. System follows the operating system theme. If the user chooses nothing, the global theme from Setup → Visual applies.

The calendar in the side menu shows the current month and, with permission, opens the full calendar or adds an entry. Chapter 7.1 explains time management.

The User info entry groups personal shortcuts. The options change with the user type and permissions:

Option What it opens Name and avatar Your profile. Workunit report The monthly work unit report. My tickets Tickets owned by the user. Workunit Quick creation of a work unit. Full graph report The people graph report. My project tasks Assigned project tasks. My tasks Assigned CRM tasks. My inventory tasks Assigned inventory tasks. Notifications The notification centre, with the number of unread notices.

About ITSM closes the menu. It shows version information and, for administrators, the License Info and System Info tabs, plus the System report button. Licensing is explained in chapter 1.4.

docs.title: Menu map
docs.text:
The menu order is not arbitrary, but it is not universal either: it depends on permissions, configured menu visibility and active modules. This is the default list for an administrator:

Menu What it contains Chapter Projects Projects, tasks, Gantt, milestones, boards, project and task types and workflow rules. 6.1 Changes Changes, teams, templates, statuses, types, priorities, risks, impacts and task statuses. 5.1 Support Tickets, CSV import, ticket types, ticket templates, work order templates, tags, teams, SLA, workflow rules, knowledge base, downloads and chat. 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 Wiki Pages, search, file upload, administration, history, permissions and syntax. 3.6 Inventory Dashboard, lists, search, stock, CSV import, tasks, types, statuses, tags and catalogue. 4.1 Reports Dashboards, report manager, templates, scheduler, library, support, people, project and custom SQL reports and time tracking. 10.1 CRM Contacts, companies, contracts, invoices, deals, quotes, products, workflows and tasks. 8.1, 8.7, 8.8 Marketing Forms, templates, campaigns, mail servers and contact lists. 9.1 People Users, groups, profiles, roles, teams, work units and time tracking. 2.1, 7.1 Setup General, visual, authentication, mail, file manager, news board, database, links, events, audit, logs, translations, backups, menu visibility and console extensions. 12.1, 12.3 Warp update Online and offline updates, options, journal and licence. 1.2, 1.4 Calendar Monthly calendar, full calendar and entry creation. 7.1 User info Profile and personal shortcuts for work, tickets, projects, CRM, inventory and notifications. 2.1, 3.1, 7.1 Links Links configured under Setup → Links, including the documentation link. 12.1 About ITSM Version, licence and system information. 1.4, 12.1

A Standalone user sees a subset: essentially their own tickets. The Setup and Warp update menus and the licence and system tabs in About ITSM are administrative. Chat and Marketing only appear if the module or integration is active and the user has permission.

docs.title: Reports and dashboards
docs.text:
A report is not meant to fill a meeting: it is meant to answer a question. Pandora ITSM gathers people, support, project and SQL reports under Reports, and adds dashboards so you can see what matters without opening five different screens. The problem is never a lack of data; the problem is mistaking a pretty chart for a well-informed decision.

This chapter explains how dashboards are built, how reports are scheduled and what each report measures. Project reports stay here, next to the rest, because they share the menu, templates and scheduler.

docs.title: Where reports live
docs.text:
The Reports menu groups:

  • Dashboards → Manage Dashboard: visual boards.
  • Report manager: templates, scheduling and report library.
  • People management: time, vacations, people and team performance.
  • Support: support, tickets, resolutions, operators and customers.
  • Project management: project reports.
  • Custom SQL report: custom queries.

Permissions are based on the Report Reader (RR) and Report Manager (RM) profile bits, plus group visibility. A user may be able to view a report but not create one, or create a SQL query but not see another group's data.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Dashboards are command boards. Each user can have their own and choose which one appears at login.

In Reports → Dashboards → Manage Dashboard you list dashboards, search by keyword and create them with Create. Each one has Update to change its name and group, and Delete to remove it. The Default dashboard includes every available widget and serves as a demonstration.

docs.title: Creating and editing
docs.text:
When creating a dashboard you set a unique Name, with no leading or trailing spaces, and a Group. The name can be changed later with Update.

To edit the content, open the dashboard and enable the edit switch. Add cell adds a cell and New widget lets you choose the widget type. Each widget is configured with the gear icon and deleted with the bin icon. You can drag it by its title and resize it from the edges.

docs.title: Customized links
docs.text:
Adds a working link that opens in the same window or a new tab. The URL must start with http:// or https://; otherwise it is treated as an internal link. An image is also required: both fields are mandatory.

Example of an internal link to the change list:

  • URL: changes/operation/changes/changes_list
  • Open new tab: enabled
  • Image: ticket.svg

The remaining fields —text, title, font and colours— are optional.

docs.title: Message board
docs.text: A rich text editor for embedding tables, links, images, lists or complete documents. It starts with a welcome message that disappears when you add your own content.

docs.title: Predefined links
docs.text:
Adds internal links with a label and icon:

  • Knowledge base.
  • Downloads.
  • Create ticket.
  • Wiki.
  • Time tracker.
  • My tickets.

docs.title: Search box
docs.text: Adds a keyword search box. Select at least one area: knowledge base, Wiki, tickets, projects, people, contacts, contracts, companies, invoices or leads.

docs.title: Support Activity Graph
docs.text: Shows an activity chart across one or more calendars from a saved ticket filter. Each user can only choose their own filters.

docs.title: Support Evolution Graph
docs.text: Shows opened and closed tickets from a saved filter, with a configurable refresh rate. It also uses only the user's own filters.

docs.title: Support SLA
docs.text: With a saved filter, shows a pie chart with the percentage of met and breached SLA.

docs.title: Support statistics
docs.text: Groups tickets from a saved filter by priority, status, type or general statistics. You must choose an option in Statistic.

docs.title: Ticket list
docs.text: Shows a paginated ticket list —five per page by default— with the fields and order you choose. It uses a saved filter and a refresh period to keep information current.

docs.title: Report manager
docs.text: In Reports → Report manager you create templates and schedules. Scheduled reports are stored in the library and can be sent by email. The system cron must be active; without cron there is no magic, only a queue waiting.

docs.title: Report templates
docs.text:
In Reports → Report manager → Templates you define the cover, header and footer of PDF reports. The cover supports images, links, formatting and margins. Available macros:

  • _fullname_: user generating or requesting the report.
  • _date_: generation date.
  • _time_: generation time.
  • _reportname_: report name.

The macros also work in the header, where the logo can be changed. Cover, header and footer can be disabled separately.

docs.title: Report scheduler
docs.text:
In Reports → Report manager → Report schedule you schedule a report to run once, weekly or monthly. Choose a template, store it in the library and optionally send a notification or the report itself by email.

Assigning a company to the scheduled report lets that company's users see and edit it. Depending on the report type, its filters appear; Custom SQL only shows the SQL reports already created. You can create as many schedules as needed.

docs.title: Report library
docs.text: In Reports → Report manager → Report library you browse generated reports and search by report type or name.

docs.title: People reports
docs.text: Pandora ITSM can track working time, breaks, remote or on-site work and vacations. Reports in this area can be scheduled weekly or monthly.

docs.title: Time tracking
docs.text:
Reports → People management → Time tracking shows daily, weekly or monthly activity recorded by a user with the Time tracker. There are preset periods —this week, this month, the last three months— and you can request a custom one.

At least one daily record must exist for the report to show data; the remaining days appear empty. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

The three vacation reports share a menu but not permissions: the detailed report requires HR and, in practice, UM to reach it from the menu; the calendar and export depend on access to Reports.

docs.title: Detailed vacation report
docs.text:
Reports → People management → Detailed vacation report presents the report in two modes: Show vacation report and the work unit report. The filters are user, group and creation date (Created from and Created to); they are applied when you click Search.

The result shows users, total vacation days, days taken and days remaining. It can be viewed full screen or exported to PDF. If the work unit report is selected, it adds unjustified days, justified non-working days due to illness, vacation and extra vacation. Exports to full screen and PDF; not CSV.

docs.title: General vacation calendar
docs.text: Reports → People management → General vacation calendar shows approved vacations in monthly, weekly or daily view. You can move forward and backward by month and return to today with Today. The user search limits the calendar to one person and non-working days are highlighted. It is screen-only.

docs.title: People report
docs.text:
Reports → People management → People report selects the current user and the last three months of all projects by default, with a ticket summary. It shows project activity and percentage, ticket charts by group and creator group, a ticket table —if Show only summary is disabled— and a summary of tickets and time worked.

Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: People monthly WU
docs.text:
Reports → People management → People monthly WU shows all users for the current month with total hours and average rating. You can change month and filter by user.

Each user's report button opens a dialog to edit their work units, one by one or in bulk. Only task work units (Work Unit Tasks) support bulk editing. Depending on privileges, each unit can be edited, deleted or blocked.

docs.title: Detailed user report
docs.text:
Reports → People management → Detailed user report requires start and end dates. It offers three options:

  • Project: groups by user and project.
  • Role and task: groups by user and task.
  • Role and task (details): adds descriptions and ticket, hour and cost totals.

Select user, period, roles, tasks and projects. It does not export to CSV, full screen or PDF.

docs.title: Vacation report
docs.text: Reports → People management → Vacation report selects all active users by default. Choose group, users and dates (Date from and Date to); dates are mandatory. View shows the table on screen and Export downloads the result. Name filtering is applied when you click View, not while typing. Exports to CSV, but not full screen or PDF.

docs.title: Team performance
docs.text:
Reports → People management → Team performance shows the weekly performance of a company's staff. Filter by group, date and Pandora ITSM area: projects, support, changes or time tracking.

With default values it returns no data, and that is normal:

  • The main filter is the company.
  • The filter interface opens with Ctrl + f.
  • The week start day comes from general configuration; Monday by default.

Exports to full screen, PDF and Microsoft Excel; not CSV.

docs.title: Support reports
docs.text: Support reports are based on recorded ticketing. They help evaluate cost, quality, time, effort, staff profiles and customer profiles.

docs.title: Support report
docs.text:
Reports → Support → Support report generates a PDF with dozens of charts, summaries, lists and parameters. To choose filters quickly, start from a saved custom ticket search.

The report has two parts:

  • Show statistics: statistical information with charts.
  • Show list: tabular ticket information.

Select one or both. Issue fields chooses the table fields without affecting the charts. It includes eight general pie charts with Top-N groupings —most active tickets, most active customers, operators, opened, closed— plus trend lists and charts.

Exports to full screen and PDF; not CSV.

docs.title: Detailed ticket report
docs.text:
Reports → Support → Detailed ticket report shows every detail of a ticket: dates, participants, description, custom fields, SLA and, optionally, work units, files, tracking and statistics.

Type at least two letters in Select issues, choose the ticket and click Report. Additional options:

  • Stats: general statistics, work unit statistics, activity by user and by status, group, owner and company.
  • Tracking: ticket changes, filterable by user.
  • Files: attached files.
  • Work Units: work units, with the option to edit time.

User privileges limit what can be seen and edited. Exports to full screen and PDF; not CSV.

docs.title: Resolution report
docs.text: Reports → Support → Resolution report lists closed tickets and shows the impact on time, dead pauses, people involved and resolution, including customer feedback. Filter by creation and closing date, creator and company. Exports to full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Ticket type report
docs.text: Reports → Support → Ticket type report groups tickets by company and type over a time interval. Filter by creator, company and group. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Operator report
docs.text:
Reports → Support → Operator report measures support quality per operator: time spent, average resolution time, customer feedback and total tickets. Filter by company, user, status and time range.

Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Customer tickets reports
docs.text:
Reports → Support → Customer tickets shows created, resolved and in-progress tickets grouped by user, year and month. Company is mandatory; Users lets you select one or more users from that company.

Options:

  • Show section state: status table by month and user.
  • Show section type tickets: type table by month and user.
  • Show section total: global total.
  • Created from Pandora FMS: separates tickets created from Pandora FMS and from Pandora ITSM.

Exports to full screen and PDF; not CSV.

docs.title: Project reports
docs.text: Project reports are in Reports → Project management. They help plan time and cost and see project evolution through the hours booked by the people involved.

docs.title: General project report
docs.text:
Reports → Project management → General project report → Select project shows a selected project. Opening it without a project shows an error message; this is normal and does not indicate a failure.

Options:

  • Show project: basic information, people, work and cost summary, task distribution, workload, activity and task summary.
  • Show task activity: for selected tasks, hours, costs, estimates and distribution and activity charts.
  • Show task work unit: date, duration, people and description of each work unit for the selected tasks.
  • Show in table: all tasks according to date, milestone or people filters.

You can filter by milestones, tasks, dates, people and related company. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: All projects report
docs.text:
Reports → Project management → All projects report filters by text in name or description, owner, people involved, date, group, archived projects and project custom fields.

The list shows identifier, group, name, owner, people involved and task progress. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Project expense report
docs.text: Reports → Project management → Project expense report shows last month's projects. Filter by start or end date and completion percentage. Show task breakdown details each task. Selecting a project lets you filter by milestones. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Project bundle of hours report
docs.text: Reports → Project management → Project bundle of hours report selects a project and a month. It shows a summary by task and tickets, with consumed and remaining hours. You can filter by company and related contracts. Exports to full screen and PDF; not CSV.

docs.title: Custom SQL report
docs.text:
Reports → Custom SQL report lets you create your own queries that return a table exportable to a spreadsheet or PDF.

Only a super administrator or a user with RM permission can create, modify and delete SQL reports. Viewing them requires RR and membership in the report's group.

A simple query:

SELECT id, name, country FROM tcompany ORDER BY country;

Fields can be renamed with aliases:

SELECT
  id AS `Identification number`,
  name AS Name,
  country AS `Country origin`
FROM tcompany ORDER BY country;

For security, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, CREATE, UPDATE, INSERT INTO, EXEC and MERGE are forbidden. Exports to CSV, full screen and PDF.

docs.title: Custom SQL tips
docs.text:
• In templates, _reportname_ can be replaced with the real SQL report name and custom images can be inserted.
  • New SQL reports are assigned to the None group; assign a specific group.
  • To discover tables and fields, create reports with SHOW TABLES; and DESCRIBE <table_name>;. This avoids creating database users: the ACL is managed in Pandora ITSM.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Define the question before choosing the report.
  • Save reusable ticket searches for dashboards.
  • Review RR/RM permissions and group visibility before publishing.
  • Keep cron active if you use the scheduler.
  • Use templates to make PDFs readable, not to hide data.
  • Do not turn a dashboard into an ownerless chart album.
  • Document which report answers each question and who reviews it.

docs.title: API v2
docs.text: Pandora ITSM's API v2 is a REST API documented with OpenAPI. You do not need to memorise endpoints or parameters: the installation ships its own Swagger, and this chapter only covers the three entry doors. Generate a token, open Swagger and fire the first call. The full resource reference lives in Swagger itself and changes with the version; copying it here would be an elegant way to become outdated.

docs.title: Before you start: network permission
docs.text:
The API does not answer everyone. It only accepts requests from the addresses listed in Setup → Setup → General setup → List of IP with access to API. By default, the list is limited to localhost and 127.0.0.1.

Add the IP or range you will call from, separated by commas. A wildcard such as 192.168.7.* is accepted, but opening the API to any address with * is a bad idea: it turns the token into the only barrier.

If Swagger or a call fails with a connection error, check this list before touching the token. It is the first place where an integration breaks.

docs.title: Generating an API v2 token
docs.text:
The token is generated from the console itself, with the user who will sign the calls:

  1. Go to People → Edit my user.
  2. Scroll down to the Create Token API v2 section.
  3. Enter a Label that identifies the use —for example, CMDB integration— and an Expiration.
  4. Click Create Token.

The token is shown only once. Copy it and store it somewhere safe; if you lose it, you can only delete it and create another. The expiration date is optional, but setting it is the difference between a token that expires and one that outlives the person who created it.

Below the form is the user's token list, with the label, expiry, last usage and the delete action. Each user manages their own: you can have several and each integration should have its own.

docs.title: Opening the Swagger shipped with the installation
docs.text:
The interactive documentation is at:

https://<IP-or-FQDN>/pandoraitsm/api/

The first time it is opened, the server takes a few seconds to organise the documentation. If the installation lives under another path, replace /pandoraitsm with the right one: the base URL is the same one you use to enter the console.

The OpenAPI specification in JSON is at:

https://<IP-or-FQDN>/pandoraitsm/api/v2/pandoraitsm.json

That file is what Swagger consumes and what you can use to generate clients or documentation with any OpenAPI-compatible tool.

Swagger groups the commands by area —users, incidents, inventory, changes, CRM, and so on— and shows the GET, POST, PUT and DELETE methods of each resource.

docs.title: Authorising in Swagger
docs.text:
With Swagger open, click Authorize. In the dialog, paste the token —only the token, without the word Bearer— and click Authorize again. The command padlocks close and you can send requests.

One important warning: the Authorize form accepts any value, valid or not. It does not check the token at that moment. The check happens when you execute a call, so always look at the server response. A closed padlock is not proof that the token works.

docs.title: Example: checking the connection with ping
docs.text:
The simplest command to validate the token and connectivity is ping:

  1. Expand the Authentication group.
  2. Open GET /ping.
  3. Click Try it out.
  4. Click Execute.

If everything is fine, the Response body shows:

{
  "valid": true
}

If it returns 401 or 403, the problem is the token or the IP list. If it returns a connection error, it is almost always the IP list or a proxy in between.

docs.title: A query call
docs.text:
Once authorisation works, every command is used the same way. For example, GET /user/list:

  1. Open the users group and the GET /user/list command.
  2. Click Try it out.
  3. Fill in page and sizePage —for example, 1 and 10— and, if you want, a sortField.
  4. Click Execute.

The response is a JSON document with two blocks: data, with the users on the page, and paginationData, with the total number of records and pages. The available parameters and required fields appear in the command itself; the Try it out button enables them and the response schema shows what you will receive.

Every command has its own schema and examples. That is the reference to consult before writing an integration, not a list copied into a manual.

docs.title: Good practices
docs.text:
• One token per integration, with a label and an expiration date. If something leaks, you know what to delete.
  • Delete tokens that are no longer used; the list is there for that.
  • Use HTTPS. The token travels in the Authorization header and must not go in the URL.
  • Do not confuse the API v2 token with the API v1 API key: they are different things and are not interchangeable.
  • Keep the list of IPs allowed to access the API as short as possible.

docs.title: API v1 (legacy)
docs.text:
The Pandora ITSM 1.0 API is still alive for compatibility. It is not a REST API: it is an HTTP call to include/api.php with an operation (op) and a list of comma-separated parameters. It returns CSV by default, XML on request and, in some calls, JSON.

If you are starting an integration, use the API v2 in chapter 11.1. This API is only maintained for old scripts and integrations that already speak its dialect. The source of truth is include/api.php and include/functions_api.php; whatever is not in the dispatcher does not exist, no matter how much old documentation mentions it.

docs.title: What it is and how to call it
docs.text:
The base URL is the console URL followed by include/api.php:

https://<Console_web_URL>/pandoraitsm/include/api.php?<parameters>

The common parameters are:

Parameter Required What it does user Yes Pandora ITSM user running the call and subject to ACLs. user_pass Yes, except bearer token User password. pass Only if api_password is configured API-specific password. op Yes Operation to run. params Depends on the operation Operation parameters, separated by token. token No Separator for params; comma (,) by default. return_type No csv (default), xml or json depending on the operation. info No info=version returns the version without authentication.

The information call needs no user, password or authorised IP:

…/include/api.php?info=version

It returns a string similar to:

Pandora ITSM Enterprise Edition 5.0.109 Build 260603 MR109

An unknown operation does not return a descriptive error: the dispatcher sleeps for 15 seconds and ends without a body. If a script hangs, check the op name first.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: API 1.0 chains several checks. Every call except info=version goes through the IP list and user authentication.

docs.title: IP list
docs.text:
The list is configured under Setup → Setup → General setup, field List of IP with access to API (token api_acl). By default it only allows 127.0.0.1.

It accepts addresses separated by commas, spaces or line breaks, and an asterisk as a wildcard: 192.168.7.* or *. The code uses a regular expression, so the wildcard can also match part of an address. Opening the API to * is convenient for testing and a bad idea in production.

docs.title: API password
docs.text:
If api_password is not empty, it must be sent in the pass parameter. If it is empty, the check is skipped.

The password travels unencrypted. If you use this method, the call must go over HTTPS; over HTTP anyone listening on the network can see it.

docs.title: User and password
docs.text: user and user_pass are required in every call that does not use a bearer token. There is no way to disable this check: the API password is a second factor, not a replacement.

docs.title: Bearer token
docs.text:
You can also authenticate with the HTTP header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is compared with the api_key field of the user named in user. The IP list still applies. If the header is present, the API does not use user_pass or pass; if the token does not match, the response is 401.

Example with curl:

curl -k \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PITSM_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://192.0.2.10/pandoraitsm/include/api.php?user=admin&op=get_groups&return_type=xml"

If authentication fails, the API responds 401 with no body. There is no different error message for a missing user, a wrong password or an unauthorised IP.

docs.title: Call format
docs.text:
params is an ordered list. The default separator is a comma, but it can be changed with token:

…&op=create_workunit&params=1,Description,0.5,0,1,1
…&op=create_workunit&token=|&params=1|Description|0.5|0|1|1

Two conventions recur in ticket calls:

  • A comma inside a value is written as :::.
  • A space is encoded as %20 in the URL.

For example, Doe, John is sent as Doe:::%20John. Not every function reverses the substitution; those that support it apply it to the title, description or name, depending on the case.

return_type accepts csv (default), xml and, only in calls that implement it, json: tickets, work units, statuses, groups, users, priorities, fields, types and ticket count.

Successful responses are not always 1: many calls return the created identifier, a 0 or a -1. ACLs are checked inside each function and may log an audit entry before exiting without a body.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Each call has its own entry. Parameters are shown in the exact order of params; a parameter marked as required must always be present, even if the format allows it to be empty.

docs.title: get_login
docs.text:
Checks that credentials are valid. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_login

Returns: 1 if authentication is correct. On failure, the call has already returned 401 before reaching here.

docs.title: create_user
docs.text:
Creates a user and assigns a group and profile. Parameters: user (required), group (required), profile (required), email (optional), password (optional; if empty, the calling user's name is used), description (optional), real name (optional), external (0 or 1).

…/api.php?user=admin&user_pass=adminpass&op=create_user&params=jorge,3,4,jorge@example.com,userpass,description,Jorge%20Surname,1

Returns: 1 on success, 0 on failure. Requires UM permission. external=1 creates level -1 (Standalone); external=0 creates level 0 (grouped).

docs.title: get_incidents
docs.text:
Lists tickets visible to the user. Parameters: search string, status, group (required; 1 for all), priority, inventory, owner, creator, ticket id and Pandora inventory id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incidents&params=day,-10,1,-1,0,admin,user1

Statuses: 0 all, 1 new, 2 unconfirmed, 3 assigned, 4 reopened, 5 pending closure, 6 pending third party, 7 closed, -10 all except closed. Priorities: 10, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, -1.

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON. Internal limit of 5,000 tickets. A non-administrator only sees tickets they own or created.

docs.title: user_exists_in_group
docs.text:
Checks whether a user belongs to one or more groups. Parameters: user, group1, group2…

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=user_exists_in_group&params=test,4,5

Returns: 1 or 0. An administrator returns 1 without checking groups.

docs.title: get_incident_details
docs.text:
Returns ticket details. Parameter: ticket id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_details&params=2

Returns: CSV or XML with the ticket fields.

docs.title: create_incident
docs.text:
Creates a ticket. Parameters: title (required), group (required), priority, description, inventories separated by :, ticket type, email copy, owner, parent ticket, status (required), extra_data, resolution, extra_data2, extra_data3, extra_data4 and the type custom fields from position 15.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=create_incident&params=Title,2,1,Description%20of%20the%20incident,1:2:3,1,copy@example.com,admin,0,1

Returns: the created ticket id or -1 on failure. Requires IW permission. An empty title aborts the call. A comma in the title or description is sent as :::.

docs.title: update_incident
docs.text:
Updates a ticket. Parameters: id, title, description, epilogue, group, priority, resolution, status, owner, parent, type, extra_data, extra_data2, extra_data3, extra_data4 and custom fields from position 15.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=update_incident&params=4,new%20title,new%20description,new%20epilog,4,2,1,3,admin,0,6

Returns: update result. If the ticket is closed, the resolution is stored; otherwise it is forced to 0. Only the owner, creator or an administrator can modify it.

docs.title: delete_incident
docs.text:
Deletes a ticket. Parameter: ticket id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=delete_incident&params=3

Returns: 1. Requires access to the ticket.

docs.title: add_inventory_to_ticket
docs.text:
Links an inventory object to a ticket. Parameters: ticket id, inventory id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=add_inventory_to_ticket&params=1,2

Returns: 1 or 0. Requires VW permission.

docs.title: get_incident_tracking
docs.text:
Returns the ticket tracking history. Parameter: ticket id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_tracking&params=2

Returns: CSV or XML with tracking records.

docs.title: get_incidents_resolutions
docs.text:
Returns the resolution catalogue. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incidents_resolutions

Returns: CSV or XML with id and name for each resolution.

docs.title: get_incidents_status
docs.text:
Returns the status catalogue. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incidents_status

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with id and name for each status.

docs.title: get_incident_priorities
docs.text:
Returns the priority catalogue. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_priorities

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with id and name for each priority.

docs.title: get_incident_fields
docs.text:
Returns the custom fields for a ticket type and, when a ticket is given, its values. Parameters: type id, ticket id (optional).

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_fields&params=4,32

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with the fields. Without a ticket, it only returns the type definition.

docs.title: get_types
docs.text:
Returns the ticket type catalogue. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_types

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with id and name for each type.

docs.title: get_tickets_count
docs.text:
Counts tickets grouped by a column and period. Parameters: column, maximum days.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_tickets_count&params=id_grupo,30

Returns: JSON with the count by group. It is the only call that always returns JSON, even if another return_type is requested.

docs.title: get_incident_workunits
docs.text:
Lists the ticket work units. Parameter: ticket id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_workunits&params=3

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with the work units.

docs.title: create_workunit
docs.text:
Adds a work unit to a ticket. Parameters: ticket id, description, hours, cost (0 or 1), public (0 or 1), profile id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=create_workunit&params=1,Description,0.5,0,1,1

Returns: 0 or an error message. It does not accept closed tickets or duplicate a work unit with the same description on the same ticket.

docs.title: get_incident_files
docs.text:
Lists the ticket attachments. Parameter: ticket id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incident_files&params=1

Returns: CSV or XML with the attachments.

docs.title: download_file
docs.text:
Downloads an attachment. Parameter: attachment id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=download_file&params=32

Returns: file content in Base64.

docs.title: attach_file
docs.text:
Attaches a file to a ticket. Parameters: ticket id, name, size, description, Base64 content.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=attach_file&params=1,example.txt,234,File%20of%20example,aW50ZWdyaWEgcm9ja3M=

Returns: 0 on success, -1 if it cannot write. If the file already exists on the ticket, it returns 0 without duplicating it.

docs.title: delete_file
docs.text:
Deletes an attachment. Parameter: attachment id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=delete_file&params=32

Returns: 0 on success, -1 if the permission check fails, -2 if it cannot delete the physical file.

docs.title: validate_user
docs.text:
Checks user and password. Parameters: user, password.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=validate_user&params=jorge,jorge_pass

Returns: 1 if correct, 0 if the user does not exist or is disabled, -1 if the password is wrong.

docs.title: delete_user
docs.text:
Deletes a user. Parameter: user.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=delete_user&params=pepe

Returns: 1 or 0. It does not allow deleting admin. Requires UM permission.

docs.title: user_exists
docs.text:
Checks whether a user exists. Parameter: user.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=user_exists&params=pepe

Returns: 1 or 0.

docs.title: get_users
docs.text:
Lists users visible to the caller. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_users

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with the identifiers.

docs.title: get_groups
docs.text:
Lists visible groups. Optional parameter: params=1 to include group 1.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_groups
…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_groups&params=1

Returns: CSV, XML or JSON with id and name for each group.

docs.title: get_stats
docs.text:
Returns a ticket metric. Parameters: metric, string, status, user, group, company, inventory, priority.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_stats&params=sla_compliance
…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_stats&params=opened,,1

Metrics: total_incidents, opened, closed, avg_life, sla_compliance, avg_scoring and avg_worktime. If no group is given, group 1 is used.

Returns: a CSV or XML value.

docs.title: get_incidents_summary
docs.text:
Returns the summary by status. Optional parameter: new, unconfirmed, assigned, reopened, verified, pending_third_person, closed, not_closed or total.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incidents_summary
…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_incidents_summary&params=not_closed

Returns: every counter or only the requested field, in CSV or XML.

docs.title: get_last_cron_execution
docs.text:
Returns the minutes since the last cron run. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_last_cron_execution

Returns: minutes, or -1 if there is no record.

docs.title: get_previous_cron_execution
docs.text:
Returns the minutes since the previous cron run. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_previous_cron_execution

Returns: minutes, or -1 if there is no record.

docs.title: get_num_queued_emails
docs.text:
Returns pending emails in the queue. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_num_queued_emails

Returns: number of emails.

docs.title: get_last_invoice_id
docs.text:
Returns the last bill_id of a submitted invoice. It takes no parameters.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_last_invoice_id

Returns: the identifier or an empty value.

docs.title: get_invoice
docs.text:
Returns invoice data. Parameter: bill_id.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=get_invoice&params=140601_0071

Returns: CSV or XML with the invoice.

docs.title: create_invoice
docs.text:
Creates an invoice. Parameters: user, task, company, bill_id, concept, amount, tax, currency, description, locked, locking user, creation date, payment date, status, reference, internal note, type (Submitted or Received), language.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=create_invoice&params=admin,,1,140601_0082,paso,3.00,,EUR,,,,,,paid,,,Submitted,

Returns: status and message, for example 1,"invoice created" or 0,"invalid billing id". Requires CW permission.

docs.title: create_company
docs.text:
Creates a company. Parameters: name, address, tax id, role, country, manager, parent company.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=create_company&params=Artica,AlbertoAguilera,12312312,1,Spain,admin,0

Returns: the created company id. Requires CW permission; the manager must exist or be empty.

docs.title: mark_created_incident
docs.text:
Marks the ticket creation record with extra information. Parameters: ticket id, text.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=mark_created_incident&params=10,External%20origin

Returns: raw update result, without CSV or XML.

docs.title: mark_updated_incident
docs.text:
Marks the ticket update record. Parameters: ticket id, text.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=mark_updated_incident&params=10,Updated%20by%20API

Returns: raw update result.

docs.title: ovo_manager
docs.text:
Specific OVO integration. Parameters: title, group, priority, description, inventory, type, extra information, group message.

…/api.php?user=user&user_pass=userpass&op=ovo_manager&params=Title,2,2,Description,10626,10,extra,msg

It uses group 11 and user ovo in a fixed way. Returns: a variable result depending on the updates it applies. It is not a general call.

docs.title: reset_double_factor
docs.text:
Resets two-factor authentication. Parameter: encrypted hash in the console format (for administrators).

…/api.php?user=admin&user_pass=adminpass&op=reset_double_factor&params=<hash>

Returns: JSON with status. A normal user can only reset their own factor.

docs.title: Extending the API
docs.text:
API 1.0 has no automatic router. Adding a call requires two pieces:

  1. A function in include/functions_api.php that receives $return_type and the parameters, and returns or prints the result.
  2. A case in the switch ($op) of include/api.php that invokes it.

The minimum skeleton is:

function api_my_call($return_type, $user, $params)
{
    // ACL checks and validation.
    $result = 1;

    switch ($return_type) {
        case 'xml':
            echo xml_node($result);
            break;
        default:
            echo $result;
            break;
    }
}

And in the dispatcher:

case 'my_call':
    $params = explode($token, $params);
    echo api_my_call($return_type, $user, $params);
    break;

Keep the output format and ACL checks inside the function. API v1 does not provide any of that for you.

docs.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
docs.text:
Pandora ITSM publishes an MCP server so an AI agent can query tickets, companies, contacts, deals, notes, email, schedules and web tracking without leaving the console. It is not a chatbot: it is a read-only layer that speaks the standard protocol of MCP clients and authenticates with OAuth 2.1.

The idea is simple: the agent stops copying and pasting data from the console and asks directly. The server answers with the same ACLs, the same audit trail and the same limits as API v2. The difference is the caller, which is now a model rather than a script.

This chapter covers the Pandora ITSM MCP server: which tools it exposes, how to enable it, how a client authenticates, what each tool returns and where access stops. API v2 remains the way to write and to integrate applications; MCP is a read-only façade for agents.

docs.title: What it is and what it allows
docs.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open protocol that lets a client (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, a web connector) discover tools and call them against a server. Pandora ITSM implements the server side over HTTP, with JSON-RPC 2.0 and OAuth 2.1 authentication.

docs.title: A read-only server
docs.text:
Every tool in the catalogue declares readOnlyHint: true. The server does not create, update or delete tickets, companies or any other object. It does not attach files or send email either. If the agent needs to write, it must use API v2 with an API token and the corresponding ACLs.

The catalogue is grouped into seven areas:

Area Tools Purpose Companies company_search, company_get, activity_feed Find accounts, read their profile and see recent activity. Tickets ticket_search, ticket_get Find tickets and read their status, description, tracking and work units. Contacts contact_search, contact_get Find people at a company and read their profile. Deals deal_search, deal_get Query the pipeline, the forecast and the detail of a deal. Notes, email and schedules note_list, email_list, schedule_list Read notes, email metadata and tasks, meetings or reminders. Web tracking webtracking_summary Count attributed contacts by source, category, campaign or month. Reference reference_data Translate identifiers and enums, and discover the allowed filters.

docs.title: What you can ask
docs.text:
Some real examples of what an agent can resolve with these tools:

  • "What is the status of ticket 4321 and what happened in the latest replies?"
  • "Summarise Acme's activity over the last week."
  • "Which deals has salesperson jlopez moved this quarter, and what is the weighted forecast?"
  • "How many contacts attributed to Google Ads arrived this month?"
  • "Give me the closed tickets in the Support group between 1 and 15 November."

The agent chains searches and reads: first it resolves identifiers with reference_data, then it searches with *_search, and finally it opens the detail with *_get.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
• It does not write. There are no create, update or delete tools.
  • It does not return email bodies or recipients; only metadata.
  • It does not return email or phone numbers in company and contact searches. To get them, request the detail of a specific contact.
  • It does not replace API v2 or the console. It is a read-only view for agents.
  • It does not share tokens with API v2: an OAuth token issued for MCP is only valid on /mcp.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Detail HTTPS Cloud MCP clients require HTTPS. OAuth redirects only allow HTTPS or loopback HTTP (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]). Public URL Public MCP URL must be an absolute HTTPS URL ending in /mcp. Without it, MCP cannot be enabled and OAuth metadata cannot be published. API ACL The List of IP with access to API list (api_acl) also applies to /mcp and the OAuth endpoints. It must include the egress IPs of the clients. With cloud clients, add their ranges or open the list to *; the real control is then the MCP policy and OAuth. User and permissions The user who authorises access must be active, included in the MCP policy and hold the product permissions required by each tool. Compatible client The client must support remote MCP servers over HTTP and OAuth 2.1 with dynamic registration and PKCE.

docs.title: Enabling and configuring MCP
docs.text: Configuration lives under Setup → Setup → MCP setup. Only administrators can open and save it. The page is organised into tabs: Status, Discovery, Connect, Access policy, Runtime settings and Authorizations.

docs.title: The global switch
docs.text:
Enable MCP server turns the server on or off. While it is off, the endpoint returns a policy error and clients cannot use any tool. When it is enabled, the page shows the remaining tabs and the getting-started guide:

  1. Enable MCP.
  2. Choose who can use it and set the public URL.
  3. Check the API ACL.
  4. Connect the client; the first connection opens the consent page.

MCP cannot be enabled without Public MCP URL. The server needs a trusted URL to build the OAuth issuer and the discovery documents, and it never derives them from the Host header.

docs.title: Status and readiness checklist
docs.text:
The Status tab shows the endpoint and five checks:

Check Meaning MCP enabled The global switch is on. Access policy At least one user or group is allowed, or the policy allows everyone. HTTPS The console is served over HTTPS. Public MCP URL The public URL is configured. API ACL The API ACL is not restricted to 127.0.0.1 or localhost.

A red dot does not necessarily block saving, but it explains why a client cannot connect. The API ACL check is the one most often forgotten: if the list only allows loopback, a client arriving from another IP receives 401 before the OAuth dance even starts.

docs.title: OAuth discovery
docs.text:
The Discovery tab shows the two URLs a client queries before authenticating:

https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server

Both documents must be published at the domain root. If Pandora ITSM runs in a subdirectory or behind a proxy, the web server must rewrite or align those paths; in that case the discovery URL appends the resource path. The Discovery tab shows the two exact URLs for the installation and includes a Check button that makes a real request and marks the result.

docs.title: Apache configuration
docs.text:
The API v2 serves the documents at /pandoraitsm/api/v2/.well-known/..., but the client looks for them at the domain root. Those paths must be rewritten in the HTTPS virtual host. Add the rules to your 443 virtual host; the block below shows the minimum context. With the installation under /pandoraitsm and the public URL https://itsm.example.com/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp:

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName itsm.example.com
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html

    RewriteEngine On

    # Protected resource (RFC 9728)
    RewriteRule ^/\.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp$ \
        /pandoraitsm/api/v2/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource [PT,L]

    # Authorization server (RFC 8414)
    RewriteRule ^/\.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/pandoraitsm/api/v2$ \
        /pandoraitsm/api/v2/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server [PT,L]

    # Fallback when the client requests the root path without the resource path
    RewriteRule ^/\.well-known/oauth-protected-resource$ \
        /pandoraitsm/api/v2/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource [PT,L]

    RewriteRule ^/\.well-known/oauth-authorization-server$ \
        /pandoraitsm/api/v2/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server [PT,L]
</VirtualHost>

Replace pandoraitsm with the real directory of the console. If the installation is at the root, change /pandoraitsm/api/v2 to /api/v2 and remove pandoraitsm from the paths. The first two rules handle the canonical path with the resource path; the last two cover clients that request only /.well-known/.... [PT,L] lets Apache pass the request to the API front controller without changing the URL the client sees.

Make sure mod_rewrite is enabled and that the rules are in the 443 virtual host, not in a .htaccess file (if you put them in .htaccess, remove the leading slash from the patterns). Then reload Apache:

# RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux
sudo systemctl reload httpd

# Debian, Ubuntu
sudo systemctl reload apache2

Check both URLs from an IP allowed in api_acl:

curl -s https://itsm.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s https://itsm.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | python3 -m json.tool

The first must return resource with the public URL and authorization_servers; the second must return issuer and the endpoints. If you get the console HTML or a 404, the rule is not matching: check the ServerName, the DocumentRoot and that mod_rewrite is loaded. If there is a reverse proxy in front, it must forward /.well-known/oauth-* to this Apache.

The protected resource document declares the resource, the issuer and the itsm.read scope. The authorisation server document declares the authorisation, token, registration and revocation endpoints, the authorization_code flow, refresh, PKCE S256 and the none client authentication method.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The Access policy tab decides which users can use MCP. There are four lists and two recursion switches:

  • Allowed users and Blocked users.
  • Allowed groups and Blocked groups.
  • Include child groups for allowed groups.
  • Include child groups for blocked groups.

Evaluation is cumulative and blocking wins:

  1. If MCP is disabled, everything is denied.
  2. If the user is disabled, it is denied.
  3. If the user is in Blocked users, it is denied.
  4. If the user belongs to a blocked group, it is denied.
  5. If the policy allows all users or all groups, or the user is in Allowed users, it is allowed.
  6. If the user belongs to an allowed group, it is allowed.
  7. In any other case, it is denied.

The interface no longer shows the "allow everyone" switches; the API keeps them for compatibility. If they are enabled through the API, the resulting policy allows everyone and the block lists still take precedence.

docs.title: Runtime settings
docs.text:
The Runtime settings tab controls the server behaviour:

Setting What it does Default Range Maximum rows per tool call Caps how many rows a tool can return in one call. Each tool schema already allows up to 50; this setting can reduce it. If the client requests more rows than allowed, it gets the configured value. 50 1–50 Requests per minute and token Sets how many requests each token can make per minute. When exceeded, the response is 429 with Retry-After. 0 disables the limit. 60 0–1000 Audit retention (days) Decides how many days calls are kept in the audit log before being purged. 90 1–3650 Public MCP URL Public endpoint URL. It is used to build the OAuth issuer and the discovery documents; without it, MCP cannot be enabled. It must use HTTPS and end in /mcp. empty HTTPS URL Authorization lifetime (days, 0 = unlimited) Sets the maximum lifetime of an authorisation from the moment the user approves consent. When it expires, the client must authorise again. 0 makes it unlimited. 90 0–3650 Allowed redirect hosts Decides which hosts a client may redirect to after consent. One host per line; *.example.com includes subdomains; empty allows any host. claude.ai, chatgpt.com, localhost, 127.0.0.1 Up to 50

Public MCP URL does not accept credentials, a query string or a fragment. If the installation is behind a proxy, the URL must be the one the client sees, not the server's internal URL.

docs.title: Authorisations
docs.text:
The Authorizations tab lists the applications each user has authorised: client name, redirect hosts, user, last IP, authorisation date, last use, expiry and a revoke button. Revoking an authorisation deletes that user's tokens for that client; it does not affect other users of the same client.

Each user can view and revoke their own authorisations from the MCP applications tab of their user profile.

docs.title: Configuring through the API
docs.text:
The policy can also be read and written with API v2, using an administrator token. These endpoints do not accept MCP OAuth tokens.

GET /api/v2/mcp/permission
PUT /api/v2/mcp/permission

The PUT accepts the policy fields and leaves omitted fields unchanged:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "allowedUsers": ["admin", "support"],
  "blockedUsers": ["temporary"],
  "allowedGroups": [1, 26],
  "blockedGroups": [],
  "allUsersAllowed": false,
  "allGroupsAllowed": false,
  "allowedGroupsRecursion": true,
  "blockedGroupsRecursion": false
}

The response returns the saved policy. A 400 means an invalid value; a 403 means the token does not belong to an administrator.

docs.title: Connecting an MCP client
docs.text: The Connect tab offers the URL, a prompt ready to paste into the agent and the alternative for web chats. The prompt is in English because the agent consumes it, not the user.

docs.title: The agent prompt
docs.text:
Connect yourself to the Pandora ITSM MCP server.

Server
- Name: itsm
- Transport: Streamable HTTP (remote MCP server)
- URL: https://itsm.example.com/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp
- Authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. The server publishes
  its metadata under /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Do not ask me for an API key or
  a client secret.

Steps
1. Identify which MCP client you are (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, VS Code...) and add
   the server with that client's official method: its CLI command if it has one, otherwise its
   MCP configuration file. Use the user-level scope unless I say otherwise.
2. Keep the existing configuration: add or update only the "itsm" entry, and show me the change
   before writing any file.
3. Start the authorization (for example, /mcp in Claude Code). A Pandora ITSM page opens in the
   browser: I will sign in and approve the access myself. Never ask for my password.
4. Once connected, list the available tools and show them to me. They are read-only.

If the URL is not reachable or its certificate is not trusted, stop and tell me the exact error.
Do not disable TLS verification. If you cannot configure MCP servers yourself (for example, a web
chat), tell me to add a custom connector with the URL above instead.

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
OpenCode adds the server with its CLI and stores the configuration at user scope:

opencode mcp add itsm --url https://itsm.example.com/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp --global
opencode mcp list

Then, in the interface, open /mcps, select itsm and complete authorisation in the browser.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add --transport http itsm https://itsm.example.com/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp --scope user
claude mcp list

Inside Claude Code, /mcp shows the server and starts sign-in. The token is stored and refreshed automatically.

docs.title: Cursor and other clients with a configuration file
docs.text:
Many clients read an mcpServers entry with the server URL:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "itsm": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://itsm.example.com/pandoraitsm/api/v2/mcp"
    }
  }
}

The exact name of the transport field changes between clients (type, transport, streamable-http). If the client does not support remote HTTP servers or cannot do OAuth with dynamic registration, it will not connect: use the agent prompt or a compatible client.

docs.title: Claude.ai and ChatGPT
docs.text: Web chats cannot configure themselves. In Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, paste the public server URL and complete consent. The application then appears in the authorisation list.

docs.title: Checking the connection
docs.text: A successful connection returns the catalogue of 14 tools with tools/list. If the client shows zero tools, check in this order: URL, certificate, API ACL, Public MCP URL, MCP policy and user permissions.

docs.title: Catalogue
docs.text: Tool Title What it returns Maximum rows company_search Company · Search Companies with creation date, billing and pagination. 50 company_get Company · Get Company profile; detail includes address, tax, billing and custom fields. 1 activity_feed Company · Activity feed Activity references for a company, contact or salesperson, without message bodies. 50 ticket_search Tickets · Search Tickets without the full description. 50 ticket_get Tickets · Get One ticket with description, tracking and, optionally, work units. 20 deal_search Deals · Search Deals with live operations and weighted forecast aggregates. 50 deal_get Deals · Get Deal detail. 1 contact_search Contacts · Search Contacts without email or phone. 50 contact_get Contacts · Get Contact profile; detail includes email, phone, mobile and custom fields. 1 note_list Notes · List Notes with truncated text and pagination. 50 email_list Emails · List Email metadata without body or recipients. 50 schedule_list Schedules · List Tasks, meetings, calls and reminders. 50 webtracking_summary Web tracking · Summary Attributed contacts grouped by source, category, campaign or month. 50 reference_data Reference · Data Identifiers, enums and allowed filters. 50 per group

docs.title: How to call a tool
docs.text:
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "ticket_search",
    "arguments": {
      "freeSearch": "printer",
      "status": "ASSIGNED",
      "size": 10
    }
  }
}

Arguments must be an object. An unknown tool name returns -32601; an argument that is not in the schema returns -32602/isError.

docs.title: Common parameters
docs.text: Only list tools share these parameters. *_get does not paginate or sort.

docs.title: Pagination
Sorting
Generic filters
docs.text:
Company, contact, deal, schedule, note, email and activity tools accept fieldConditions: up to 10 conditions on real columns. jsonPath and derived aliases are not supported.

{
  "fieldConditions": [
    { "field": "createdAt", "operator": ">=", "value": "2026-01-01" },
    { "field": "country", "operator": "in", "value": ["ES", "FR"] }
  ]
}

Supported operators:

Operator Use =, !=, <>, >, <, >=, <= Simple comparison. like, not_like Text match. in, not_in List of up to 50 values. between, not_between Two-value range. is_null, is_not_null Null or not null. is_empty, is_not_empty Empty or not empty.

ticket_search does not accept fieldConditions; use its named filters (status, priority, idGroup, idUser, dates). To find out which fields and operators each tool accepts, call reference_data with types: ["filter_fields"].

docs.title: Dates
docs.text: Dates are sent as YYYY-MM-DD. The server also accepts an ISO 8601 date and time and keeps the date. In ranges, the upper bound includes the whole day when the tool declares it so (createdTo, lastActivityTo). An invalid date returns isError with the field name.

docs.title: Identifiers and reference data
docs.text:
Identifiers are the console's. They are not invented or derived from the name. Before filtering by status, priority, group, pipeline or stage, request the tables from reference_data:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "reference_data",
    "arguments": {
      "types": ["ticket_statuses", "ticket_priorities", "groups"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: company_search
docs.text:
Finds companies by text, tags, dates, billing or generic conditions. It does not return email or phone.

Parameter Type Notes freeSearch string Name or comments. tags integer[] All tags must match. dateBegin, dateEnd date Last update, inclusive. createdFrom, createdTo date Creation date, inclusive. lastActivityFrom, lastActivityTo date Last activity, inclusive. minBilling, maxBilling integer Billing range. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idCompany, name, createdAt, lastUpdate, lastActivityAt, country, manager, billing.

Returns idCompany, name, idCompanyRole, country, manager, createdAt, lastActivityAt, activeContractDates and billing.

docs.title: company_get
docs.text: Parameter Type Notes idCompany integer ≥ 1 Required. detail boolean false by default. With true, adds address, idTax, comments, parent company, payment conditions, dates, billing and custom fields.

docs.title: activity_feed
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes idCompany, idUser integer / string Filter by company or salesperson. fromDate, toDate date Activity range. freeSearch string Free text. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idCompanyActivity, createdAt, idCompany, idContact, idDeal, section, action.

Returns references to company, contact, deal, note, email, schedule, meeting, form, contract and invoice, without message bodies.

docs.title: ticket_search
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes freeSearch string Title or description. idCompany integer Current company of the creator, not a historical snapshot. status string NEW, UNCONFIRMED, ASSIGNED, REOPENED, VERIFIED, PENDING_THIRD_PERSON, CLOSED, NOTCLOSED. priority string INFORMATIVE, LOW, MEDIUM, SERIOUS, VERY_SERIOUS, MAINTENANCE. idGroup integer ≥ 0 Group. idUser string Ticket owner. fromDate, toDate date Creation date, inclusive. sortField string idIncidence, startDate, updateDate, closeDate, title, status, priority, idGroup, owner, idCreator.

Returns idIncidence, idCompany, startDate, closeDate, updateDate, title, owner, status, priority, idGroup and resolution. Visibility is enforced by the user's group ACL.

docs.title: ticket_get
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes idIncidence integer ≥ 1 Required. includeTracks boolean true by default; includes up to size tracking entries. includeWorkunits boolean false by default; includes work units. size integer 1–20 Tracking or work unit rows.

Returns the ticket data (idIncidence, idCompany, title, description, status, priority, owner, idGroup, idCreator, startDate, updateDate, closeDate, resolution, epilog, idParent, idIncidenceType). Description and epilog are truncated to 4000 characters; tracking and work units to 2000.

docs.title: contact_search
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes freeSearch string Name, email or description. idCompany integer Company. tags integer[] All tags must match. companyRoles integer[] Company roles. disabled boolean Filter disabled contacts. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idContact, fullname, createdAt, updatedAt, idCompany.

It does not return email or phone. Returns idContact, idCompany, companyName, fullname, position, disabled, manager, createdAt and updatedAt.

docs.title: contact_get
docs.text: Parameter Type Notes idContact integer ≥ 1 Required. detail boolean false by default. With true, adds email, phone, mobile, description, custom fields and newsletter subscription.

docs.title: deal_search
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes freeSearch string Name or description. idCompany, idOwner integer / string Company or salesperson. idPipeline, idStage integer Pipeline or stage. stages integer[] Several stages. createdFrom, createdTo date Creation. updatedFrom, updatedTo date Last update. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idDeal, name, amount, closeDate, startDate, createdAt, updatedAt, lastActivity, idOwner, idCompany.

Returns idDeal, name, idOwner, idCompany, idPipeline, idStage, amount, closeDate, startDate, updatedAt and lastActivity. It adds aggregates.liveOperations and aggregates.forecast for the same filter.

docs.title: deal_get
docs.text: Parameter Type Notes idDeal integer ≥ 1 Required. detail boolean false by default. With true, adds description, custom fields and creation date.

docs.title: note_list
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes idCompany, idContact, idDeal, idContract integer Object the note belongs to. idUser string Author. freeSearch string Note text. fromDate, toDate date Creation. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idNote, createdAt, updatedAt, idCompany, idContact, idDeal, idUser, pinned.

Text is truncated to 1000 characters. Returns idNote, idCompany, idContact, idDeal, idContract, idUser, note, pinned, createdAt and updatedAt.

docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes freeSearch string Subject. idCompany integer Company. idContacts integer[] Linked contacts. excludeCampaignEmails boolean Exclude campaign email. excludeScheduledEmails boolean Exclude scheduled email. fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idEmail, sentAt, subject, idCompany, idDeal, isSent.

It does not return body or recipients. Returns idEmail, idCompany, idDeal, subject, isSent, sentAt, createdBy, createdAt, statusDelivery, isScheduled and attachments.
