docs.title: schedule_list
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes idCompany, idContact, idDeal integer Related object. assignedTo string Assigned user. state string open, in_progress, completed, on_hold, cancelled, expired. priority string low, medium, high, urgent. type string todo, mail, meeting, call. freeSearch string Title or description. fromDate, toDate date Range according to dateField. dateField string expirationDate, resolutionDate or createdAt (default). fieldConditions object[] Up to 10 conditions. sortField string idSchedule, title, expirationDate, resolutionDate, reminderDate, priority, state, type, assignedTo, createdAt, updatedAt.

Description is truncated to 1000 characters. Returns idSchedule, title, description, type, priority, state, assignedTo, expirationDate, resolutionDate, reminderDate, idCompany, idDeal, idContact, createdBy, createdAt and updatedAt.

docs.title: webtracking_summary
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes groupBy string Required: source, sourceCategory, campaign or month. source string Exact source. sourceCategory string google_ads, chatgpt, direct, social. campaign string Exact campaign. attribution object Exact UTM or click ID filter. fromDate, toDate date Visit date, inclusive.

Returns groupBy, value and totalLeads, ordered by value. A contact may count in more than one group.

docs.title: reference_data
docs.text:
Parameter Type Notes types string[] Reference groups. If omitted, returns all. idPipeline integer ≥ 1 Filters the stages of one pipeline.

Available groups: ticket_statuses, ticket_priorities, groups, company_roles, deal_pipelines, deal_stages, schedule_types, schedule_priorities, schedule_states, stage_types, traffic_source_categories and filter_fields.

filter_fields returns, per tool, the condition fields, operators, maximum conditions, sort fields and maximum sort fields. It is the way to discover filters before using them.

docs.title: MCP policy and product ACLs
docs.text:
The MCP policy decides who can enter. Then each tool applies the product ACL:

Tool Permission checked company_search CR company_get CM activity_feed CR ticket_search Group ACL of the ticket list. ticket_get IR plus the ticket group ACL. deal_search CR deal_get CR contact_search CM contact_get CM note_list CR email_list CR schedule_list CRM webtracking_summary CM reference_data CR

A user allowed in MCP but without the product permission receives a tools/call with isError: true and the ACL message. There is no way to bypass the ticket group ACL: both the list and the detail apply it.

docs.title: Rate limit
docs.text:
The limit is per token and per minute. The default is 60 requests per minute. All calls count, not only tools/call. When exceeded, the response is 429 with Retry-After and a JSON-RPC -32002 error.

The counter is stored in tmcp_rate_limit and cleaned up opportunistically. A value of 0 disables the limit; do not do that on an exposed installation.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
Every tool call is recorded in tmcp_audit with:

Field Content id_user User who authorised the token. token_uuid Token UUID. tool Tool name. arguments Arguments, with secrets redacted and long texts trimmed. rows_returned Rows returned. duration_ms Duration. status ok, error or denied. error_code, error_message Failure reason, if any. ip Source IP. mcp_session Request identifier. created_at Date.

Arguments are redacted if the key contains pass, token, secret, authorization, cookie or session; texts are cut to 500 characters and the structure to three levels and 50 keys. Denied or rate-limited tool calls are also recorded.

Administrators can see the calls under Setup → Audit log → MCP, a tab that only appears when MCP is enabled. The default retention is 90 days.

docs.title: Privacy and truncation
docs.text:
Tool What is trimmed company_search, contact_search Do not return email or phone. contact_get With detail=true, returns email, phone and mobile. email_list Does not return body or recipients. ticket_get Description and epilog to 4000 characters; tracking and work units to 2000. note_list Text to 1000 characters. schedule_list Description to 1000 characters.

These limits are not configurable per tool. The goal is to keep an agent from dumping half the database into the model context.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix The client cannot discover OAuth (404 on /.well-known/...). The documents are not published at the domain root or the proxy does not rewrite them. Check the Discovery tab and the web server rewrite. 401 before the browser opens. The client IP is not in api_acl. Add the IP or range under Setup → Setup → General setup. 403 when enabling MCP. Public MCP URL is missing or the licence is invalid. Set the HTTPS URL ending in /mcp and check the licence. 503 on the metadata. Public MCP URL is empty. Set it; the OAuth issuer is never derived from Host. Consent is requested again and again. The authorisation expired (Authorization lifetime) or the refresh failed. Authorise again or extend the authorisation lifetime. 429 with Retry-After. Per-token limit exceeded. Wait or raise Requests per minute and token. The client sees zero tools. User without MCP policy, without product permissions or a client without OAuth. Check the policy, the ACL and client compatibility. size returns fewer rows than requested. Maximum rows per tool call reduces the size below the requested value. Raise the setting up to 50 or paginate. size greater than 50 returns an argument error. The schema limits size to 50. Request 50 or paginate. Unknown argument. The client sends a parameter that is not in the schema. Check tools/list or reference_data. Tickets from a group do not appear. The user's group ACL. Check the user's groups; MCP does not bypass the ACL.

docs.title: Relationship with API v2
docs.text:
MCP and API v2 share the base, authentication, ACL and licence, but they are not the same:

  • API v2 is the way to write and to integrate in general.
  • MCP is a read-only façade for agents, with tools and schemas designed for a model.
  • An MCP OAuth token is only valid on /mcp.
  • An API v2 token is also valid on /mcp, but it is not the recommended flow for agents.
  • The API v2 OpenAPI reference includes the /mcp, /mcp/permission and OAuth routes; it is useful to generate clients and to check response codes.

If you need to create tickets, update companies or run actions, use API v2 from chapter 11.1 with an API token and the user's permissions. MCP does not write.

docs.title: Pandora FMS integration
docs.text:
Pandora FMS monitors; Pandora ITSM responds. The integration exists so that the alert and the ticket do not live in separate worlds: a monitoring alert can open a ticket, and the technician who resolves it can see the asset that triggered it.

The integration runs in two directions. From Pandora FMS, tickets in Pandora ITSM are created, closed, viewed and edited, either by hand or automatically through alerts and event responses. In the other direction, Pandora ITSM receives the inventory of the Pandora FMS agents and turns it into Computer objects with their hardware, software and extended information.

Everything relies on the Pandora ITSM API v2. There is no shared database and no special agent: FMS calls the API with a token, and the API does the rest.

docs.title: Requirements and permissions
docs.text:
Before configuring anything, check these points:

  • Pandora FMS and Pandora ITSM can reach each other over the network, preferably over HTTPS.
  • The Pandora FMS version is 783 or later if you are going to use the joint installation from its console.
  • The Pandora FMS IP is allowed in Setup → Setup → General setup → List of IP with access to API in Pandora ITSM. By default only localhost is allowed.
  • You have an API v2 token generated in Pandora ITSM. Chapter 11.1 explains how to create one.
  • The token user has the IM (ticket management) and VW (inventory write) permissions. Without them, the API rejects FMS calls.

The token is the integration credential. Do not share it with other users or reuse it for a second tool; if it leaks, delete it and create another.

docs.title: Configuring the communication
docs.text:
There are two steps in Pandora ITSM: allow the IP and create the token.

  1. Add the Pandora FMS IP or range in Setup → Setup → General setup → List of IP with access to API.
  2. Generate a token in People → Edit my user → Create Token API v2, with a label such as Pandora FMS and an expiration date.
  3. Check that the token user can manage tickets (IM) and write inventory (VW).

In Pandora FMS, the integration is configured in its incident management section, setting the Pandora ITSM URL and the token. The detailed procedure lives in the Pandora FMS manual; it is not repeated here because it changes with the monitoring console and is not Pandora ITSM documentation.

When the communication works, FMS can create and close tickets in ITSM and show existing tickets. The quickest test is to open a ticket from FMS and check that it appears in Support → Tickets in Pandora ITSM.

docs.title: Inventory synchronisation
docs.text:
Synchronisation turns Pandora FMS agents into Pandora ITSM inventory objects. It is configured in Setup → Setup, tab Pandora FMS Inventory.

The screen has three blocks:

  • Clean objects: days after which objects marked as Missing and without a parent are deleted. 0 disables the cleanup.
  • Remote inventory: default values for the objects created by the synchronisation. Default owner is mandatory; associated companies and users decide their visibility.
  • Nodes connected: the Pandora FMS servers that have successfully connected to Pandora ITSM.

The node table shows the node name, the connection path —for example, http://172.16.0.1:90/pandora_console/api/v2—, the progress of synchronised agents, the connection status and the delete operation. A green dot means the node responds.

The node is not added by hand in Pandora ITSM: Pandora FMS registers it when the communication works. If it does not appear, the problem is in the FMS configuration, the URL or the token, not on this screen. To restart a connection, delete the node and configure it again from Pandora FMS.

Each synchronised object type sets its pace with Sync interval: Never, Weekly, Every 15 days, Monthly or First time only. The option only appears when nodes are configured and the type is associated with a Pandora FMS schema. Type, field and stock details are in chapter 4.1.

Synchronised objects are of type Computer and are linked to the agent through id_pandora. Their record shows the Hardware, Software and Extended Info tabs with the information collected by Pandora FMS.

Synchronisation is not immediate: the inventory cron, include/inventory_cron.php, runs it, usually every five minutes. On each run it records the inventory_crontask mark, synchronises the nodes, expires overdue schedules and removes Missing objects that no longer have a parent.

docs.title: Joint installation from the Pandora FMS console
docs.text:
Pandora FMS can install a Pandora ITSM instance from its own console. It is a quick way to test the integration, not the recommended path for production.

In Pandora FMS, go to Management → Settings → System Settings → ITSM and click Install ITSM.

Before installing, Pandora FMS checks three things:

  • That the itsm database does not exist; if it does not, it is created.
  • That the Pandora FMS user —usually pandora— has permission to create it.
  • That the /var/www/html/pandora_console/itsm directory does not exist; it will be created during the installation.

If the database user lacks permissions, the MySQL administrator must grant them before continuing:

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON `itsm`.* TO `pandora`;

The installation downloads the required packages from the official Pandora FMS repository and creates the ITSM directory inside the Pandora FMS console. The progress shows the steps and, at the end, a link to access the Pandora ITSM console for the first time.

When it finishes, check that you can access Pandora ITSM and that Pandora FMS can see the tickets. If the joint installation fails, review the MySQL permissions and disk space before repeating it.

docs.title: Good practices and common problems
docs.text:
• Use a dedicated token for the integration, with a label and an expiration date. If something leaks, you know what to delete.
  • Allow only the Pandora FMS IP, not an open range.
  • Check that the token user keeps IM and VW; a profile change breaks the integration without warning.
  • If the node does not appear, check the URL and token in Pandora FMS. If it appears but does not progress, look at the cron and the connection status.
  • Do not delete a node while it is synchronising. Wait until it finishes or the progress stops.
  • The joint installation is for testing. For production, install Pandora ITSM separately and configure the integration through the API.

For API and token details, go back to chapter 11.1. For object types, fields and stock control, to chapter 4.1. For tickets coming from FMS, to chapter 3.1.

docs.title: Pandora RC integration
docs.text:
Pandora RC is not just another remote desktop: it is a cloud-based remote management system. The agent connects out to the portal, not the other way around, so the device can change IP address, sit behind a firewall or use a home network without breaking the session. Pandora ITSM only opens the door from the inventory object.

The integration has two parts: configuring the portal credentials and preparing the inventory object that points to the agent. If either is missing, the remote access tab does not appear or the connection fails.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Pandora RC is a SaaS remote device management service. Each device has an installed agent and an identifier; the Pandora ITSM console uses that identifier to request a token and open a session inside an inventory tab.

The session is shown in an iframe with these views:

Tab What it is for Information Agent summary and connection status. Terminal Remote terminal. Display Remote desktop. Processes Device processes. Services System services. Files File browser.

The tabs only work if the Pandora RC agent has the corresponding modules enabled. The integration does not enable them on its own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The entry point is Setup → Setup → Pandora RC. Only administrators or profiles with FM permission can enter; the integration is not available in SaaS installations.

The form has two blocks that are saved separately:

  1. Enable Pandora RC: select Yes and click the grey Update button in that row. That button saves only the enablement.
  2. Pandora RC API: fill in user, password, hostname, port and timeout, then save with the green Update button at the bottom right.

If you save credentials before enabling the integration, the credentials form is not shown at all. Enable it first, then configure it.

The API fields are:

Field Default What it expects User Empty Pandora RC user. Password Empty User password. API Hostname portal.ehorus.com Portal host, without protocol or port. API Port 443 Portal HTTPS port. Request timeout 30 Maximum wait in seconds; 0 disables the limit.

The values are stored in the configuration with the ehorus_enabled, ehorus_hostname, ehorus_port, ehorus_req_timeout, ehorus_user and ehorus_pass tokens. The password is stored in the configuration; it is not shown in clear text outside the form.

Enabling the integration for the first time creates the global PandoraRCID field for Pandora FMS object types and migrates old eHorus Id values. On installations upgraded from older versions it is normal to still see the eHorus Id label; the value is preserved and ends up in the new field.

docs.title: Testing the connection
docs.text:
The Test button (labelled Start) tests the values currently in the form, without saving them. It sends a request to the portal and shows a success or failure icon with one of these messages:

Message What it means Empty user or password The user or password is missing. User not found The portal does not recognise the user. Invalid password The password is wrong. Connection timeout The portal does not answer within the timeout.

A successful test saves nothing: click the green Update afterwards. If the test fails, check hostname, port, credentials and network access before touching the rest of the integration.

docs.title: Preparing the inventory object
docs.text:
Before connecting, the Pandora ITSM Apache server must allow the console to be embedded in a same-origin iframe:

Header always set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"

Without that header, the browser may block the iframe and the remote session stays blank.

The inventory object must have a value in the PandoraRCID field — or in the legacy eHorus Id —. That value is the Pandora RC agent identifier.

  1. Go to Inventory → Create new object, enter a name and click Create.
  2. Open the Click here to continue working with Object #XXX link to open the newly created object.
  3. In Object type, choose Computer or Pandora agents, depending on the device type.
  4. In Custom fields, fill in PandoraRCID with the agent identifier. On older installations the field appears as eHorus Id.
  5. Click Update changes to save it.

The field is global for Pandora FMS object types. If it does not appear, check that the integration is enabled and that the object type is one of those that receive the field; on an older installation it may still be displayed with the eHorus Id name.

docs.title: Remote connection
docs.text:
With the object ready, open its inventory page. If the integration is enabled and the field has a value, the Pandora RC tab appears with the product icon.

On entering, the console shows Remote management of this device with Pandora RC and the Launch button. When you click it, Pandora ITSM requests a token from the portal, loads the iframe and shows the session tabs. If the agent has a password, the session itself asks for it when connecting; keep it at hand.

The session token expires. When that happens, the iframe is removed and the message The connection was lost and the authorization token was expired. Reload the page to request a new authorization token. appears. Reload the page to request a new one.

docs.title: Requirements and common problems
docs.text:
• The Pandora ITSM server must be able to reach https://<hostname>:<port> on the portal. The usual port is 443.
  • The portal certificate must be valid: TLS verification is not disabled.
  • The integration requires administrator or FM permission and is not available in SaaS.
  • The agent must have the terminal, desktop, processes, services or files modules enabled for the tabs you want to use.
Symptom Likely cause What to do Pandora RC is not enabled The integration is disabled. Enable it in Setup → Setup → Pandora RC. Missing eHorus Id The object has no agent identifier. Fill in PandoraRCID or eHorus Id and save. There was an error retrieving an authorization token Wrong credentials, host, port or TLS. Use Test and check network access. There was an error retrieving the agent token The identifier does not exist or the user cannot access the agent. Check the field value and Pandora RC permissions. There was an error retrieving the agent data The agent does not answer or the portal does not return it. Check that the agent is connected. The iframe stays blank X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN is missing or the browser blocks it. Add the header in Apache and reload. The connection was lost and the authorization token was expired The session token expired. Reload the object page. Connection timeout The portal does not answer within the configured time. Increase the timeout or check connectivity.

The integration does not store the remote session in Pandora ITSM: the token is ephemeral and the real conversation happens between the browser and the Pandora RC agent. If access fails, the problem is usually the network, the certificate or the agent, not the inventory object.

docs.title: AI and chatbot
docs.text:
The Pandora ITSM chatbot is not a window that says "hello" and then waits. It is a support system with two parts: a chat server with its web client and, optionally, an artificial intelligence engine that learns from the knowledge base and from conversations to suggest answers.

Without AI, the chat still works: users open a conversation and an operator answers. With AI, the system can answer on its own, assist the operator or do both depending on the mode. The difference between "having chat" and "having a chatbot" is that second part, and in training it.

The architecture has three elements: the chat client, which the user interacts with; the chat server, which the operator works with; and the prediction engine, which generates the answers. The client and server ship with Pandora ITSM; the prediction engine is installed separately.

docs.title: Chat server
docs.text:
Global configuration is in Setup → Setup → ChatBot, under Chat Global Options.

The main fields are:

  • Enable chat: turns the service on.
  • Ws url, Ws port and Ws password: address, port and password of the chat web service.
  • Ws channel by default: channel used by default.
  • Check chat server: checks the connection; a green dot means it responds.
  • General chat: Disabled, Only IA or Manual.
  • Ticket chat: Disabled or Enabled for chat inside tickets.
  • Enable SSL: enables HTTPS and shows the certificate and key paths.

Ws url must be the public URL of the Pandora ITSM installation —the same one shown in Public access to server in general setup—, not an internal address the user's browser cannot reach. If the chat does not connect, check that URL before touching Node.js.

If AI is enabled, the the buttons to update the knowledge base model and the conversational model buttons appear below; they retrain the models with the current information.

docs.title: HTTPS and Node.js
docs.text:
Serving the chat outside the console should use HTTPS. Enable Enable SSL, replace the sample certificates with your own, save with Update and check that Check chat server stays green.

The chat server is a Node.js application under extras/chat_server. A typical installation on a yum system is:

curl -fsSL https://rpm.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash -
yum install -y nodejs
npm i -g pm2
cd /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/extras/chat_server
npm update
pm2 start server.js

Use a Node.js version compatible with the current dependencies —the server uses Express 5, so it needs a modern version— not the Node 12 from old manuals. If npm complains about the version, the chat will not start even if the configuration is correct.

To start it with the system, create /etc/systemd/system/pandoraitsm-chat.service:

[Unit]
Description=Pandora ITSM Chat Server
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.js
Restart=always
User=root
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/html/pandoraitsm/extras/chat_server

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

And enable it:

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now pandoraitsm-chat.service

The database connection is configured in extras/chat_server/config/config.js. The default values work for a standard installation; change them if the database is on another server or uses other credentials.

docs.title: AI engine and per-channel configuration
docs.text:
The prediction engine is installed as root and listens on port 6000/tcp:

yum install -y python3 python36-Cython
wget http://<server>/prediction_engine-latest.tgz
tar xvzf prediction_engine-latest.tgz
cd prediction_engine
./install.sh
systemctl restart prediction_engine.service

AI is configured per channel, not globally: Support → Chat → Channel Manage, click the channel name and Enable Chat IA.

There are two AI modes:

  • Pandora ITSM AI: uses the local prediction engine. Set IA url —the web service URL, for example http://192.168.1.10—, IA port —6000 by default— and Mode IA:
  • Manual: the AI does not answer; the operator runs the conversation.
  • Semi-auto: the AI suggests answers and the operator chooses.
  • Full-auto: the AI answers on its own.
  • ChatGPT (OpenAI): uses the OpenAI API. Set API Key, Model (gpt-4 or gpt-3.5-turbo), Max tokens, Context time, Temperature, Avatar, Title, Subtitle and Context.

Full-auto also shows the response times and the certainty threshold:

  • Initial response time: seconds before the first answer.
  • Response time between conversations: wait between one question and the next.
  • Progress bar timeout: time the operator has to choose an answer before the AI answers on its own.
  • Certainty threshold: minimum confidence, between 0 and 1, to accept an answer. A low value answers everything; a high one prefers silence.

In ChatGPT, Context is the system message sent at the start. Pandora ITSM adds the instruction to answer in the user's language —or the channel's default language if the user's is not available—. Temperature ranges from 0 to 1: the lower it is, the more predictable; the higher, the more creative.

Before changing models or training, make a backup:

cp -r /opt/prediction_engine/models /opt/prediction_engine/models.bak

To restore:

cp -f /opt/prediction_engine/models.bak/* /opt/prediction_engine/models/

docs.title: Training the models
docs.text:
The normal path is the the buttons to update the knowledge base model and the conversational model buttons in Setup. Manual training is advanced and only makes sense if you need control over the corpus.

The question-and-answer model is trained with a CSV in this format:

lang;question;answer
"es";"¿Cómo abro un ticket?";"En Support → Create new ticket."
"en";"How do I open a ticket?";"In Support → Create new ticket."

You can generate it from the Pandora ITSM database:

SELECT id_language AS lang, title AS question, data AS answer
FROM tkb_data
INTO OUTFILE '/opt/prediction_engine/data/pandoraitsm_kb.csv'
FIELDS TERMINATED BY ';' ENCLOSED BY '"'
LINES TERMINATED BY '\n';

Compress the CSV, place it in /opt/prediction_engine/data/ and train:

cd /opt/prediction_engine/src
python kb_train.pyc

Conversational dialogues are defined in YAML per language:

categories:
  - Support
  - Billing
conversations:
  - - Hello
    - How can I help you?
  - - I want to open a ticket
    - Go to Support and click Create new ticket

The files go in /opt/prediction_engine/data/chat_es or chat_en, depending on the ISO language code, and are trained with:

cd /opt/prediction_engine/src
python chat_train.pyc

Besides the YAML files, Support → Chat → Conversations → Data management lets you add conversational items by category and language and search them by keyword.

docs.title: Using the chat and channels
docs.text:
Channels define where conversations happen. Support → Chat → Channel Manage lists the channels and lets you create, edit, delete and generate the code to embed them.

Each channel needs at least one operator. With Edit users you add users and set their description, avatar and languages. The operator can have a different avatar from their user record and several support languages.

Operators work from Support → Chat → Chat View. The screen shows conversations with status, user, channel, language, active time, operator and associated ticket. To receive sound notifications you must be on that screen; the chat does not notify you from another section.

If an internal user opens the chat, the conversation shows who it is. If an anonymous visitor opens it from outside, it appears as an external user.

To use the chat outside Pandora ITSM, click Generate Bundle on the channel. The star icon shows the JavaScript snippet to embed in the website or application. The snippet URL is the Public URL configured on the chat server; it must be reachable from where the users are, usually the Internet.

docs.title: Good practices and common problems
docs.text:
• Use HTTPS if the chat will be outside the console. The browser warning scares away any visitor.
  • Dedicate one channel per use —internal support, public website, presales— and do not mix operators and languages without a reason.
  • Before training, copy /opt/prediction_engine/models. A badly prepared corpus takes the previous model down with it.
  • If the chat does not connect, check in this order: Ws url, the Node.js service, Check chat server and the certificates.
  • If the AI does not answer, check the channel mode, the engine URL and port, and that the prediction_engine service is on port 6000.
  • Rotate the OpenAI API key if you share it or suspect it has leaked.

docs.title: Advanced configuration
docs.text: Advanced configuration is where Pandora ITSM stops being a freshly installed product and becomes the organisation's system. Here you decide language, URLs, email, authentication, menu visibility and the values that affect tickets, projects and CRM. Most settings have a sensible default; the trouble starts when someone changes one without knowing what depends on it.

docs.title: Where configuration lives
docs.text:
Most of it lives in Setup → Setup. Each block has its own screen and tokens. After changing values, click Update to save them to the database. An unsaved change is a good intention.

Many sections require super administrator or a specific profile bit. If a setting does not appear, it is not an interface bug: a permission is probably missing.

docs.title: General setup
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → General setup holds the global parameters:

Field What it controls Language Global language; the user's language takes precedence. Site name Name shown in titles and subjects. Enable error log Error log in pandora_itsm.log. Timezone for Pandora ITSM Time zone; Europe/Madrid by default. List of IP with access to API IPs allowed to use the API, comma-separated; * allows anyone. Default admin user Super administrator for periodic tasks. API password Password for API requests. First day of the week First day in calendars; Monday by default. Welcome view Welcome screen period; 21 days by default. Login hash password Key for a unique pre-authentication URL. Enable HTTPS access Forces HTTPS. Use SSL certificate and Path of SSL certificate Certificate and path; /etc/ssl/certs/pandoraitsm.pem by default. Access port Access port; 80 by default. Public access to server Public URL; must include the /pandoraitsm suffix. CSV encoding type and Separator data in CSV CSV encoding and separator. Chromium path Browser path for report generation. Maximum direct download size (MB) Maximum download size. Max. upload file size (MB) Maximum upload size; PHP also applies. Max. Upload file size in CRM / incidents CRM and ticket-specific limits. Temporary directory for PDF files Temporary PDF directory; /tmp/ by default. Hide version Hides the version in footer and login. Show modal last time logged Shows the user's last login. Active automatic time tracking stop Stops time tracking at Stop time tracking after (8.5 hours by default).

If you enable HTTPS, check the certificate and trust chain. PHP may need openssl.cafile in php.ini.

Public access to server is dangerous if misconfigured: the console can become unreachable. The emergency exit is to fix the token in the database:

UPDATE tconfig SET value='http://URL/pandoraitsm' WHERE token='access_public';

docs.title: Visual setup
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Visual setup controls appearance:

  • Theme: global and per-user theme; Default (Light) by default.
  • Favicon: tab icon.
  • Block size for pagination: items per page; low values avoid performance issues.
  • Global dashboard (welcome message): welcome dashboard.
  • Font for ITSM: interface and PDF font.
  • Tabs menu: tabs, drop-down menu or both.
  • Global search limit: results per area.

Global search covers open tickets, projects, people, contacts, contracts, companies, invoices, leads and Wiki. Each user sees only what their ACL allows. Custom logos and favicons live in images/custom_logos and images/favicon.

docs.title: Password policy
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Password policy setup. The policy does not apply to super administrators. Enable password policy is the master switch: if it is off, the other options do nothing.

Main fields: minimum length (5 by default), numbers, symbols, expiry in days (0 = never), forced change on first login, lock minutes (5 by default) and failed attempts. Automatic password generation also follows the policy when enabled. Authentication details are in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: Issue setup
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Issue setup groups ticket settings:

  • Ticket submission settings: Manual, Simplified or Smart.
  • Visual options: show creator/owner, ticket search limit (300 by default), quick edit, date format, work unit completion date and comment order.
  • Ticket behaviour: rating, creator/owner changes, automatic work unit on creation, type changes, mandatory type, external users, auto-assignment and customer validation before closing.
  • Work unit options (WU): automatic close (45 days by default), default time (0.25 h), email on work unit management, internal units by default and public comments.
  • Workflows: check closed tickets and days to check (15 by default).
  • Email sending options: which changes send email, notification grouping, attachments, internal units and work unit creator notices.
  • Customization: statuses, resolutions, priorities and special days.
  • Default custom columns: ticket list columns.
  • Survey Questions: survey when the rating is negative.

Functional details are in 3.1 Tickets and incidents, 3.2 Workflow and statuses and 3.3 SLA, escalation and quality.

docs.title: Changes setup
docs.text: Setup → Setup → Changes setup adjusts change notifications and behaviour. The module logic is in 5.1 Change management.

docs.title: Email and templates
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Email setup configures sending (SMTP) and receiving (POP/IMAP):

  • Notification period: minimum between SLA notices (24 hours by default).
  • System email from address: system sender.
  • SMTP Host, Port, User, Password and encryption.
  • OAuth 2.0 for Microsoft 365, with Client ID, Tenant ID and Secret.
  • SMTP queue retries, Max. pending emails and Max. emails sent per execution.
  • POP/IMAP Host, Port, User, Password, protocol and Message delimiter.
  • Accept any certificate off by default; do not enable it except in extreme cases.

Receiving is only needed if tickets are created or updated by email. Details, providers and OAuth are in 3.4 Email and support.

Email templates setup edits .tpl files and subjects. Default templates can be duplicated and made default. Macros cover tickets, changes, change tasks and work units; the full list is in the template setup and in 3.4.

Email queue control shows pending emails, attempts and status. They can be reactivated or bulk-deleted.

docs.title: Menu visibility
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Visibility management hides sections per group:

  • Hidden: not shown, even by direct URL.
  • Full: full access.

Without configuration, access is full. Each section is checked against a profile bit: projects PR, tickets IR, inventory VR, knowledge base KR, file releases KR, calendar AR, work orders WOR, people and setup any profile. Super administrators always see everything. If a user has several groups, the least restrictive visibility applies. A rule for All replaces previous ones for that section.

docs.title: Pandora FMS inventory
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Pandora FMS inventory controls inventory and remote reception:

  • Duplicate inventory name: allows repeated names.
  • CSV compatibility import: import/export format.
  • Default owner, Associated company and Associated user for remote inventory.

Inventory is documented in 4.1 Inventory.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Setup → Setup → Authentication configuration chooses local, Active Directory, LDAP or Pandora FMS. Super administrators always authenticate locally. Session timeout (secs) sets session length (9000 seconds by default). Two-factor authentication and the rest of the details are in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: CRM setup
docs.text: Setup → Setup → CRM setup has four blocks:

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text:
• Enable auto ID and Invoice ID pattern: default 21/[1000]; the variable part is in brackets and only applies to Submitted invoices.
  • Invoice header logo: logo in images/custom_logo.
  • Header, taxes, payment methods and footer.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text: Contract Statuses lets you edit, delete and add contract statuses.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
• Email batch campaigns: emails per block (500 by default).
  • Web tracking JavaScript: tracking code.
  • Captcha: Cloudflare, with site key.

docs.title: Deals
docs.text:
• Default pipeline deal.
  • Time since last update (days): stale opportunities.
  • Schedule reminder repeat hours: 24 by default.
  • Days to expire schedule: 7 by default.
  • Notification email (Deal Registrations).

CRM details are in 8.1–8.7.

docs.title: Old data maintenance
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Old data maintenance decides how long data is kept. 0 means keep forever. Defaults:

Data Days Events 30 Closed tickets 0 Work units 0 Work orders 0 Audit 15 Sessions 7 Workflow events 900 Ticket attachments 0 File tracking 30 Backups 30 Invalid emails 30 Reports 365 Archived chatbot rooms 365

Reset all data deletes all data and attachments. It is not cleaning: it is starting from scratch.

docs.title: Project management
docs.text:
Setup → Setup → Project management sets defaults:

  • Users without work unit autocomplete.
  • Working hours per day (8).
  • Work unit autocomplete in days (0).
  • Default time for simple (4 h) and multiple (4 h) work units.
  • Currency (€).
  • Vacation days (22).
  • Disable adding tickets and work units to pending or verified tasks.
  • User who receives vacation request notifications.
  • Weekly work unit notice (40 h).

Details are in 6.1 Projects and tasks and 7.1 Time management.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• Pandora RC: enables remote management.
  • ChatBot: server and channels.
  • GitLab: access token to read project tickets.

Integration chapters are in Part 11.

docs.title: Administration tools
docs.text:
• File manager: upload and organise files in attachment, attachment/downloads, images and images/custom_logos.
  • Diagnostic info: version, PHP, database, system, performance, logs, attachments and server date.
  • News board: global news by group and with expiry; supports _lastlogin_.
  • DB Manager: SQL console for super administrators or DM profile; misuse is irreversible.
  • Links: external or internal menu links; internal ones use paths such as wiki/operation/wiki/wiki.
  • System events: cron, scheduled reports and failures.
  • Audit log: user actions, text and date search, CSV export.
  • Error log: pandora_itsm.log, with a clear option.
  • Translate strings: custom translations over the original English.
  • Console extensions: registry, installation and activation of console extensions; see 12.3 Console extensions.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Change one block at a time and click Update.
  • Test changes in a staging environment before production.
  • Document who changed each option and why.
  • Review HTTPS, email and authentication after any infrastructure change.
  • Back up before touching old data or the database manager.
  • Do not use Reset all data as a cleaning tool.

docs.title: Maintenance and backups
docs.text: Maintaining Pandora ITSM is not only updating the version: it is preserving data, being able to roll back and knowing what is happening when something fails. This part covers backups, Warp Update, licensing and the maintenance tasks that prevent surprises.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: Setup → Backup has three parts:

docs.title: Backup list
docs.text:
Lists existing backups in the backup folder of the Pandora ITSM directory. From there you can download, restore or delete them.

Restoring replaces the current database with the backup. Everything created between the copy and the current moment disappears. It is not a read-only operation.

docs.title: Backup programming
docs.text:
Schedules automatic backups. You set:

  • Schedule name.
  • Mode: database only, attachments only or both.
  • Frequency; weekly by default.
  • Email for error notices.

Schedules can be edited or deleted.

docs.title: Backup manager
docs.text: Creates a manual backup at the current moment, with a name and mode. It can also upload a previously downloaded backup; it must have the structure generated by the tool and not already exist in the database. It then appears in the list and can be restored.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
Warp update groups:

  • Update offline: update from a package.
  • Update online: update from the network.
  • Options: updater configuration.
  • Warp journal: operation history.

The installation and update procedure is detailed in 1.2 Update. Before updating, back up and review the version requirements.

docs.title: License
docs.text:
Warp update → License shows the administrator user limit, the quota used and the installed license. Update license validates the entered license.

Request new license opens the request form. Enter the Auth key from support and validate online. If the console has no internet, use the request link and generate the license from a browser with access; then paste it and update.

License details are in 1.4 Licensing.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
Maintenance tasks are spread across several screens:

  • Old data maintenance: decides how long events, tickets, work units, audit, sessions, reports and backups are kept.
  • Audit log: reviews user actions and exports to CSV.
  • Error log: reads pandora_itsm.log.
  • Diagnostic info: version, PHP, database, performance, attachments and date.
  • DB Manager: SQL queries for experts; misuse is irreversible.
  • System events: cron, scheduled reports and failures.

A reasonable routine is to review logs and diagnostics, check that cron works, verify attachment space and review backups before touching old data.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Back up before updating, restoring or changing old data.
  • Test restoration, not only backup creation.
  • Keep a copy outside the Pandora ITSM server.
  • Review the Warp update result and journal.
  • Check the license after changing versions.
  • Clean old data with criteria, not on impulse.
  • Document backup frequency and who reviews it.

docs.title: Console extensions
docs.text:
Console extensions add pages, tabs and menu entries without modifying the Pandora ITSM core. They are managed in Setup → Console extensions: from there you can download the example template, upload an extension, enable or disable it, replace the package and delete it.

Only extensions registered as managed and enabled run. Code copied by hand into extensions/ or enterprise/extensions/ is no longer loaded: to migrate an old extension, upload it through the manager. Extensions are stored in extensions/ and registered in textension. The same operations are available through API v2 at /extension.

docs.title: Extension format
docs.text:
An extension is uploaded as a single .php file or as a .zip. The ZIP must have an index.php at its root; the rest of the files are optional.

Package requirements:

  • index.php at the ZIP root.
  • .php files and static assets: .js, .css, .json, images (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, ico, svg), fonts (woff, woff2, ttf), .txt and .map.
  • Safe relative paths, with no .., and a maximum depth of 16 levels.
  • Up to 256 entries, 10 MB ZIP, 32 MB expanded and 8 MB per file.
  • No data/ directory: it is reserved for the extension runtime data.
  • The PHP code must declare a top-level hook pair:
  • extensions_add_side_menu_option with extensions_add_main_function, for an Operation page.
  • extensions_add_godmode_side_menu_option with extensions_add_godmode_function, for a Godmode page.
  • extensions_add_tab_option with extensions_add_tab_function, for a ticket tab.

The hook callback must be a local named function or an inline closure. The extension can include a README.txt with instructions and an index.php as its entry point. The template downloaded from the manager includes a working example and explains the structure in its own README.txt.

docs.title: Installing, enabling and replacing
docs.text:
An extension is installed from Setup → Console extensions with Upload extension: pick the .php or .zip file, give it a name and decide whether it stays enabled. The upload creates the file or directory in extensions/ and registers the extension as managed.

Updating an extension no longer means deleting it and installing it again. If you upload a package with the same filename as an installed extension, the console warns that it is already installed and asks for confirmation in the Update extension dialog (Update to continue, Cancel to leave it). Confirming replaces the package without touching the data. The same update can be done from the extension edit form, replacing the file with one that has the same name. The filename is the extension identity, not a decorative label: it is compared case-insensitively, and only counts when the previous extension is managed.

In extensions packaged as ZIP, persistent data lives in the extension's own data/ directory. That directory is the only one that survives replacement: the new package replaces the previous one entirely, deletes the files that are not in the ZIP and moves data/ as it is into the new package. If the update fails, the previous extension and its data stay as they were.

data/ is a reserved directory. A ZIP that includes it at the root is rejected: that directory only exists for the extension runtime data, and the package cannot ship it. This way an update never overwrites real data. It is not served over a URL either, even when it contains JSON or TXT: the files the interface loads go in another package directory. Deleting the extension also deletes its data, as before.

For data to survive, the extension code must write it to __DIR__.'/data' and create the directory the first time with mkdir($dir, 0700). Any other file it writes outside data/ is lost on the next update. If it needs initial values, it can ship them in another ZIP directory, for example defaults/, and copy them to data/ only when they do not exist. If the data are application records, it is better to store them in the database through the application services. A single .php extension has no directory of its own: if it needs persistence, package it as a ZIP.

In API v2, POST /extension accepts the replace=true field to update an installed extension with the same behaviour. Without that field the response is still a 400 error, so current integrations do not change.

docs.title: Security and scope
docs.text:
Extension code runs with the server's permissions: it is not a sandbox. Install only your own or reviewed extensions, and remember that a package can include Operation pages, Godmode pages, ticket tabs, assets and menu hooks. A disabled extension is not loaded, but its files remain on the server until it is deleted.

An extension does not automatically inherit the ACL of the menu section where it is shown. It is important that the extension itself checks the profile access bits that should allow users to view and operate it; otherwise, any user who reaches the page could run it. Its place in the menu organises, it does not protect: the ACL is controlled inside the extension, in addition to the section where it lives.

docs.title: Installation, updates and licences
docs.text: Short answers to the problems that come up most often before Pandora ITSM is up and running. Each answer links to the chapter with the full procedure.

docs.title: What does the server need to install Pandora ITSM?
docs.text: Two things that are easily forgotten: 2 GB of RAM and 10 GB of free disk. The installer supports EL9, EL10, Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04, with PHP 8.2 or 8.4 and MySQL 8.0 or 8.4. If the server falls short, the script stops; it does not negotiate. Details are in 1.1 Installation.

docs.title: The installer stops before it starts. What should I check?
docs.text: In order: that the distribution is one of the supported ones, that there is enough memory and disk, that the server can reach the official Pandora FMS repository and that no previous installation exists —packages, directory or database with the same name—. The symptom table in 1.1 Installation maps each failure to its check.

docs.title: The console does not respond after the script. Is it broken?
docs.text: Almost never. Check Apache, PHP-FPM and SELinux, and read the logs before reinstalling. If the console opens but data does not load, the problem is usually the database or config.inc.php. A "it does not work" without a log is a conversation that starts badly; attach the log to the incident.

docs.title: No update is available
docs.text: Check three things: that the pandora_uid registration is correct, that the server has Internet access and that Limit to LTS updates is not enabled if you expect an FR release. The procedure and the error table are in 1.2 Updating.

docs.title: Memory error while applying an update
docs.text: Raise memory_limit to 800M or more and run the process again. If the failure happens with a patch, restore the backup before insisting. PHP limits are explained in 1.2 Updating.

docs.title: The .itsm file for the offline update will not upload
docs.text: Check that the extension is .itsm, that the size does not exceed post_max_size or upload_max_filesize, and that the form can write to the temporary directory. The recommended values are in 1.2 Updating.

docs.title: How do I know the update was actually applied?
docs.text: Look at About ITSM, the Warp update journal and the MR status. If the version does not change, it may be an unapplied update or a cache; sign in again before calling it done. The post-update check is in 1.2 Updating.

docs.title: How many administrators can I create?
docs.text: As many as Manager Count in the licence allows. Before creating a new one, check the counter; disabling the account of someone who leaves frees a slot. Do not make an administrator out of someone who only needs to read. Limits and licence blocking are in 1.4 Licensing.

docs.title: What happens if the licence expires?
docs.text: The console enters limited mode. Renew before the Expires date, especially if you have a bulk user creation planned. The licence is not pasted into tickets or shared by email; keep it somewhere safe. Details in 1.4 Licensing.

docs.title: Can I use the admin account for everything?
docs.text: No. admin is a rescue account, not a working user. Sharing it removes traceability and turns any incident into an argument about who did what. Create named users with the minimum profile and reserve admin for what really needs it.

docs.title: Users, access and organisation
docs.text: Access, permission and structure problems. If the short answer is not enough, the linked chapter has the full procedure.

docs.title: The super administrator cannot sign in with AD/LDAP
docs.text: It is local by design. The super administrator authenticates with the local password even if the rest of the directory uses AD or LDAP. Keep that password as a rescue route and do not replace it with a remote account. Details in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: A remote user cannot sign in and the password is correct
docs.text: Check whether local fallback is disabled and whether the remote bind works. The Test button in the authentication settings says more than twenty login attempts. The symptom table is in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: LDAP or AD does not connect
docs.text: It is usually DNS, port, TLS or Base DN. Run Test and check the server log; if the certificate is not valid, do not disable verification blindly. The procedure is in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: An automatically created user has no profile or group
docs.text: Automatic creation worked only halfway. Check the level, profile, group and company assigned by the remote method. A user without a profile can open their own record but cannot work. Details in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: The 2FA code is rejected
docs.text: Synchronise the server clock. TOTP codes depend on time; a one-minute offset is enough to make everything fail. If the problem affects the super administrator and the reset link does not arrive, check SMTP. Details in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: The console does not load after enabling HTTPS
docs.text: Check the certificate, the public URL (access_public) and the Apache configuration. A certificate valid for the browser but not for the internal URL is still a problem. Go back to 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: The user is locked out after several attempts
docs.text: Wait the configured minutes or review the user before unlocking. If it happens often, the lock is not the problem: the password, the authentication method or the client clock is. Details in 2.2 Authentication and security.

docs.title: Contact or user? I am not sure which one to create
docs.text: If the person must open tickets or enter the console, create a user. If they are only a commercial contact for email, campaigns or deals, create a contact. A contact has no credentials and does not consume a licence. The full comparison is in 2.3 Companies and contacts.

docs.title: Why can I not see a company that exists?
docs.text: Because the CRM is governed by companies, not groups. With CR you see your branch; with CM you see every company, not only those in your hierarchy. Also check the company assigned on the user record. The ACL map is in 2.3 Companies and contacts.

docs.title: Which profile should a new user get?
docs.text: The minimum that lets them work; widening later is easy, taking privileges back once they are spread around is not. Check Manager Count before creating an administrator and document which profile each group has. See 2.1 Users, groups and profiles.

docs.title: Tickets, workflows and email
docs.text: Errors that appear when tickets do not flow or email does not come in. The full tables are in the linked chapters.

docs.title: A workflow rule never runs
docs.text: Check that the rule is enabled and that the conditions are not so restrictive that no ticket can meet them. Start with one condition and add the rest later. Details in 3.2 Workflow and statuses.

docs.title: The rule runs on closed tickets when it should not
docs.text: The token that allows checks on closed tickets is enabled. Disable it or add a status condition. The list of common errors is in 3.2 Workflow and statuses.

docs.title: The rule changes the status but nothing else happens
docs.text: The action you expect probably lives in another rule with different conditions. The order and scope of rules matter; review both. See 3.2 Workflow and statuses.

docs.title: The email arrives with no data or empty macros
docs.text: A misspelled macro or an empty field produces an apparently correct and completely useless email. Check the macro name and the field value before blaming the mail server. Details in 3.2 Workflow and statuses.

docs.title: The flow gets stuck and the ticket does not move
docs.text: A rigid status mapping without an escape valve leaves the ticket in limbo. Add a rescue transition or review the mapping. See 3.2 Workflow and statuses.

docs.title: Emails do not create tickets
docs.text: The destination address does not match any mail queue. Check the POP3/IMAP account and the group's Email origin. If the email arrives but is ignored, the sender does not match the configured origin. Full table in 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: The ticket is created without an owner
docs.text: The group has no default user. Assign one; otherwise the ticket is born orphaned and someone has to distribute it by hand. Details in 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: The user writing by email does not exist
docs.text: Automatic creation is disabled or the user is on the blacklist. Decide whether you want users created from email and with which profile; do not leave it to chance. See 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: Changes by email are not applied
docs.text: The [INCIDENT] syntax is wrong or the user has no permission on the ticket. Email does not guess: if the instruction is not well formed, it is ignored. Details in 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: Replies are cut off
docs.text: The Message delimiter is misconfigured. Adjust the separator to the mail client that replies; do not change the server one blindly. See 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 stops working overnight
docs.text: The OAuth secret has expired or been revoked. Reauthorise the application and check the expiry date. The procedure is in 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: Large attachments fail
docs.text: The limit is in the email and in the attachment manager. Raise it carefully: a huge limit also lets someone fill the disk. See 3.4 Email and support.

docs.title: Inventory and changes
docs.text: Questions that appear when inventory does not add up or a change gets stuck.

docs.title: How many object types and fields should I create?
docs.text: As few as possible. Every extra field is paid for on every registration, filter and import. Use global fields for what all types share and own fields for what is specific. See 4.1 Inventory.

docs.title: The CSV import fails or imports strange fields
docs.text: The current format requires nine columns and the | separator: name, owner, status, receipt date, removal date, description, companies, associated users and parent. Owner and status are mandatory. Custom fields come after, in template order. See 4.1 Inventory.

docs.title: Stock does not add up
docs.text: Check Min. stock and Max. relations before blaming the inventory. An object with a relationship limit appears on the second level of stock control; one without a limit counts as a single unit. See 4.1 Inventory.

docs.title: I cannot see an inventory object that exists
docs.text: The object ACL rules: public, owner, associated user or associated company. If you are none of those, you do not see it, even with VR. See 4.1 Inventory.

docs.title: Pandora FMS objects do not reach the inventory
docs.text: Check that the node is connected, that Default owner is set and that the inventory cron runs. The object type also needs a Sync interval other than Never. See 11.4 Pandora FMS integration.

docs.title: A change stays in New and does not move
docs.text: Without authorisation there is no planning. Authorise the change from the Authorization tab; if the type is Standard, it should be born authorised. Also check that the team is correctly assigned. See 5.1 Change management.

docs.title: I cannot close a change
docs.text: All tasks must be Verified, not just Completed. Completed means it finished; Verified means someone reviewed it. Final validation is irreversible. See 5.1 Change management.

docs.title: Does the CHM permission see every change?
docs.text: Yes. CHM is not limited to the team's branch: it sees all open and closed changes. Hand that bit out sparingly. See 5.1 Change management.

docs.title: I deleted a team and its changes disappeared
docs.text: That is expected: deleting a team cascades the changes planned with it and their tasks, with no way back. The interface asks you to type DELETE, but there is no recycle bin. See 5.1 Change management.

docs.title: Projects, time, CRM and marketing
docs.text: Recommendations that come up again and again when organising work, hours and customer relationships.

docs.title: A project does not appear or cannot be worked on
docs.text: Define a clear owner and a project group from the start. Without an owner, the project has no governance; without a group, visibility becomes unpredictable. See 6.1 Projects and tasks.

docs.title: Hours do not match the budget
docs.text: Assign roles and costs before booking hours, and keep estimates and actual hours up to date. Project reports are for comparing, not for justifying after the fact. See 6.1 Projects and tasks and 10.1 Reports and dashboards.

docs.title: Should I archive or delete a finished project?
docs.text: Archive it. Deletion takes the history and the hours with it; archiving keeps traceability and removes it from the active list. See 6.1 Projects and tasks.

docs.title: I cannot approve holidays
docs.text: You need the VCM permission or administrator rights. The inbox is in People → Work unit → Vacation Management. See 7.1 Time management.

docs.title: A holiday request is rejected on its own
docs.text: There are already approved holidays in that range for the same user. The system does not allow overlapping periods; check the calendar before submitting it again. See 7.1 Time management.

docs.title: A contact does not appear in the CRM
docs.text: If it has no company, it falls outside the CRM ACL. Always assign a company; without one the contact exists but cannot be seen from the hierarchy. See 8.1 Contacts.

docs.title: A company has no governance
docs.text: A real manager is missing. A company without an owner has no one responsible for its data and visibility. Assign a manager and review the hierarchy. See 8.2 Companies.

docs.title: I cannot delete a contract
docs.text: It has invoices or tickets associated. Archive or close it instead of deleting it; deletion breaks traceability. See 8.3 Contracts.

docs.title: I duplicated a quote by mistake
docs.text: Do not duplicate quotes: version them or create a new one linked to the same deal. Check taxes, discounts and expiry date before approving. See 8.4 Quotes.

docs.title: A deal does not move because there is no pipeline
docs.text: Define pipelines and stages before creating deals. A deal without a stage is a note, not an opportunity. Assign an owner and link contacts and contracts from the start. See 8.5 Deals.

docs.title: An invoice cannot be issued or is duplicated
docs.text: Do not reuse the Bill ID and check the numbering before issuing. Once reviewed, lock it; an issued invoice should not keep being edited. See 8.6 Invoices.

docs.title: A CRM workflow does not run
docs.text: Test it with a test contact or deal before enabling it. Use concrete conditions, actions with a visible effect and do not chain workflows that trigger each other. See 8.7 Workflows.

docs.title: A campaign goes to spam or does not go out
docs.text: Check the sender, SPF and DKIM, exclusion lists and unsubscribes. If you use dynamic lists, the cron must be running. Do not buy external lists: the domain reputation is yours. See 9.2 Campaigns and 9.3 Email and email lists.

docs.title: Reports, API and integrations
docs.text: Report, token, node and chatbot problems. The short answers point to the chapter with the procedure.

docs.title: A report comes out empty
docs.text: Check RR/RM permissions and group visibility before touching the report. If you use the scheduler, check that the cron is still running. A report with no data is almost always a permission or date problem. See 10.1 Reports and dashboards.

docs.title: The API returns 401 or 403
docs.text: The token is invalid, has expired or the user lacks permissions. For the Pandora FMS integration, the user needs IM and VW. Also check that the IP is allowed in Setup → General setup → List of IP with access to API. See 11.1 API v2.

docs.title: Swagger accepts any token in Authorize
docs.text: That is normal: the form does not check the token. The check happens when a call is executed. Always read the response; a closed padlock is not proof. See 11.1 API v2.

docs.title: API v2 token or API v1 key?
docs.text: They are different things and are not interchangeable. The v2 token is created in People → Edit my user → Create Token API v2; the v1 API key is another credential. See 11.1 API v2.

docs.title: The Pandora FMS node does not appear in ITSM
docs.text: Check the URL and token in Pandora FMS. FMS registers the node when communication works; it is not added by hand in ITSM. If it appears but does not progress, look at the cron and the connection status. See 11.4 Pandora FMS integration.

docs.title: Pandora FMS does not create tickets in ITSM
docs.text: Check that the token user still has IM and that the IP is still allowed. A profile change breaks the integration without warning. If the ticket is created but does not appear, check the queue and the group. See 11.4 Pandora FMS integration.

docs.title: I cannot open the remote connection with Pandora RC
docs.text: There was an error retrieving an authorization token usually means credentials, host, port or TLS. The certificate must be valid; verification is not disabled. If the iframe is blank, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN is missing. See 11.5 Pandora RC integration.

docs.title: The chat does not connect
docs.text: Check in this order: Ws url, the Node.js service, Check chat server and the certificates. If the chat is outside the console, use HTTPS and check that the public URL is reachable. See 11.6 AI and chatbot.

docs.title: The AI does not answer
docs.text: Check the channel mode (Manual, Semi-auto, Full-auto), the engine URL and port, and that the prediction_engine service listens on port 6000. If you use ChatGPT, check the API key and the model. See 11.6 AI and chatbot.

docs.title: What should I do if the OpenAI API key leaks?
docs.text: Rotate it in OpenAI, save it again in the channel and review recent usage. Do not share it between channels or paste it into tickets. See 11.6 AI and chatbot.

docs.title: Users, groups and profiles
docs.text:
Pandora ITSM is organised around a simple idea that then gets complicated just enough: each user has a profile in a group. The group decides what information they see; the profile decides what they can do with it. A misconfigured permission does not throw an error: it grants access. And that is worse.

The point of this chapter is the usual one: least privilege is not an audit fashion, it is how you stop a user from breaking what they do not understand. With well-separated groups and tight profiles, the rest of the product works better.

docs.title: The model: group, profile and user
docs.text:
The permission structure rests on three concepts:

  • User ID: unique name to log in to the web console.
  • Group: set of users with visibility among themselves. It can be a department, a customer or a company.
  • Profile: set of access bits that defines what the user can do.

A user can have several profile + group combinations. For example, project manager in one group and ticket operator in another. Permissions are not global: they apply to the group where they are granted.

On top of this there are Teams: groups of users from different groups who work together on Support, Changes or CRM without duplicating accounts or changing their profiles.

docs.title: User management
docs.text:
The manager is in People → User management.

  • To edit, click the User ID.
  • To delete, select the row and click Delete selected, or use Delete user in the Actions column.
  • To create, click Create user +.

Each user has two switches that should not be confused:

  • Activation: whether the account is enabled.
  • Login enabled: whether they can log in interactively to the console.

Some users only exist to manage tickets by email: they do not need interactive login.

On the user form you can choose the Dashboard (welcome screen) they see on login and assign a Company. The company matters: in several sections access depends not only on the group but also on the user's company.

docs.title: Users editing their own data
docs.text: Any user can change their data from People → Edit my user or from the shortcut in the header. There they can see their API 1.0 key in a QR code or generate a token for API 2.0. A user with no profile can also access this menu option.

docs.title: Impersonate users
docs.text:
An administrator can enter the console as another user to check what that user sees and can do before granting or removing permissions. The action is on the user form, in the General info header: Impersonate user. It only appears to administrators and for valid users.

After confirmation, the session becomes the impersonated user's session and a permanent amber banner shows the effective user, the real administrator and the Stop impersonating button. Every browser tab shares the impersonation because the session cookie is shared. The administrator's session is not lost: Stop impersonating restores it and returns to the original page.

You cannot impersonate another administrator, a disabled user, an account without login, yourself or a chained impersonation. If the target user stops meeting the requirements during the session (for example, if they become an administrator), the console automatically restores the administrator.

Actions performed during impersonation are recorded in the audit log with the real administrator and the impersonated user, and the effective user's traces carry the suffix [Impersonated by <administrator>]. Start, stop, automatic restore and unauthorised attempts are recorded in the audit log. If the administrator clicks Logout while impersonating, impersonation stops first; a second Logout closes the administrator's own session.

docs.title: User types
docs.text:
Type What it can do Grouped user Accesses, views and modifies the information of the groups assigned to them, according to their profile. Grouped only by company Like a grouped user, but only sees tickets from users in the same company and group. Standalone user In Tickets they only see tickets they created or that are assigned to them. Used to support external customers. Super administrator Full access and privileges over every section and group. Always has login enabled.

A super administrator can be deactivated as an account, but their login remains active. It is a deliberate exception, not an oversight.

docs.title: User administrators and licence
docs.text:
Only users with the UM permission or super administrators can create and delete users.

Pandora ITSM keeps a special count of administrators because the licence limits how many there can be. If the number is exceeded, the console blocks login for the extra administrators; the oldest keep access and the newest are left out. They appear in the list with login disabled.

To free seats: disable or delete administrators, change their profile to a standard one or expand the licence. Details are in 1.4.

docs.title: Profiles and permissions
docs.text:
Profiles are managed in People → Profile management. Each profile has a name, a two- or three-letter abbreviation and a set of access bits.

At the end of the user form you assign the group and profile combination:

Each section uses the bits in its own way: tickets combine group and profile; downloads use categories; CRM uses companies and their parent/child hierarchy. There is no single meaning for "having permission": you have to look at the section.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Bit What it allows PR · View project See the projects the user is assigned to. PM · Edit project Create and modify project groups. Counts as an administrator for licensing.

The project manager can operate on their projects and tasks, and delete them. The owner has the same permissions as the manager. The administrator can do it on any project. Subtasks inherit the parent task permissions.

docs.title: Tickets
docs.text: Bit What it allows IR · View tickets See tickets where the user is creator, editor or author of a work unit. IW · Edit tickets Create tickets and edit existing ones. Editing is limited to the ticket owner. IM · Delete tickets Delete tickets, manage incident types and manage SLAs. Counts as an administrator. IC · Close tickets Close tickets without being the owner.

docs.title: Escalation and quality
docs.text: Bit What it allows SI · Escalate tickets Assign tickets to a group the user cannot access. QA · Quality control See quality reports and closed-ticket reviews.

docs.title: Knowledge base
docs.text: Bit What it allows KR · View See knowledge base articles. KW · Edit Create and edit articles. KM · Manage Delete articles. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Downloads and directories
docs.text: Bit What it allows FRR · View folders See uploaded directories and files. FRW · Edit folders Upload files, update existing ones and create directories. FRM · Manage folders Delete files. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: Bit What it allows VR · View inventory See own objects, public ones, those of the user's company or those specifically assigned. VW · Edit inventory Create and edit objects the user can access. VM · Manage inventory Delete objects and manage object types. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: Bit What it allows RR · View reports See reports and their data. RM · Manage reports Create, modify and delete reports, templates and schedules.

docs.title: Wiki
docs.text:
Bit What it allows WR · View See the Wiki. WW · Edit Create and edit pages. WM · Manage Modify, delete and assign users to the Wiki. Counts as an administrator.

Per-page read and write permissions are configured in the Wiki itself.

docs.title: CRM
docs.text:
CRM does not work by groups but by companies and their parent/child hierarchy. If a user has access to a company, they inherit access to its child companies, except the standalone user, who only sees their own.

Bit What it allows CR · View CRM See companies, contacts and deals the user can access. CW · Edit CRM Create and edit accessible companies, contacts and deals. CM · Manage CRM Modify or delete companies and their structure. Counts as an administrator. CA · CRM Admin Advanced CRM administration: forms, marketing and module settings. CIR · View invoices See invoices from accessible companies. CIW · Edit invoices Create and modify invoices. CIM · Manage invoices Delete invoices. DRR · Deal Registrations View and manage deal registrations. AR · Read calendar See the user's calendar and others according to visibility. AW · Edit calendar Add and edit calendar items. AM · Manage calendar Delete items, including visible third-party ones. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Pandora ITSM administration
docs.text: Bit What it allows UM · Manage users Create, edit and manage user profiles. Counts as an administrator. DM · Database management Access the database console and run SQL. Counts as an administrator. FM · Framework management Access configuration and administrative options. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Human Resources and ChatBot
docs.text: Bit What it allows HR · Human Resources Edit or delete work units for special tasks: holidays, sick leave, etc. CUW · View ChatBot users See the list of users included in the ChatBot. COW · View ChatBot operators See the list of operators. COM · Manage ChatBot Manage ChatBot users and operators.

docs.title: Change management
docs.text: Bit What it allows CHR · Read changes See changes from the teams the user belongs to. CHW · Edit changes Create change requests and see the Changes configuration. Can add themselves to or leave the team; only a superadmin or a change manager can add them back. CHM · Manage changes See all open and closed changes and edit according to their role. Counts as an administrator.

docs.title: Importing users
docs.text:
People → Import users from CSV allows mass user creation. Only administrators have access.

Group, profile, global profile and avatar are chosen in the console form; the CSV values for those fields are discarded. If the password policy is enabled, it can be applied to imported users.

CSV columns, in order:

  1. id_user
  2. password
  3. real_name
  4. email
  5. telephone
  6. description
  7. avatar
  8. disabled
  9. id_company
  10. num_employee
  11. enable_login
  12. Custom fields, in the order they exist in the system. If you do not want to give a value, leave a blank space.

docs.title: Custom user fields
docs.text:
People → User fields allows you to create your own fields: text, textarea, selector, linked field or checkbox. Only an administrator can define them.

  • Show in list: the field appears as a column in the user list.
  • Show in search: the field appears in the user filter. Search is case-sensitive.

docs.title: Group management
docs.text:
People → Groups Management is only visible to users with user-management permissions. They can manage their group or groups and always see the All group, which cannot be edited or deleted.

Tickets always belong to a group. A default user can be set for new tickets in the group; afterwards the user can escalate tickets within their group if they have permission.

Group fields:

Field What it does Forced email Enables or disables sending tickets to the group emails. Parent Parent group. Default user User assigned by default to new tickets. Icon Group image. Send customer satisfaction email Sends a satisfaction survey on close. Open ticket limit Maximum simultaneous open tickets for the group in the last year; for external users, per user. Enforced open tickets limit Prevents ticket creation at the limit; otherwise it only warns. Total ticket limit Maximum tickets for the group in the last year, open or closed. It is restrictive. Ticket SLA SLA applied to the group's tickets. Default inventory object Inventory object associated by default with new tickets. Email from Address shown as the notification origin. Group email Addresses that receive notices about ticket changes in the group.

Removing a user from a group also removes the profile associated with that group. If the user only had that profile, they are left without enough rights.

docs.title: Per-group email queues
docs.text:
People → Group management → Email → Email origin configures the email queues that create tickets. It requires a mail account configured in the console.

Pandora ITSM can only download from one POP3 or IMAP account, so aliases are used on the mail server to separate destinations. Depending on the destination address, the ticket goes to one group or another, and the sender can be created automatically.

docs.title: Teams
docs.text:
People → Teams lets you create work teams that group users from different groups for Support, Changes or CRM, without duplicating accounts or changing their profiles.

Creating a Team requires two fields:

  1. Name: team name; spaces are allowed. Do not use only spaces: it cannot be edited and will have to be deleted.
  2. Manage: user who will administer the team.

Optionally, add a mailbox, preferably the manager's, and a description.

By default the three options are checked: Support, Change and CRM. Each creates its own team in the corresponding feature. At least one is recommended.

Deleting a Team from this screen also deletes the associated teams in the features. It is irreversible.

With Add users + you filter enabled users by group or company and add them to the Team. The All option adds all filtered users, or all enabled users if there is no filter.

A user disabled in user management cannot work on the Team's tasks even if they remain in the list. For Support they need one of the IR, IW, IM, IC, SI bits; for Changes, CHR, CHW, CHM; for CRM, the CR, CW, CM, CA or DRR bits and the right level in companies, invoices and calendar.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Create one group per department, customer or company; do not mix everything in All.
  • Grant the minimum profile that lets the user work; expanding later is easy.
