Bit What it allows CHR Read the changes of the teams you belong to. CHW Create changes and view the Changes → Management configuration; add users to your own team or leave it. CHM See all changes, open and closed, and edit them according to your role within the change.

The real scope combines the bit with the role:

  • Super administrator: sees and manages all changes as if it were their manager.
  • Change or team manager: manages the changes where they are manager, validates tasks, authorises and closes.
  • Team member: sees the changes of their team and the ones they opened; can add work units, notes and attachments, and change task statuses.
  • Read-only: sees the changes of their team and their own; on their own they can edit, on the rest they can only add work and notes.

For profile and group details, go back to chapter 2.1.

docs.title: Good practices
docs.text:
• Create the teams before the changes and check the Team field on every creation: the first in the list is not always the right one.
  • Use templates for what is repeatable and keep the Standard type for what is genuinely pre-authorised.
  • Break large changes into child tasks; tracking and time are much easier to understand.
  • Require tasks to be Verified before closing: Completed does not mean someone reviewed it.
  • Review the ACL before handing out CHM: the management bit sees all changes, not only those of its team.

docs.title: Projects and tasks
docs.text:
A project is not a list of tasks with colours: it is a contract of time, cost and responsibility. Pandora ITSM lets you plan that contract, book hours against it and check whether reality matches what was promised. Everything else —the Gantt chart, the board, the reports— are ways of looking at the same problem from different angles.

The idea behind this chapter is simple: a project is managed with people, tasks and hours, not with good intentions. If hours are not booked against a task, the cost is fiction; if tasks have no owner, the Gantt chart is decoration.

docs.title: What a project is
docs.text:
Project management combines projects, tasks, roles and people. Tasks can have subtasks and be organised hierarchically. A task can also have associated tickets and work units where each person's time is recorded.

The entry point is Projects → Project list. From there you create projects, check their status, filter by group or type and open the overview.

A project has a Project manager —the creator by default—, a project group, a team of people with different roles, and a set of tasks. The project does not do the work: it organises it. The people and the work units do the work.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
In Projects → Project list → Create project you define the basic data:

Field What it means Name Project name. Project manager Responsible user. The creator by default. Project group Logical group the project belongs to. CC Email address that receives project notifications. Start and End Start and end dates. Status template Task status template. Tag template Task tag template. Company and Contract Associated company and contract, if applicable. Description Descriptive text. Project Types Project type and its custom fields. Replicate tasks from other project into this Copies tasks from another project.

Replicating tasks is convenient for projects that repeat, but it copies the original dates: every task must be readjusted afterwards. It is not a clone with a mind of its own.

A project can be linked to a company or a contract only if none of its tasks is already linked to a company or contract, and vice versa. The restriction prevents the same work from being charged to two different customers.

docs.title: Overview and editing
docs.text:
Clicking a project name opens Project overview. The Details section can be edited directly; Quick edit changes the main fields, such as the project group, the status template and the tag template.

The main tabs are:

  • Task planning: task planning and task list.
  • Board view: board by status.
  • Gantt chart: time diagram.
  • Milestones: project milestones.
  • Full edit: the same interface used to create the project.

At the bottom you find Notes, Tracker, Attachments, Members and Budget. These are not decorative tabs: each one answers a different question about the project.

docs.title: Statistics, distribution and activity
docs.text:
Statistics summarises people involved, total work hours, planned hours, billable hours and project duration. Workload distribution and Task distribution show the percentage split of work and tasks. Activity shows what happened and when.

The Budget tab calculates profitability and compares estimated cost, total cost, amount charged and average cost per hour. It also breaks cost down by role. If hours are not booked properly, this report is a work of fiction with a table layout.

Tracker records project operations: opening, closing, changes and additions of information. It is the history that answers "who changed this, and when?".

docs.title: People and roles
docs.text:
In Members you add or remove project users with Add role people. A user can have a global role in the project and a different role in each task. Permissions depend on the role: from full modification to simply reporting work.

Roles are managed in People → Roles management. Pandora ITSM includes these default roles:

  • Project manager.
  • Systems engineer.
  • Junior consultant.
  • Junior programmer.
  • Senior programmer.
  • Analyst.
  • Senior consultant.
  • Support engineer.

The Project manager role can only be edited, not deleted. Each role has an hourly cost used to calculate task and project costs. Additional costs —expense invoices or other charges— are booked directly against the task.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Planning is done in Project overview → Task planning. The list shows tasks with their status, dates, progress, hours worked, deviation, priority and tags. You can sort by any column.

The Hours worked column opens a summary of the task's work units: cost, hours, breakdown and filters by date, milestone or person. Filtered information can be exported to CSV.

The Op. column groups the actions:

  • Members: people taking part in the task.
  • Issues: associated tickets.
  • Work units: add work units.
  • Edit: edit the task.
  • Delete: permanently delete the task.

For a ticket's work units to be booked against the task and project, you must assign a role and enable Add to project's cost when creating them.

docs.title: Creating and editing a task
docs.text:
With Create at the bottom of the list you create a task with its basic data: name, priority, parent task, start and end dates, owner and estimated hours. You can also enable email notifications at start and end, the overtime notice and recurrence.

Recurrence —weekly, monthly or annual— keeps an hour counter per period. The counter resets at the end of each interval, but booked hours remain in the task total. The recurrence interval cannot exceed total hours.

After creating it, edit it to assign people in Add users to task, set costs, tags, priority, task type and custom fields.

The edit form also includes:

  • Estimated cost and Fixed cost.
  • Related company and Related contract/s.
  • Progression based on hours: calculates progress from work units. If disabled, moving the progress bar does not change the task status.
  • Task links: time relationships with other tasks.

docs.title: Task links
docs.text:
Links define the chronological order:

Link What it enforces Start to start Linked tasks cannot start before this task starts. Finish to start Linked tasks cannot start before this task ends. Finish to finish Linked tasks cannot end before this task ends, although they may end later.

docs.title: Tracking and moving
docs.text: Pandora ITSM records the opening, closing, changes and additions of information for each task, including work units and attached files. If a task moves to another project or parent task, its work units stay linked to it.

docs.title: Work units
docs.text:
Project work units can be created from the task planner —the recommended option— or from People → Work unit → Add work unit.

There are two paths that should not be confused:

  • A ticket's work units book the ticket time when it is assigned to a task, has a role and Add to project's cost is enabled.
  • Manual work units book exactly the time entered.

The manual form can split a work unit into blocks of hours —four by default— forward or backward in time, keeping the content and changing the date. It is useful for booking a week of work without creating ten records by hand.

There are two special cases: Work from home and work units without a project or task. They are computed as special tasks inside a special project. Holidays and sick leave have their own section in People → Work unit → Vacations and sick leave.

docs.title: Task custom fields
docs.text:
In Projects → Tasks types you create task types. Each type can have custom fields: numeric, text, date, true/false, list or linked. When editing a task you choose the type and its fields appear.

The behaviour is similar to ticket custom fields: they classify, filter and report. A task type with twenty fields nobody fills in does not improve planning.

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text:
A milestone is a zero-duration task that represents an important date: end of a phase, report delivery, customer review. It is managed in Project overview → Milestones and can be used to filter reports and searches.

Milestones support custom fields with Milestone fields:

  • Name: mandatory; names can repeat.
  • Field visibility: shows the field in the milestone list.
  • Type: text, text area, combo or checkbox.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
In Project overview → Attachments you can upload, download and delete project files. Each file can have a description and can be searched by keyword, location —project, tickets or work units— and date.

Source code files such as .php or .pl are not allowed; compress them before uploading. Only an administrator or the file creator with project administration permissions can delete it.

docs.title: Gantt chart
docs.text:
In Project overview → Gantt chart you see tasks and their chronological relationships. It can be opened full screen, and you can add tasks and subtasks and link them by dragging from the end of one task to the start of the next.

Unlinked tasks can be moved in time. Linked tasks follow the logical restriction: one does not start before the previous one ends. Show real planning compares the plan with the work actually done and can be viewed by month, week or day.

docs.title: Archiving and deletion
docs.text:
When a project ends it can be archived from Projects → Project list → Options → Archive. The project moves to the archive view and keeps all its information.

An archived project can be unarchived or deleted. Deleting it removes its tasks and leaves work units orphaned: they still exist, but without a project or task. Archived projects do not send automatic notifications for task, project or milestone closure.

To see active and archived projects, open Filters, set Active to Any and apply. The list returns to the default filters when refreshed.

docs.title: Board view
docs.text:
Board view organises tickets and tasks in columns by status. The horizontal bar at the bottom scrolls through all columns. The filter section lets you filter by users, completion percentage, tags and other values.

Each column can be collapsed or expanded. Each task has quick actions to edit, create a work unit, move it, copy it or delete it. Tasks are collapsed by default and can be expanded.

With Ctrl you can select several tasks and move them as a block to another column. It is the fastest way to reorganise a project without opening each task.

docs.title: Task status templates
docs.text:
In Projects → Task status templates you define task statuses. The default template includes four statuses —Pending, In process, Completed and Verified— with their colour and visibility.

The default template and its four statuses cannot be deleted. Creating a new template copies those four statuses, which also cannot be deleted. If a template in use is deleted, the project returns to the default template. Changing a project's template clears the current status, so you must assign one from the new template.

docs.title: Task tag templates
docs.text:
In Projects → Task tag templates you define task tags. The default template includes Low, Medium and High.

You can create templates per project and add your own tags. Changing a project's template deletes tags already assigned to tasks. It is one of those operations best tested on a toy project before doing it on the important one.

docs.title: Exporting to CSV
docs.text:
The board view exports selected tasks to CSV. The file includes, among others, these columns:

ID, Project, Parent Task, Task name, Description, Completion,
Work units hours, Status, Priority, Start, End, Estimated hours,
Cost, Periodicity, Start period, Interval hours, CC, Send email,
Set hours, Involved people, Tags

Over HTTPS the download starts automatically; over HTTP you may need to authorise it in the browser. The export contains the selected tasks, not a complete copy of the project with its statuses and tickets.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The Notes tab stores internal messages as a logbook. They can be searched by keyword and linked to a task; by default they are not linked to any task.

Notes are excluded from system reports, so they are not the place to record hours or costs. In the current interface they can be edited and deleted; do not treat them as an immutable record.

docs.title: Workflow rules
docs.text:
In Projects → Workflow rules you define automatic rules for projects and tasks. They are independent of ticket workflow rules and ship with four sample rules disabled.

Each rule has an execution mode:

  • Cron: evaluated periodically.
  • Real time: evaluated when the user performs an action.

Conditions are created in the Conditions tab and can combine project and task fields. The default relationship is OR; AND, AND NOT, OR NOT and XOR are also available. Conditions can be ordered with Up and Down.

Actions are created in the Actions tab: send an email to one or more users, change the project manager, and so on.

Email templates can use these macros:

Macro Value _next_milestone_ Date and time of the next milestone. _project_completion_ Project completion percentage. _project_cost_deviation_ Project cost deviation. _project_costs_ Project cost. _project_end_date_ Project end date. _project_estimated_costs_ Estimated project cost. _project_estimated_hours_ Estimated project hours. _project_manager_ Project manager. _project_name_ Project name. _project_pending_hours_ Pending project hours. _project_start_date_ Project start date. _project_used_hours_ Hours worked on the project. _project_users_ Users involved in the project. _task_completion_ Task completion percentage. _task_end_date_ Task end date. _task_estimated_hours_ Estimated task hours. _task_name_ Task name. _task_pending_hours_ Pending task hours. _task_recurrence_ Task recurrence. _task_start_date_ Task start date. _task_used_hours_ Hours worked on the task. _task_users_ Users involved in the task. _workflow_content_ Summary of hours, recurrence and other data.

docs.title: Project groups and types
docs.text:
Project groups are managed in Projects → Project groups. They group projects that share characteristics. The name can repeat and the icon is optional. Then assign each project to its group and filter by it in the list.

Projects types are managed in Projects → Projects types. A project type can have custom fields: text, numeric, date, true/false, lists, hierarchically linked lists and URL with description. Those fields can be filtered in the project list.

Each project type custom field has three common options:

  • Show in the projects list: displays it as a column in the list.
  • Global field: adds it to all existing and future types.
  • Required: forces a value to be set.

Be careful with global fields: once created they can only be deleted, not edited. If they are also marked Show in the projects list, as many columns appear as project types exist. A project without a type uses the first one in the list when edited, so check the type before saving.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Define a clear owner and project group from the start.
  • Assign roles and costs before booking hours.
  • Use types and custom fields only if they will be filtered or reported.
  • Keep estimates and actual hours up to date.
  • Use milestones for the dates that really matter.
  • Archive finished projects instead of deleting them.
  • Review status and tag templates before changing them.
  • Read the project reports after booking hours, not before any exist.

docs.title: Time management
docs.text:
Clocking in is not an administrative punishment. It is the raw material of the reports: if the time record is fiction, the report is fiction too. Pandora ITSM records the working day, breaks, location and vacations, and then turns that data into calendars, reports and automatic rules.

This chapter covers both halves of time management: daily time tracking and absence management. The agenda and calendar close the loop, because an hour booked without context is just a number.

docs.title: Time tracking
docs.text: The entry point is People → Time tracking. Superadministrator profiles see everything; everyone else depends on their permissions and the configured menu visibility. In current versions there is no separate module to unlock: if the profile has access to People and the menu is visible, the entry appears.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
People → Time tracking → Activity shows the summary for the day and the controls for the working day. There are three actions:

  • Start time: starts the timer. Before it starts, it asks for the location: Office, Work from home or Clients.
  • Pause time: stops the timer without closing the working day.
  • Stop time: closes the working day and leaves the record available for reports.

After starting, the start button is disabled and pause and stop are enabled. To resume after a pause, press the start button again and choose the location. The screen shows worked time, paused time, current status and location, plus a table with the day's intervals: status, location, time range and worked time.

Automatic stop is enabled by default. It is configured under Setup → Setup, with the Active automatic time tracking stop checkbox and the Stop time tracking after field, which accepts hours between 0 and 23 in steps of 0.05. The initial value is 8.5 hours. If it is disabled, the timer runs until someone stops it; if it is enabled, the system closes the interval when the limit is exceeded. The check runs in the console: if the browser is closed, the interval may remain open until the next connection.

docs.title: Team
docs.text:
People → Time tracking → Team is the supervision view. It shows each team member's avatar, name, email, phone, location and status.

The filters are:

Filter What it does Search by keyword Searches by name, email address or phone. Location Filters by Office, Work from home or Clients. Status Filters by Stopped, Active, Paused, Vacations or Sick leave. Company Administrators only; limits the list to one company.

Status is read by colour:

Colour Status Green Active, with the timer running. Blue Paused. Red Stopped, with no working day open. Orange On vacation. Purple On sick leave.

Vacation and sick leave take precedence over time tracking: if the user has a vacation or sick leave work unit on that day, the list shows that colour even if the timer is stopped.

docs.title: Weekly and monthly time tracker
docs.text:
People → Time tracking → Week and People → Time tracking → Month show activity day by day. By default they show the user running the query; profiles with HR permission can choose another person with the user search.

The header summarises worked time and paused time for the period. Each day shows the start and end time, the break, the location and a timeline with the intervals. The previous and next week or month buttons move through periods; the next button is disabled while the period has not ended yet.

With HR permission, Edit entry appears on each day. It opens the activity editor, which lets you add an interval, change the time or location of an existing one and delete it. A manual edit is marked with the warning icon (Alter activity) so the report does not confuse a corrected entry with an original clock-in. A standard user sees their week and month, but cannot edit from these views.

For the full history there is Reports → People management → Time tracking, available to HR. It filters by user, period (This Week, This Month, Last Month, Last 3 Months or Custom), start and end dates and report type (Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Monthly Detailed). It offers CSV report and Full screen.

docs.title: Workflow rules
docs.text:
People → Time tracking → Workflow automates notices and stops based on what the team records. Only profiles with HR permission or administrators can enter. An HR user is limited to their group in the conditions; the company is chosen separately. An administrator can choose any group.

Clicking Create a workflow creates a rule with a description. In the list you can disable, enable or delete it. Opening the rule name gives access to its conditions and actions.

Conditions filter users by company or group and check four values:

Condition What it measures Time worked (or more) Accumulated worked time. Paused time (or more) Accumulated paused time. Exceeded time of day Time exceeded during the day. Effective weekly time (hours:minutes) Weekly hour limit, calculated from the configured first day of the week.

The global condition decides how checks are combined: Match all fields, Match any field or No match. Each condition can be related to the others with AND, OR, AND NOT, OR NOT or XOR, and reordered with Up and Down.

Actions always send email:

  • Send email to affected user: notifies the user affected by the rule.
  • Send email to: sends to a list of comma-separated addresses.
  • Automatic stop and send email to affected user: also stops the time record.

The system cron runs the rules. In the standard installation it is include/integria_cron.php, every five minutes. If the cron does not run, the rules are not evaluated, no matter how active they are.

docs.title: Agenda and calendar
docs.text:
The calendar in the side menu is the quick view; Full calendar opens the full agenda. The Calendar entry requires agenda access permission (AR), and adding an entry requires write permission (AW).

The full agenda can show or hide entries, work units, projects, tasks, customers and inventory, and navigate by month, week or day. Creating an entry asks for a title, public visibility, duration (One hour, Two hours, Four hours or One day), alarm, date, time and description. The same form updates or deletes it.

The vacation calendar is another view: it lives under Reports → People management → General vacation calendar and is explained below, because it only paints approved absences, not the work agenda.

CRM Tasks, sales activity and the call and video meeting integrations are documented in 8.8 Tasks.

docs.title: Vacation management
docs.text: Vacations are not an email to the boss. They are special work units that go through approval and, once accepted, appear in the calendar and in reports. The flow has three parts: request, approval and reporting.

docs.title: Vacation request
docs.text:
People → Work Unit → Vacations and sick leave opens the request form.

The fields are:

Field What it does Username Affected user. Defaults to the requester. HR, UM, VCM and administrators can choose another person. Task Absence type: Vacations, Not working for disease, Not justified or Visit to the doctor. Extra vacation Marks the request as extra vacation. The approval queue keeps it and shows it in the Extra vacation column. Start date First day of the period. Days used Working days covered. Description Reason or comment. Add row date Adds another period to the same request.

Only Vacations goes through the approval flow and creates a pending record. The other three options create work units directly, without approval.

When you click Add, the system checks that there are no approved vacations in the same range. If there are, the request is rejected with a warning. If everything is correct, it stays pending and an email is sent to the person configured for vacation notices.

docs.title: Vacation approval
docs.text:
People → Work Unit → Vacation Management is the approval queue. It requires the VCM (Manage Vacations) permission or administrator status.

The Vacation Request tab shows user, dates, days, whether it is extra vacation and the status. The status changes between Pending, Accept and Reject and is saved with Submit.

On acceptance, the console creates one work unit for each working day in the period, skipping holidays. If approved vacations already exist in that range, the operation fails and warns. On rejection, only the status changes. In both cases an email is sent to the user.

The Vacation Request List tab is the history: same table, with the final status of each request.

Vacation reports are documented in 10.1 Reports and dashboards.

Time management ends where real work begins: with data someone can read, compare and correct. If time tracking is taken seriously, reports help you decide; if not, they only decorate a meeting.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text: A contact is a person in the CRM: someone you call, email or visit. It is not a Pandora ITSM user and has no access to the application. That difference was explained in 2.3 Companies and contacts; here we cover the record, its fields and the tools attached to it.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
Contacts are managed in CRM → Contacts → List. Each contact belongs to a company, and any user with access to that company can see its contacts, contracts and invoices.

The basic record asks for three things:

  • Full name.
  • Email.
  • Company.

You can also fill in Phone, Mobile, Position, Manager Company, Disabled, Description and Tags. Manager Company is the Pandora ITSM user who manages the contact's company; it does not turn the contact into a user.

docs.title: Custom fields
docs.text: In CRM → Contacts → Contact fields you create custom fields with the usual types: text, long text, date, numeric, true/false and lists. They hold information that does not fit the basic record: language, preferences, schedule, customer number or any data you later want to filter.

docs.title: Contact tags
docs.text:
Tags are managed in CRM → Contacts → Tags. Each one has Title, Tag Description (Optional), Tag Color, Hex Color Code, Tag Color Text and Hex Color Code Text. Background and text colours make them easy to tell apart.

A contact can carry several tags. They are assigned in the contact record, in the Tags field, and can be used as a list filter. They are useful for campaigns, sectors, commercial status or any cross-cutting criterion. They do not grant permissions.

Workflows can add tags and use tags in their conditions. If you delete a tag, it is no longer available and disappears from the items that had it.

docs.title: Contact view
docs.text:
Opening a contact shows its information and its relationship with the rest of the CRM:

  • Company and company data.
  • Associated deals.
  • Pandora ITSM user with the same email, if any.
  • Notes.
  • Emails sent to the contact.
  • Opportunities and related activity.

That view is the starting point for work: write, create a note, schedule a call or review the history.

Sales activity, calls and video meetings are documented in 8.8 Tasks.

docs.title: Email from the CRM
docs.text:
CRM sections can send email if Pandora ITSM is connected to a Google Workspace corporate account. The connection is configured in Setup → General Setup with the Client ID and Secret generated in Google Cloud.

Each user then connects their account from their profile settings. Once connected, send buttons appear in companies, contacts and deals. The cron checks the connected inboxes and records emails in Pandora ITSM when the address matches a contact.

Addresses or domains that must not be processed go to the CRM blacklist in Setup. Emails from those domains are discarded if there is no active thread.

docs.title: Contact forms
docs.text:
In CRM → Forms → Contacts you create forms to publish on a website and register contacts from outside Pandora ITSM. Each form field maps to a contact field: name, email, company, phone, and so on.

When the form is ready, Generate Bundle produces the JavaScript to embed on the website. If the email already exists, the contact is updated; no duplicate is created.

Creation, publishing and mapping are detailed in 9.4 Forms.

docs.title: Contact workflows
docs.text: Contacts can be automated with CRM → Workflows. Rules can run on creation, on change or by cron, and can send email, create notes or tasks, update fields, add tags or delete contacts. Details are in 8.7 Workflows.

docs.title: Disable and delete
docs.text: A contact can be disabled without deleting it, preserving its history. Deleting removes the record and its CRM relationships; before doing so, check whether it has deals, emails or notes.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Do not duplicate contacts: use email as the reference and update the existing one.
  • Always assign a company; without it, the contact falls outside the CRM ACL.
  • Use tags for campaigns and custom fields for stable data.
  • Review the email blacklist before connecting corporate inboxes.
  • Document who manages each company and each contact.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text: The company is the axis of the CRM: it groups contacts, contracts, invoices, deals and tickets. Without a company there is no hierarchy, no ACL and no way to know who owns what. Its role in access control is explained in 2.3 Companies and contacts; here we document the record and its configuration.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in CRM → Company → List. The company record contains:

Field What it means Company name Company name. Manager User who owns and manages the company. Parent company Company it depends on. Fiscal ID Tax identifier; used in invoices. Company Role Company role for classification and filtering. Website Website. Country Country. Payment conditions Payment terms. Services Enabled IT services. Tags Organisational tags. Address Address. Comments Notes.

A company without a Parent company is visible only to its manager and super administrators. The hierarchy organises customers, suppliers and subsidiaries; it does not hide data from users who already have group access.

docs.title: Company roles
docs.text: In CRM → Company → Roles you create, edit and delete roles. A role is a basic classification for filtering: customer, supplier, partner, distributor, and so on. It grants no permissions; profile bits and company membership do that.

docs.title: Custom fields and sections
docs.text:
In CRM → Company → Custom fields you add company-specific fields. In CRM → Company → Sections you group those fields into blocks so the record does not become an endless form.

When creating or editing a section, choose the custom fields that appear in it. A field is assigned to one section and is shown inside it; if the field is deleted, it also disappears from the section. Fields must exist first in Custom fields: the section only groups them, it does not create them.

The combination is useful when each company type needs different information: billing data, commercial terms, technical contacts or any attribute you later want to filter. A section with no fields adds nothing; before creating one, decide what information it will group and who will fill it in.

docs.title: Company tags
docs.text:
In CRM → Company → Tags you create company tags with Title, optional description, background colour and text colour. A company can carry several tags; they are assigned in its record and filtered from the list.

They classify by sector, relationship type, commercial status or campaign. They do not grant permissions and do not replace the company role.

docs.title: IT services
docs.text:
IT services classify tickets by service and limit which services each company can choose. They are managed in CRM → Company → Services.

Each service has a name, owner and description. Two important options:

  • Enabled by default: enabled automatically when creating or editing a company.
  • Apply to all existing companies: applies it to all companies already created.

Then assign services to each company. When opening a ticket, the user can only choose the services enabled for their company. Ticket workflows can use the service as a condition or filter.

docs.title: Import and export
docs.text:
Company import is in CRM → Company → Import companies from csv. The column order is fixed:

name, address, fiscal_id, country, website, comments, id_company_role,
id_parent, manager, last_update, payment_conditions, billing,
Office Phone, General email

Custom fields go at the end, in the defined order, and must already exist. The parent company and manager must already be registered.

The company list can be exported to CSV with Export to CSV. Search statistics shows statistics such as companies grouped by manager, activity or sales.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The CR, CW and CM profile bits control viewing, writing and managing the CRM. A company manager can modify it; users in the same company can see it, but only those with management permissions can modify data from their colleagues' companies. The full case study is in 2.3.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Create the main company first and use it as the parent of customers and suppliers.
  • Assign a real manager; a company without an owner has no governance.
  • Use roles to classify, not to grant permissions.
  • Define field sections before filling the record with twenty loose fields.
  • Review IT services per company before opening tickets.
  • Export before importing: a CSV is a snapshot, not a backup.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text: A support contract is the formal promise behind a ticket, a licence or a renewal. Pandora ITSM uses it to know what each company is covered for, until when, and what can be invoiced. It is not a law-firm contract manager: it is the piece that connects CRM, support and billing.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in CRM → Contracts → List. To edit a contract, click its Contract reference, the short descriptive field each company can name its own way.

The main fields are:

Field What it means Company Company the contract belongs to. Contract type Contract type. Contract reference Short reference for lists and searches. Related invoices Associated invoices. Related contracts Related contracts. Begin date and End date Validity period. Private Visible only to users in the same company. Status Contract status. Description Long description. Tags Tags. Custom fields Fields from the contract type.

A company can have several contracts. When generating an invoice from a contract, select it again with the magnifier in Contract number before continuing. Contracts can be copied to renew them with new dates and the same terms.

docs.title: Contract types
docs.text:
In CRM → Contract → Contract types you define types such as services, licences or maintenance. Each type can have its own or global custom fields.

Custom fields support text, date, lists, sublists and other types. They are grouped into categories so the contract does not show a flat list. If you change a contract's type, the values of the previous custom fields are deleted. Test it on a sample contract first.

docs.title: Contract tags
docs.text:
In CRM → Contracts → Tags you create contract tags. Each one has a title, optional description, background colour and text colour. They are assigned in the contract's Tags field and can be used as a filter.

They are useful for marking renewals, licences, maintenance or any status you do not want to turn into a custom field. They do not change the contract's validity or status.

docs.title: Documents and templates
docs.text:
When editing a contract you can click Create PDF from template and choose a template. The PDF is generated from the contract data and attached automatically in Files.

Templates are edited in CRM → Contracts → Contract templates. They are HTML with macros. Some useful ones:

Macro Value ___contract_id___ Contract identifier. ___contract_name___ Contract reference. ___contract_number___ External or invoice number. ___contract_description___ Long description. ___contract_start_date___ Start date. ___contract_end_date___ End date. ___contract_company_name___ Company name. ___contract_status_name___ Status name. ___contract_custom_field_XX___ Contract custom field. __company_address__ Company address. __company_fiscal_id__ Tax identifier. __date_begin__ and __date_end__ Contract dates.

Templates support images, pasted text and raw HTML from Source code.

docs.title: Related invoices
docs.text: In Related invoices you see the invoices of the contract's company and can link one or more. The invoice has a Related contracts field for the reverse relation. The relation does not replace the invoice: it only makes clear which contract justifies it.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use readable, unique contract references.
  • Check the type before changing custom fields.
  • Do not delete contracts with invoices or tickets; close or archive them.
  • Generate the PDF from a template and keep it attached.
  • Document what each contract covers and until when.

docs.title: Quotes
docs.text: A Quote is a formal estimate: a commercial proposal linked to a deal or contact that the customer can review and approve. It is not an invoice or a contract; it is the document that explains what an opportunity costs before it becomes business.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in CRM → Quotes → List. When creating one you choose:

Field What it means Name Quote name. Deal Opportunity it is linked to. Only your own deals not in Won or Lost appear. Contact Recipient contact. Template Presentation template. Status Draft, Published, Approved or Canceled. Expiration Date Validity deadline.

docs.title: Lines, taxes and currencies
docs.text:
The commercial content is built with line items:

  • Name, Description, Qty, U/C, Disc % and Total.
  • Add line item adds a manual line.
  • Add line item from catalog takes a product from the catalogue.
  • Add modifier adds taxes, discounts or fees.
  • Add currency adds a conversion to another currency.

The editor calculates subtotal, modifiers and final total. Currency conversions show the factor and converted total, and you can choose whether they appear in the table. There is also a Total text field for the amount in words.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
In CRM → Products you define the goods or services used in quotes. Each product has:

Field What it means Name Commercial name; appears in the PDF. Description Technical or commercial detail. Reference Internal code or SKU. Frequency One time, Monthly, Annually, etc. Term Service or contract duration. Type Service, Product or Subscription. URL Link to documentation or terms. Cost per unit Base price; multiplied by quantity. Active If disabled, it does not appear when creating quotes.

A well-maintained catalogue avoids manual errors and speeds up quote creation.

docs.title: Templates and macros
docs.text:
In CRM → Quotes → Templates you create the HTML templates applied to the quote. Macros replace company, contact and quote data. Some common ones:

Macro Value __company_name__ Company name. __company_address__ Address. __company_tax_id__ Tax identifier. __contact_fullname__ Contact full name. __contact_email__ Contact email. __quote_name__ Quote name. __quote_amount__ Amount. __quote_currency__ Currency. __quote_expiration_date__ Expiration date. __quote_status_name__ Status. __quote_owner_name__ Owner.

Templates support HTML and company, contact and quote custom fields.

docs.title: Approval and relationship with deals
docs.text:
The quote can be previewed and downloaded as PDF. The public view lets you share it with the customer without giving console access. When approved, the status changes to Approved and it remains linked to the deal.

The deal holds the opportunity, amount and close date; the quote holds the formal proposal. The contract is created later, when the deal is closed, and the invoice when it is time to bill. They are not the same object and should not be forced to be.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Keep the product catalogue with correct prices and frequency.
  • Use different templates for services, products and subscriptions.
  • Check the expiration date before sending.
  • Do not duplicate quotes: version them or create a new one linked to the same deal.
  • Check taxes, discounts and conversions before approval.
  • Archive or cancel quotes that are no longer alive.

docs.title: Deals
docs.text: A Deal is a sales opportunity. While the contact is a person and the company is the entity, the deal is the object that tracks economic value, pipeline stage and closing probability. Without deals, the CRM is an address book; with deals, it is a pipeline.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Pipeline: the visual path of the opportunity, divided into stages. Configured in CRM → Pipelines.
  • Stage: the specific phase inside the pipeline. A deal usually ends as open, won or lost.
  • Amount: estimated value of the operation.
  • Close date: expected closing date, key for sales forecasting.

Each pipeline can have its own stages. A renewals pipeline does not need the same phases as a new-projects pipeline.

docs.title: Creating and managing deals
docs.text:
In CRM → Deals → List you create and manage opportunities. The main fields are:

Field What it means Deal name Opportunity name. Description Business detail. Owner Responsible user. Company Company it belongs to. Pipeline Sales pipeline. Amount Estimated amount. Close date Expected closing date. Start date Start date. Stage Phase inside the pipeline. Tags Tags. Contacts Contacts involved. Contracts Related or expected contracts.

Available contacts and contracts depend on the selected company. Without a company, the form cannot offer those lists.

docs.title: List, board and views
docs.text:
A deal can be viewed as a list or as a Board with columns by stage. On the board you drag opportunities from one phase to another and see the pipeline at a glance.

Filters can be saved as views: by quarter, year, owner, company, stage or any combination. A saved view is a recurring question; if you will not repeat it, do not save it.

docs.title: Custom fields
docs.text: In CRM → Deals → Custom Fields you add deal-specific fields: data that does not fit the standard record and that you later want to filter or report.

docs.title: Deal tags
docs.text:
In CRM → Deals → Tags you create tags with Title, optional description, background colour and text colour. A deal can carry several; they are assigned in its record and filtered in list or board view.

Workflows can add tags when creating or modifying a deal. They do not grant permissions; they are an organisational mark.

docs.title: Deal registration
docs.text:
CRM → Deal Registration lets partners or resellers register opportunities without entering the main pipeline. It requires the Deal Registration permission.

The fields are:

  • Name.
  • Description.
  • Status: Opened, POC, Tender, Win or Lost.
  • Deal size, in the CRM currency.
  • Company: an existing one or a new one created as a child of the user's company.

Registrations stay in Deal Registration and do not automatically appear in Deals. To turn one into a real opportunity, create the deal with that information. It is a separate funnel, not a silent duplicate.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Define pipelines and stages before creating deals.
  • Use realistic amounts and close dates you can defend.
  • Assign an owner to every opportunity.
  • Link contacts and contracts from the start.
  • Review saved views every quarter.
  • Do not confuse deal registration with the main pipeline.

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text: Pandora ITSM can issue and consult invoices inside the CRM. It is not an ERP: it does not calculate cash cycles or manage defaults. It helps you know what has been billed, to whom, when, and which contract it relates to.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in CRM → Invoices. The list shows all invoices by default; Search finds by invoice identifier or company, and Contract number finds by contract.

Opening an invoice shows its data, files and related contracts.

docs.title: Main fields
docs.text:
Field What it means Bill ID Invoice number, unique. The system calculates the next one from global CRM configuration; exceptions can be defined. Reference Informative reference: order, purchase order, etc. Invoice status Pending payment, Paid or Cancelled. Internal note Internal comment not shown in the PDF. Description Text that does appear in the invoice. Language PDF language. Related contracts Linked contracts. Files Generated PDF and attachments.

Header, logo, tax, payment methods and footer are configured globally in the CRM.

docs.title: Invoice type and ACL
docs.text:
There are two types:

  • Received.
  • Submitted.

Permissions use the CIR, CIW and CIM bits:

  • CIR: view and download.
  • CIW: create and lock; edit Received invoices.
  • CIM: edit and unlock, including Submitted.
  • Super administrator: unrestricted.

Submitted invoices are locked automatically when created or edited. Only CIM can unlock them. Received invoices do not generate a PDF.

docs.title: Locking and PDF
docs.text:
A locked invoice can only be modified by its creator. Editing a Submitted invoice regenerates the PDF and replaces the previous one; the interface warns with a modal. Received invoices do not generate a PDF.

When downloading:

  • If there is only a PDF, the PDF is downloaded.
  • If there is a PDF and attachments, a ZIP is downloaded.

docs.title: Related contracts
docs.text:
In Related contracts you can add one or more contracts. The window lets you filter and select, including contracts already added. Save the invoice for the relations to be kept.

The relation is informative and for traceability: it does not change the invoice amount or status. That is what the invoice is for, not the contract.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text: Only administrators or users with the CIM profile can delete invoices. Deletion is not cancellation: if the invoice already exists, the right move is usually to set it to Cancelled and keep the trail.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Check numbering and exceptions before issuing.
  • Do not reuse the Bill ID.
  • Use Internal note for what must not appear in the PDF.
  • Lock issued invoices once reviewed.
  • Link each invoice to the contract that justifies it.
  • Download and keep a copy of the PDF outside Pandora ITSM.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: A CRM workflow is a rule that automates contacts or deals: it sends an email, creates a note, updates a field or adds a tag when a condition is met. It is not the ticket workflow from 3.2; they share a name and nothing else.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in CRM → Workflows → List. Only two types are available:

  • Contacts.
  • Deals.

Contract, invoice, quote and company types exist in the code but are disabled in the current interface. Documenting what cannot be used only creates questions.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Each rule has a mode:

  • On creation: runs when the contact or deal is created.
  • On change: runs when it is modified. For deals you can choose the watched field (Deal field to watch).
  • Scheduled: runs by cron.

Available cron intervals are Hourly, 12 Hours, Daily and Weekly. Without active cron, scheduled rules do not run.

docs.title: Rule fields
docs.text: Field What it means Title Rule name. Description What the rule does. Type Contacts or Deals. Mode On creation, On change or Scheduled. Schedule interval Interval when the mode is Scheduled. Deal field to watch Field that triggers the rule for deals. Tags Rule tags. Enabled Activates or disables the rule. Conditions Filters that must be met. Actions What runs.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Conditions are built with a query editor over contact or deal fields, including custom fields. They can be combined with logical operators and grouped so the rule does not fire on any match.

A condition that is too broad turns the workflow into an email factory. An impossible condition turns it into decoration. Test it with a sample contact or deal.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
For Contacts:

  • Send email.
  • Create note.
  • Create task.
  • Set updated at to now.
  • Update field.
  • Add tags.
  • Delete contact.

For Deals:

  • Create note.
  • Send email.
  • Add tags.

Email actions use the CRM SMTP configuration. If email does not go out, check the server first, then the rule.

docs.title: Workflow tags
docs.text:
In CRM → Workflows → Tags you create tags to classify rules. They have Tag title, Tag Description (Optional), Background color, Hex background color code, Text color and Hex text color code. They are assigned to the rule in the Tags field.

They are not contact or deal tags: these organise workflows. A workflow can add tags to a contact or deal as an action, and those tags are the item's tags.

The workflow list lets you enable, disable and force a rule to test its behaviour without waiting for cron. Forced execution is a testing tool; it does not replace a well-written condition.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• New contact: if created with the Web tag, send a welcome email and create a note.
  • Stalled deal: if the mode is Scheduled, the pipeline is Renewals and the close date is near, create a note and add the Follow-up tag.
  • Updated contact: if the Country field changes, update the corresponding tag and notify the owner.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Write the title as a sentence that explains the goal.
  • Test with a sample contact or deal before enabling.
  • Use specific conditions and actions with a visible effect.
  • Do not chain workflows that trigger each other without control.
  • Review inherited rules and disable those that no longer make sense.
  • Document who maintains each rule and why it exists.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: CRM tasks are the glue between the record, the calendar and sales activity. This chapter brings together CRM Tasks, the Activity view and the call and video meeting integrations. They used to be split between time management and contacts; now they share a place because they feed each other: a call generates activity, a meeting task can create a Google Meet, and Activity shows the result of all of it.

docs.title: CRM Tasks
docs.text:
The former Company tasks, Schedules and Meetings are unified as CRM Tasks, or simply Tasks. The entry now lives under CRM → Tasks, not inside each company, although tasks can also be created from a company, contact or deal form.

A task has a type:

Type Purpose To-do A generic task, with no call or email. Call A phone call. Email An email sent when the task runs. Meeting A meeting, optionally with Google Meet.

The usual fields are title, description, due date and time, reminder, priority, assigned user and status. The date has Today, Tomorrow and Next week shortcuts. The reminder ranges from No remind to one month before, and the assigned user receives a notice at that moment. The statuses are Pending, In progress, Completed, On hold, Cancelled and Expired; the Active filter groups pending, in progress and on hold.

When you create a task from the list, choose the company first; contact and deal selectors are not shown until there is a company. From a company, contact or deal form, those fields are already in context.

Email tasks let you prepare subject, body, CC and BCC, and can be based on an email template. The message is queued and sent when cron runs the task; if the task is deleted before that, the email is not sent. This type does not offer calendar synchronisation.

Meeting tasks can create a Google Meet link and synchronise with Google Calendar if the user has connected their account. The meeting, recording and transcript are explained in the Calls and video meetings section of this chapter.

The list shows the type with an icon in the first column, hides the ID by default and lets you filter by text, assignee, due date, status, company, contact and deal. It also supports saved filters and custom columns.

docs.title: Sales activity (Activity)
docs.text:
CRM → Activity is the sales follow-up view. It collects user activity in a single list, below Tasks, and answers questions such as "which calls has this salesperson made this week" or "which emails and deals has this customer moved in the last seven days".

The activity types are Calls, Emails, Notes, Meetings, Tasks, Quotes and Deals. Each row shows the type, date, user, company, contact and a summary. Clicking a row opens the detail in a modal: the full email, the call audio and transcript, or the note. If the activity is a deal, the deal opens in a new tab.

Filters narrow the list by type, user (from two characters), date range, company and contact. The default range is the last week. You can also save filters and choose columns, as in the rest of the CRM lists.

Activity does not create activity by itself: it shows what calls, emails, notes, meetings, tasks, quotes and deals generate. If an activity is missing, the problem is usually at the source, not in the view.

docs.title: Calls and video meetings
docs.text: The CRM can integrate with Zadarma to call from the contact form and with Google Meet to create meetings with a link and transcript.

docs.title: Zadarma
docs.text:
The integration has two levels. The administrator configures Zadarma in Setup → Setup → CRM setup with the account API key and API secret. Each user then fills in their user form, under Zadarma, with the WebRTC widget Zadarma key, their Extension / SIP and the widget Zadarma secret.

With both levels configured, the contact form shows the call button. The CRM cron collects outbound calls, downloads the recording and transcript, and creates a call activity. The transcript stays in an editable field for manual comments. The audio and transcript can be reviewed in CRM → Activity.

Zadarma credentials are administrative and per-user; do not share them between accounts or copy them into tickets.

docs.title: Google Meet
docs.text:
Google Meet uses the same Google OAuth client as email. The administrator configures Client ID and Secret in Setup → Setup → General setup, under User mail configuration. Each user connects their account from People → User management → their form → Calendar settings → Connect to Google Calendar.

When you create a CRM Task of type Meeting, you can enable Google Meet to generate the meeting link. If the account allows it, the meeting is recorded and transcribed; the CRM cron collects transcripts from finished meetings and stores them in the activity. The account needs access to Google Meet and Google Docs, because the transcript is read as a Google document.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: A marketing template is the base design for an email or campaign document. It is not the email that gets sent: it is the structure you reuse so every campaign does not start from a blank canvas.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in Marketing → Templates. Each template has:

Field What it means Name Template name. Description What it is for and when to use it. Subject Default subject. Type Template type. Contact for template test Contact used for preview testing.

Subject and content support macros written with double underscores, for example __contact_fullname__. Macros are replaced when the campaign is generated.

docs.title: Block editor
docs.text:
The editor works with blocks and is organised in three panels:

  • Add: adds structures and content.
  • Content: organises sections.
  • Design: colours, fonts and styles.

Blocks include columns, text, links, headings, images, buttons, dividers, spacers, custom HTML, alerts, coupons, testimonials, products, countdowns, social networks, hero and complete footer.

You can preview the result and send a test to the chosen contact. A template you have not tested in a real email client is a template whose appearance you do not know yet.

docs.title: Use from campaigns
docs.text: When creating a campaign in Marketing → Campaigns you choose a template. The campaign inherits its design and subject and adds the recipient list, sending server and schedule. Later template changes do not rewrite campaigns already sent.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Name templates by purpose, not by colour.
  • Keep one base template and variants for specific campaigns.
  • Always test on mobile, desktop and email client.
  • Do not embed images that depend on a local path.
  • Document which macros each template uses.
  • Archive obsolete templates instead of deleting them without control.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text: A campaign is the organised sending of a message to a contact list. Pandora ITSM lets you prepare the content, choose recipients, schedule the date and measure what happened after sending.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
They are managed in Marketing → Campaigns. When creating a campaign you define:

Field What it means Name Campaign name. ITSM Campaign ID Internal identifier. Sender Email Sender; if set, it replaces the server one. Static Contact Lists Static lists included. Dynamic Contact Lists Dynamic lists included. Static Contact Lists to Exclude Static lists excluded. Dynamic Contact Lists to Exclude Dynamic lists excluded. Subject Subject; supports __ macros. Status Draft, Scheduled, Processing, Sent or Archived. Mail server Sending server. Campaign Date Sending date. Campaign Owner Responsible user.

docs.title: Lists and exclusions
docs.text:
A campaign can combine static and dynamic lists. Static lists are a manual selection; dynamic lists are recalculated at send time. Exclusion lists subtract contacts: they prevent sending to people who unsubscribed or belong to another campaign.

Before sending, the interface calculates recipients and shows how many are unsubscribed or invalid. That number is the last chance to catch a badly built list.

docs.title: Scheduling and sending
docs.text:
Draft lets you prepare without sending. Scheduled leaves it scheduled for Campaign Date; Processing means it is running, Sent means it was sent and Archived means it was retired.

Sending uses the chosen mail server. Scheduled campaigns and dynamic lists are processed by system cron running:

php /var/www/html/pandoraitsm/include/campaign_crm.php

Without that process, the dynamic list keeps yesterday's snapshot and the scheduled campaign is never sent.

docs.title: Testing and tracking
docs.text:
Before sending you can send a test email to a specific address. It checks subject, design, links and personalisation without spending the campaign.

After sending you can review open, click and bounce rates. A low open rate may be a subject, sender or reputation problem; a low click rate is usually a content or segmentation problem.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Segment before writing; do not send the same message to the whole CRM.
  • Review exclusion lists and unsubscribes.
  • Test on several email clients.
  • Schedule in the recipient's time zone, not yours.
  • Do not buy external lists: your domain reputation is yours.
  • Measure and document each campaign so you do not repeat mistakes.

docs.title: Email and email lists
docs.text: A campaign needs two things besides design: a server that delivers the email and a list of people to receive it. Pandora ITSM separates both so infrastructure and content do not get mixed.

docs.title: Mail servers
docs.text:
In Marketing → Mail servers you configure outbound channels. It is compatible with PostMark and with your own SMTP servers.

Field What it means Name Server name. Sender Email Address shown as sender. Host SMTP server IP or domain. Port Connection port. Encryption Security and authentication method. User name Server user. Password Password or token. Email Batch Emails processed per block.

Correct SPF and DKIM configuration helps email reach the inbox instead of spam. The marketing server does not have to be the same as the support server; if you separate them, document which one each campaign uses.

docs.title: Static lists
docs.text:
In Marketing → Static contact lists you create fixed lists of manually selected contacts. The interface allows filtering, bulk selection and CSV import.

A static list is a snapshot: if a contact changes company or unsubscribes, the list does not update itself. Review it before each send.

docs.title: Dynamic lists
docs.text:
In Marketing → Dynamic contact lists you create lists based on CRM filters and rules. The list is recalculated automatically at send time: if a contact meets the criteria, it enters; if it stops meeting them, it leaves.

Dynamic lists can filter by contact and company tags. A campaign can therefore segment by tags without duplicating contacts into static lists.

docs.title: Subscription and unsubscribe
docs.text:
Contacts can unsubscribe from communications. Unsubscribes and invalid addresses are subtracted before sending and should be reviewed so you do not email someone who asked not to receive more messages.

Unsubscribing does not delete the contact: it marks them so campaigns skip them. Deleting would lose the history and the commercial relationship.

docs.title: Use from campaigns
docs.text: When creating a campaign you choose which static and dynamic lists to include and which to exclude. The campaign does not store a copy of contacts: it queries the lists at send time.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use a recognisable sender and a domain with SPF and DKIM.
  • Prefer dynamic lists for segments that change.
  • Review static lists before each send.
  • Keep cron active if you use dynamic lists.
  • Respect unsubscribes and do not buy external lists.
  • Separate support and marketing servers if volume justifies it.

docs.title: Forms
docs.text: A form is the front door for contacts from a website. It is not a campaign or a list: it is the mechanism that turns an anonymous visit into a contact with a name, email and company. Pandora ITSM manages it from the CRM, but its use is clearly marketing.

docs.title: Where they are
docs.text:
Forms are managed in CRM → Forms. The list lets you create, duplicate, delete and generate the embed code for each form.

Each form has:

Field What it means Name Form name. Language Any or a specific language. Description What it is for. Email Addresses that receive a notification, separated by commas. Assigned to Assigned user or Form team. Assigned user / Form team Internal recipient of the form. Submission type Default, Submission message or Redirect to URL. Form submission message Message shown after sending. Redirect to URL Destination URL after sending. Button label Button text. Warn on companies already registered Warns if the company already exists.

docs.title: Form builder
docs.text:
The editor has two areas: Available Fields and Form Builder. Available fields are:

  • Text Input, Textarea, Label/Text.
  • Email, Phone, URL, Number, Date.
  • Select, Checkbox, Radio Button.
  • Hidden Field.
  • Custom Styles.
  • Captcha.
  • Policy Acceptance.

Drag each field to the form and configure it. It can map to a standard contact field or a custom field, and be marked as required.

docs.title: Key fields
docs.text:
A field marked as a key field identifies existing contacts. It is usually email or phone. If the value matches an existing contact, the form updates that contact; it does not create a duplicate. If it does not match, it creates a new one.

That behaviour is the difference between a useful form and a duplicate factory.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
When the form is ready, Generate bundle produces the JavaScript to embed on the website. The form appears on the page and sends data to Pandora ITSM.

The result can be:

  • A confirmation message on the same page.
  • A redirect to a specific URL.

Both options are configured in Submission type.

docs.title: Notifications and assignment
docs.text:
The Email addresses receive a notification for each submission. The form can be assigned to a user or a team so the contact lands in the right inbox.

Warn on companies already registered helps detect duplicate companies before creating another record. It does not merge them automatically: it warns.

docs.title: Languages and translations
docs.text: The Language field limits the form to a language. The translation editor adapts labels and messages to each language. If the website is multilingual, the form should be multilingual too.

docs.title: Use in marketing
docs.text:
Contacts captured by a form enter the CRM and can be part of dynamic lists by tags, fields or company. A campaign can then segment by those criteria without exporting or duplicating contacts.

The form captures; the list organises; the campaign sends. Mixing the three usually ends in a CSV nobody can maintain.

docs.title: Privacy and security
docs.text:
• Use Captcha to stop bots.
  • Add Policy Acceptance if you need explicit consent.
  • Always publish the form over HTTPS.
  • Do not include sensitive data you do not need.
  • Review the privacy policy and data processing.
  • Do not put credentials or tokens in hidden fields.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Ask only for the data you will use.
  • Use email as the key field to avoid duplicates.
  • Test the form on the real website, not only in the editor.
  • Define a clear confirmation message.
  • Assign each form to a responsible user or team.
  • Periodically review created contacts and duplicate companies.
